containers.frame_rationale: Gi and no-gi diverge modestly here, not dramatically, and every divergence is a pace-and-friction effect rather than a legality effect. Critically, no option is ruleset-illegal in this position — there is no collar/lapel dependency and no leg-lock legality question — so all seven moves stay nonzero in both frames and no availability zero applies.

containers.frame_rationale: 50-50 is a symmetric leg entanglement, so 'bottom' is simply the seat playing for the come-up, and the ruleset — not the geometry — decides the character. In the GI the position is a two-point sweep economy plus a straight-ankle (botinha) war: the heel hook is illegal, so the entire leg-lock threat collapses onto the straight ankle lock, which becomes a co-workhorse with the position-reversal sweep (together ~50% of gi attempts), while the counter heel hook drops to near-zero and toe hold/kneebar are suppressed to brown/black legality. In NO-GI the same seat becomes a mutual inside-heel-hook hand-fight: the counter heel hook jumps to the single largest line item (~20%), the sweep share roughly halves (people fight for the inside heel rather than come up), and straight ankle/extract/SLX flatten into a mid cluster with toe hold and kneebar fully live. The gi/no-gi fork here is genuine and legality-driven, not noise — which is exactly what the sealed site values (identical gi=nogi everywhere) failed to capture.

containers.frame_rationale: Ashi Garami/Top is the player whose leg has been trapped but who holds the stronger posture (standing or on top), trying to escape, pass, or counter the leg-locker below. The gi/no-gi fork is the single largest driver of this distribution and was unanimous across the panel. In the gi there is no heel-hook tax: the trapped player can safely posture, strip the foot off the knee line, and pass, so the 'leave the position' cluster dominates — Ashi Garami Escape (~22-23) + Pass to Side Control (~20) + Back Step Pass (~15) is roughly 58% of gi attempts, while counter-entangling is comparatively rare (~10). In no-gi a hasty extraction gets you heel-hooked, so the trapped player instead counter-entangles and plays the leg pummel: Counter Ashi Entry becomes the single most frequent action (~17), the counter Toe Hold roughly doubles (~7 gi to ~12 nogi), transitioning into your own leg entanglement climbs (~8 to ~11), and casual Escape drops (~23 to ~13). Passing stays central in both frames but is more committal and slightly more frequent in the gi. Toe Hold is IBJJF-legal in the gi only at brown/black belt, so it is population-rare rather than unavailable — floored, not zeroed. No listed top move is fully unavailable in either ruleset: the heel hook that causes the entire fork belongs to the bottom role, not this one.

Available but mechanically taxed: a hasty foot extraction in no-gi exposes the heel to a hook, which is exactly why its no-gi rate (~13) sits far below its gi rate (~23). Reduced, not zeroed.

containers.frame_rationale: The positional spine of bottom backside-50-50 is ruleset-invariant: the defender's first job is to stand up in base, clear the knee line (Ashi Garami Escape), or hip out, and those escapes plus the counter-entangle dominate attempts in both gi and no-gi. The divergence is entirely in the leg-attack layer. No-gi, heel hooks are legal and central, so the symmetric shootout - Counter heel hook plus the two heel-hook finishes - claims roughly a quarter of all attempts, compressing every positional escape by a few points. In the gi, heel hooks are banned under IBJJF and mainstream rulesets, so that share evaporates: the bottom player's only real leg attack becomes the Straight Ankle Lock Entry (which nearly doubles from ~7 to ~13-15), and the freed volume flows back into the positional escapes (stand-up, hip escape, counter-entangle), each a few points higher than its no-gi counterpart. Net: mirrored on the positional core, forked on the finish layer - gi is escape-and-straight-ankle, no-gi is escape-and-heel-hook-shootout.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi and no-gi pictures diverge sharply and for a single mechanical reason: legality of the heel hook. In no-gi (ADCC/EBI/sub-only) backside 50-50 is fundamentally a heel-hook station — the Outside Heel Hook dominates attempts (~20-26) and, because the position's canonical INSIDE heel hook is absent from this move set, the outside hook absorbs that finishing mass; the back take (~14-18) and the honey-hole/saddle bridges (~10-14) fill out a genuinely head-heavy no-gi distribution. In the gi, heel hooks are IBJJF-illegal, so that ~22 points of heel-hook mass has nowhere to go and redistributes into the legal top-game: passing out of the tangle for points (50-50 Pass ~19-27), taking the back (~16-26), and the brown/black leg layer of kneebar and toe hold (~15-24 each). Saddle entry and honey-hole entries, which are heel-hook setups, deflate in the gi (~4) and inflate in no-gi (~10-14), while counter heel hook and outside heel hook fall to near-zero in the gi per the availability rulings. Net: the gi is a pass-or-back-take position with a toe-hold/kneebar threat; no-gi is a heel-hook-first entanglement.

containers.frame_rationale: This position forks harder on ruleset than almost any in the corpus, and the fork is legality-driven, not stylistic. In no-gi, cross ashi-garami exists to expose the heel: the outside heel hook is the headline finish (~18-19% mean, with an honest bimodal tail — outside-heel purists like Gordon/Danaher/Kade push 21-27, inside-heel opportunists like Lachlan/Marcelo weight the generic heel node higher), and the saddle upgrade (~17%) is the primary advancement. In the gi both heel-hook nodes are hard zeros (IBJJF heel-hook ban, all belts) AND the saddle's payoff evaporates (heel hook from saddle illegal, reaping is a DQ), so ~37 points of no-gi attack mass reroute into the two moves that stay legal and finishable in the gi — the toe hold (~23%, workhorse) and the kneebar (~20%, legal at brown/black) — plus more repositioning (Cross Ashi Transition ~16%) and bailing to a legal, scorable 50-50 (~14%). Saddle entry is the sharpest internal dissent in the gi frame: Lachlan/Roger hold it near 5-8 on reap-DQ risk, while Danaher/Gordon/Craig keep it ~13-16 arguing you can hold inside sankaku legally for a straight-ankle. Net: same legs, two different sports — no-gi is heel-hook-and-saddle, gi is toe-hold-and-kneebar.

The two gi zeros (Outside Heel Hook, generic Heel Hook) are bulletproof ruleset zeros — IBJJF bans all heel hooks in the gi across every belt, so these are genuine availability zeros, not rare events. The record Σ|Δ|=84 divergence is fully mechanism-justified: the two heel-hook nodes carry ~37% of no-gi mass and are legally deleted in the gi, forcing a coherent reroute (37 out; net +42 redistributed after Saddle -4/Backside -1) into the gi-legal finishers Toe Hold (+15) and Kneebar (+12) plus more repositioning/50-50 bail (+7/+8). Rank orders pass a coach's-eye recognition test in BOTH frames: no-gi is heels-first (19/18) then saddle-upgrade (17); gi is toe-hold-and-kneebar (25/21) with saddle downgraded and heels dead — each is exactly the frame's real decision tree. The single live objection — gi Saddle at 13 sitting at the top of the pro-saddle dissent camp (Giles/Roger favor 5-8) — resolves to accept: panel mean 12.7 rounds correctly to 13, the legal inside-sankaku straight-ankle mechanism supports low-teens even with heel hooks illegal, and a 1-point nudge would break the exact-100 sum for zero real-world gain. containers.frame_rationale: Honey Hole (the saddle / inside sankaku), bottom role, is the leg-entangled defender racing to survive inside and outside heel-hook attacks. In BOTH rulesets the single most-attempted action is the hand fight — Grip Break on the entangling feet to strip the heel grip (~22-25%), the head of the distribution — before any escape can begin. The gi/no-gi split is driven entirely by heel legality. No-gi the heel is legally exposed, so (a) Counter heel hook is a live, frequently-attempted bite-back (~11-14) that nearly vanishes in the gi (~1-3, IBJJF-illegal), and (b) the exchange is a finish-race that compresses patient extraction. In the gi, with the heel not legally attackable, the defender can hip-escape (Hip Escape to Guard ~18 vs ~13) and stand out (Standing Escape ~15 vs ~11) more patiently, and Sweeps are a hair safer (~8 vs ~6) — those points absorb the near-absent gi heel counter. Counter-entangle to 50-50 and Reverse to Outside Ashi tilt slightly no-gi (leg-lock reversal meta); Inversion Escape is a ruleset-neutral scramble (~11). Net: identical handfight-first head both frames; no-gi adds a heel counter and shrinks patient escapes, gi trades the heel counter for more standing and hip-escape extraction.

In the gi, with no heel-hook threat (IBJJF), the defender can recover guard with grips, frame and shrimp, extract the knee line at leisure, and come up to stand or sweep for points, so those clean basics carry more weight and rolling/inverting are comparatively safer.

containers.frame_rationale: This is the sharpest ruleset fork in the corpus, and it is driven entirely by heel-hook legality plus reaping. In no-gi the saddle exists FOR the inside heel hook ('Heel Hook from Saddle'), which is ~31-32% of all attempts — the position's reason to exist — with the outside heel hook, toe hold, kneebar and backside-50-50 sharing the remaining volume. In the gi, reaping rules make the saddle itself rare, and the heel is legally off the table (both heel hooks drop to a floor of 1, kept positive only for gi sub-only contexts), so the freed probability mass flows almost entirely into the two gi-legal finishes — kneebar (~24) and toe hold (~23) — plus slightly more re-alignment volume (back take, fallback to inside ashi). So gi and no-gi are forked, not mirrored: the no-gi distribution is heel-hook-dominant and head-heavy on one move, while the gi distribution is a balanced kneebar/toe-hold twin-tower.

availability_rulings.reason: The reaping position plus the IBJJF heel-hook ban make the inside heel hook near-absent in mainstream gi. Held at FLOOR 1 (not zeroed) because the gi frame spans sub-only / ADCC-style gi rulesets where inside heel hooks are legal, and the pack itself carries a positive gi success rate (11) — so it is rare, not unavailable.

Same heel-hook legality suppression as the inside variant. Held at floor 1 rather than 0 — attempted only in gi sub-only / no-reaping-enforced contexts and in training, effectively never in IBJJF gi competition. Not a genuine availability zero.

flags: DUPLICATE: 'Fallback to Inside Ashi-Garami' and 'Saddle Fallback to Inside Ashi' are the same retreat (both -> inside-ashi-garami/top); their combined ~12% no-gi / ~17% gi retreat share is double-counted. See removal_candidates.

STRUCTURAL: 'Outside Heel Hook from Saddle' is mechanically atypical from the saddle, whose signature finish is the INSIDE heel hook; kept because the panel assigns it real no-gi attempt volume (~9), but part of that likely reflects inside-heel-hook attempts being lumped in / side-switching, and it may belong to a different ashi configuration.

Every gi/no-gi divergence has a mechanism (backside-50-50 no-gi-heavy meta; calf slicer / estima / kneebar / toe hold gi-legal while heel hooks are banned; more back-take pivoting in gi when legs are suppressed). The single defect: the panel's OWN availability_rulings state both heel-hook moves are held at FLOOR 1 in gi (rare-not-unavailable, gi frame spans sub-only rulesets, pack carries positive gi success), and panel_mean gi = 1.09 for both — yet proposed_final rounds them to 0, contradicting the ruling. containers.frame_rationale: The single meaningful gi/no-gi split here is the legality of the reverse heel hook. In no-gi the reverse heel is a live threat, so the Reverse Heel Hook Counter (~12) and, to a lesser degree, Counter-entangle to 50-50 (~11-12) are rational counter-attacking games and take real share; SLX recovery also ticks up with no-gi scramble pace. In the gi, heel hooks are banned in mainstream/IBJJF competition, so the counter collapses to a 1-2 floor and its weight redistributes to the straightforward 'rip the leg out and square up' options — Ushiro Ashi-Garami Escape and Leg Extraction to Guard both climb, making the gi frame even more extraction-dominant (~44% combined) than no-gi. Gi grips add little offense from behind the leg here; if anything they slow the attacker and marginally aid extraction. Everything else (turtle bail, deep half, sweep) is held near-equal across rulesets because none of those mechanics depend on grips or submission legality.

availability_rulings.reason: Heel hooks are banned in IBJJF and most mainstream gi competition, so a reverse-heel counter-attack is effectively unavailable in the gi frame. containers.frame_rationale: The gi and no-gi frames diverge because Ushiro Ashi-Garami is inherently a knee-reaping/heel-hook position, and heel hooks (plus reaping entries) are illegal under IBJJF-style gi rules. In the gi frame the four heel-hook finishes go to zero (availability rulings) and the reaping saddle/inside-ashi entries collapse to near-zero (Saddle Entry ~3-6, Inside Heel Hook transition ~2); that freed attempt mass concentrates on legal, position-first lines — Follow to Back Control becomes the clear workhorse (Roger/Craig push it toward 24 on a position-before-submission logic), backed by the straight Ankle Lock Finish, Kneebar, Toe Hold, Return to Outside Ashi, and Ashi Garami Maintenance. In the no-gi frame the full heel-hook arsenal is live, so mass spreads across Saddle Entry (feeds the honey-hole heel hook, ~10-14), the inside/outside heel-hook finishes, and the Outside Heel Hook Adjustment, flattening the distribution; Follow to Back stays a top line but no longer dominates because finishing threats compete for attempts. Net: gi is head-heavy on back-take + legal leg locks; no-gi is broader and heel-hook-weighted.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Giles/Danaher + Statistician) tried to break the proposed Ushiro Ashi-Garami/top distribution across all five vectors and it largely held. Sum coherence PASS (gi=100, nogi=100). Head-mass is correct-shaped: gi top-5 share 77% (head-heavy on back-take + legal leg locks, as the frame predicts) and nogi top-5 share 49% (flat/broad, heel-hook arsenal fragmented across 5 labels), matching the frame_rationale. The four availability zeros (Outside Heel Hook Adjustment, Heel Hook from Ushiro Ashi, Inside/Outside Heel Hook from Ushiro Ashi-Garami) are bulletproof — inside/outside heel hooks are categorically IBJJF-illegal in the gi, so gi=0 is availability, not a low nonzero. The why_selected concern #1 (zeroing 'Inside Heel Hook from Ushiro Ashi-Garami' gi from prior 10) is a correct fix of a genuine prior error (heel hook at gi=10 is impossible). Every gi/no-gi divergence has a mechanism: Follow-to-Back dominates in gi because finishes are scarce; Ankle Lock inflates in gi (16 vs 6) because the attacker SUBSTITUTES the legal straight ankle onto the same exposed foot the illegal heel hook would target; Saddle Entry 4gi/11nogi because the saddle is a reaping entry near-illegal in gi. A coach of this position would recognize both priority lists. ONE bounded correction survives: 'Inside Heel Hook from Ushiro' is proposed gi=2, but it is an inside heel hook and MUST be zeroed under the exact same illegality logic that zeroed its four siblings — a nonzero gi occurrence for an inside heel hook is an internal-consistency leak that contradicts the position's own frame_rationale ('the four heel-hook finishes go to zero'). We zero it (gi 2->0) and route the freed 2 points to Follow-to-Back (gi 20->22), the position-first workhorse, preserving the sum and the rank order. Ashi Garami Maintenance gi=13>nogi=8 is the weakest surviving number (stall-for-legal-entry mechanism is a stretch) but stays panel-faithful (mean 12.65) and is accepted. Topology flags (Outside Heel Hook Adjustment is_submission=false landing at game-over; Maintenance landing at opposite-role bottom) are graph-coding issues out of the occurrence panel's scope — the magnitudes themselves are panel-faithful and accepted. Net: 12 of 13 moves accepted as-authored; 1 heel-hook leak zeroed with a mechanical rebalance. Far below the >half-mass re_elicit threshold; a bounded adjust.

containers.frame_rationale: In both frames the back-bottom picture is dominated by the same reality: you cannot escape until the strangle hands are neutralized, so Hand Fighting is the modal attempt (~22-24%) regardless of ruleset, and it is the only truly head-heavy entry. The gi/no-gi divergences are second-order and mechanical. Without the gi, sweat and the absence of collar/lapel grips make sliding escapes marginally easier, so the Shoulder Walk Escape and Back Door Escape tick up a point or two in no-gi and Granby/Rolling become a hair more viable on a slick opponent. In the gi, collar and lapel grips give the top player extra strangle threats and control, which both keeps the hand-fight share high (Mendes weights gi hand-fighting above no-gi for exactly this) and makes patient frame-based escapes — Turn In and Face and hip-escape-to-half-guard — the disciplined mainline (Roger and Lachlan lean these slightly higher in the gi). No move is ruleset-exclusive here: every entry is a positional escape with no collar-only submission or leg entry, so nothing is zeroed and there are no availability rulings; the gi/no-gi gap is a few points redistributed toward sliding escapes in no-gi versus grip-and-frame escapes in the gi.

containers.frame_rationale: The single largest gi/no-gi divergence is the collar. In the gi the bow-and-arrow choke is a co-headline finish rivaling the RNC (13-16% of attempts) because the cross-collar plus belt/pant grip lets the attacker bend the spine; in no-gi that mechanic disappears entirely, collapsing the bow-and-arrow to ~1 (Mikey to 0) and redistributing that mass to the RNC (which climbs from ~21 gi to ~28-29 no-gi) and to the body triangle (which rises from ~5-6 gi to ~9-10 no-gi, since without collar/belt friction the legs become the primary spine-and-hip control). Maintenance and RNC hand-fighting setup stay roughly frame-neutral. Everything else is a small, frame-stable tail dominated by control cycles rather than low-percentage submissions, because leaving the back for an armbar is a poor trade both with and without the gi.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger Gracie, Marcelo Garcia, John Danaher + The Statistician) attacked the distribution across 4 rounds and could not break it. Sum coherence is exact (100 gi / 100 nogi). The lone zero (Bow and Arrow Choke no-gi) has a bulletproof availability argument: it is a collar-dependent strangle requiring a deep cross-collar plus belt/pant grip, mechanically absent no-gi; the panel's true-0-to-1 ballot and the flagged overstatement of the calibrated anchor-4 justify the deliberate 0 override. Every gi/no-gi divergence carries a clean mechanism and the redistribution closes exactly: the vanished gi bow-and-arrow mass (13) is reallocated to RNC (+6), body triangle (+3, legs replacing the collar as spine control no-gi), and small tail bumps (+4). Rank order is coach-endorsed in BOTH frames (gi: RNC 21 / maintain 16 / bow-arrow 13 as co-headline collar finish; no-gi: RNC 27 / maintain 16 / body triangle 8 rising to #3, the canonical no-gi back system) and correctly fixes the sealed old-site errors (flat RNC 43 with no frame split, body triangle at 1, no bow-and-arrow split). Head-mass (top-5 = 61% gi / 64% no-gi) is well-calibrated for an apex control position with a deep maintain-and-recycle decision tree. The why_selected concern (over-populated/fragmented hub) is confirmed real (4 armbar, 2 triangle, 2 short-choke variants) but the panel handled it correctly by driving each fragment to floor/near-floor, so the distribution is sound; the fragmentation is a structural/dedup task for humans (already flagged), not a mass-misallocation to fix by moving numbers. Every proposed value sits within rounding of its panel mean. All raised objections (Body Triangle gi arguably +1, Maintenance/Body-Triangle overlap, armbar aggregate ~10-11%, RNC-setup double-count) were examined and self-withdrawn as either grounded-and-locked against an exact sum or out-of-scope for per-move correction. Unanimous accept.

containers.frame_rationale: No move on this list is ruleset-unavailable in either frame - every option is a body-mechanics escape from a locked body triangle, with no lapel/collar dependency and no leg-lock-legality issue, so there are zero availability zeros. The gi/no-gi differences are entirely friction-, sweat-, pace-, and grip-driven and are small (1-3 points). No-gi leans higher on the slippery/athletic exits: Back Door Escape (sweat lets you slither out the back while gi friction and grips re-trap you mid-slide) is the cleanest divergence, and Standing up in Base is marginally higher no-gi for the same friction reason. No-gi's faster cadence lets you cycle repeated Triangle Clear and elbow-fight attempts slightly more. The gi leans the other way on the one patient, grip-based escape - Frame and Shrimp to Guard - where the jacket rewards deliberate framing back to open guard. Success rates diverge more than attempt frequency (the jacket slows the clear), but attempt distribution stays close across frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely the rarest attempt from a LOCKED body triangle - the lock prevents the hip rotation needed to invert and reverse, so it's near-fantasy (Gordon) and survives only on occasional scramble inversions in modern light/no-gi grappling. containers.frame_rationale: Body Triangle / Top is the same control-and-strangle platform in both rulesets, but the gi opens a second finishing wing that the no-gi frame simply does not have. In the gi, the two collar chokes — Bow and Arrow (~11) and Cross Collar (~12) — together claim roughly a quarter of all attempts, which mechanically depresses the RNC share to the high-20s and softens the emphasis on the raw squeeze. In no-gi both collar chokes are hard zeros (no garment to grip), and those ~23 points redistribute onto the RNC (up to the mid-to-high 30s, the clear dominant action), the Short Choke (~11), the Body Triangle Squeeze (~12, elevated because the rib/diaphragm crush becomes a genuine attacking fatigue weapon rather than pure control), and a small bump to Roll to Truck and Kimura. Back Control Maintenance stays high and roughly frame-flat (~18-24) because re-securing the seatbelt and hand-fighting to keep the lock is the single most frequent action from here regardless of ruleset.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger, Marcelo, Danaher, Statistician) ran 4 rounds trying to break the distribution and every attack collapsed. Both frames sum to exactly 100. The why_selected concern (zeroed Bow and Arrow no-gi) is bulletproof: Bow and Arrow and Cross Collar are collar/lapel-dependent strangles with no no-gi analogue, given explicit availability_rulings and unanimous 0.0 panel dispersion — the SEALED site's nonzero no-gi values (11, 4) were a straight ruleset misread. Marcelo's gi objection (BowArrow should outrank CrossCollar) withdrew once the panel means (CrossCollar 12.47 tighter/higher than BowArrow 11.45) showed the two-collar cross-choke is legitimately the marginally more-attempted gi finish from body triangle; 12 vs 13 is noise. Danaher's no-gi Squeeze-magnitude objection (13 feels head-heavy) held its nose and accepted because every alternative allocation (more onto an already-38 RNC) is worse, and the panel agrees tightly (mean 13.0, dispersion 0.67) that the no-gi rib/diaphragm crush is a genuine attacking action, not the site's absurd 3. Divergences all carry mechanisms: gi-only collar chokes (garment), no-gi elevation of Squeeze/Short/Truck absorbing the redistributed ~23-point gi collar share, Truck as no-gi/EBI culture. Head-mass concentration (gi top5 81, nogi top5 89) is a forced consequence of two legitimate zeros collapsing the tail, not over-fitting. The Maintenance correction (site 13 -> panel 20) is the container's best fix and matches the position's maintenance-heavy identity. No consequential rank inversions from rounding. containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi picture is near-symmetric because every listed move is a grip/structural back-escape available under both rulesets, and the dominant behavior in both is neck-defense hand-fighting (Hand Fighting from Back + Hand Fight from Seat Belt Control + Escape Seat Belt Control carry ~40%). The divergences are second-order and mechanism-driven: no-gi runs slightly hotter on the slide/scramble family (Back Door, Standing up in Base, Granby) because sweat and the absence of gi friction make sliding out and rolling easier and more frequently attempted, while the gi runs slightly hotter on the hand-fight core and slightly colder on Turn In and Face because collar/lapel threats make neck defense more urgent and the fabric friction slows turning escapes. No move is ruleset-illegal here, so there are no per-frame zeros.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Giles/Danaher/Ryan + Statistician) failed to break the distribution over 3 rounds of hostile review. Both frames sum to exactly 100. No zeros exist, so no availability burden. Head-mass is moderate not spiked (top-5 = 64% gi / 62% no-gi), correct for a diffuse back-survival grind rather than a single-escape container. The why_selected concern (the 90/90 L1 shift vs old site values) is a justified decomposition: the old data crammed all neck-defense into one node (Hand Fighting from Back = 43) and pinned the three seatbelt-specific survival entries at 1 each; the panel legitimately redistributed that same survival behavior across the three neck-defense nodes the schema exposes (~17 + 14 + 8), which Giles endorsed on mechanism and re-merging would only recreate the old artifact. Danaher's rank challenge (Turn In and Face buried) was withdrawn once frequency-of-attempt was distinguished from importance: neck-defense happens first and repeatedly, so it out-frequences the turn-in follow-through; Turn In at 10 sits mid-pack, already bumped 2.5x from its prior of 4. All gi/no-gi divergences are <=1 point and mechanism-grounded (gi hotter on hand-fight core via collar/lapel strangle urgency; no-gi hotter on slide/scramble family via sweat/reduced friction), none reversing rank. Gordon's Back Door concern is an honestly-logged black-belt-ceiling dissent, not a population-attempt-frequency error, so 6/7 is left as-is. Every proposed integer is the nearest int to its panel_mean with tie-breaks used only to close the sum to 100; no fabricated deviations. Low dispersion throughout (all <1.4) indicates high panel agreement.

containers.frame_rationale: The single decisive gi/no-gi fork here is the collar. In the gi, Seat Belt back control feeds two twin strangle engines — the Rear Naked Choke and the Bow and Arrow (a lapel-dependent choke, ~14% of gi attempts). In no-gi the Bow and Arrow is structurally impossible (no lapel to grip), so its entire share collapses into the RNC, which is why no-gi RNC (~26-28) sits roughly 7-8 points above gi RNC (~19-20) while total strangle volume stays constant across frames. Two smaller, mechanism-backed divergences ride along: Body Triangle Lock rises no-gi (~10 vs ~8 gi) because with no cloth to grip you close the legs to hold the back; and Roll to Truck rises no-gi (~5 vs ~2 gi) because the truck feeds the leg-entanglement/heel-hook meta that lives in no-gi and is dampened by gi legality and points. Back Control Maintenance is the highest-volume non-scoring action in BOTH frames (~15-16) and anchors the distribution's head alongside the RNC; the remaining moves form an honest situational tail.

The stray nogi:1 values in Round 1 (kade, mendes, marcelo, gordon) were rounding noise on an unavailable move, ruled to 0.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Giles/Danaher/Ryan + Statistician), 3 converging rounds, could not break the distribution. Sums are exact (gi 100 / nogi 100). The why_selected concern (zeroed Bow-and-Arrow nogi, prior 7) is a CORRECT availability ruling, not a defect: the bow-and-arrow is a lapel-dependent collar strangle with no no-gi mechanism, so its ~15pt gi share legitimately collapses (primarily into RNC 21->30, +8.3 in the panel means, with defensible small leaks to Body Triangle +3 and Roll to Truck +3 via the no-gi leg-entanglement meta). Every gi/no-gi divergence greater than 1 point carries a stated mechanism: RNC +9 (collar-engine collapse), Body Triangle +3 (no cloth -> close legs to hold back), Roll to Truck +3 (truck/heel-hook meta, gi legality/points damping). The lone zero has a bulletproof structural argument. Rank order is coach-recognizable in BOTH frames (gi: RNC > Maintenance > Bow-and-Arrow > Body Triangle > back-upgrades > tail; nogi: RNC > Maintenance > Body Triangle > 6/6/5 cluster). Head mass (gi top-5 = 68, nogi top-5 = 70) is appropriate for back control's fragmented decision tree. The TARGET COLLISION flag (two verbs -> one destination node x2) is a downstream graph-dedup/renormalization concern, NOT an attempt-share error in this container. Giles' initial 'strangle volume not conserved' attack was withdrawn once the panel confirmed the residual is behaviorally-honest substitution into control/truck pathways no-gi. Ryan's only quibble (nogi RNC could be ~32) sits inside the defensible band and does not warrant a change. No move's mass is misallocated; corrections would be gratuitous.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split here is entirely mechanism-driven by the grip fight. In the gi, cloth grips let the attacker cement the rear bodylock/seatbelt, so the defender concedes more: Rolling to Guard (the pull-to-guard concession) sits slightly higher in the gi, and the hand fight to break the lock is marginally harder. In no-gi the lock slips (sweat, no fabric anchor), so the two turn-to-face exits (Grip Break and Face, Turn In and Face) and the wrestling-style exit (Standing up in Base, Arm Drag Escape) tick upward while pure guard concession drops. Every move is legal and mechanically available in both rulesets, so there are no forced zeros; divergences are small (1-4 points) and reflect grip-vs-slip and pull-guard-vs-wrestle-out, not availability.

flags: Sealed site values were badly miscalibrated and effectively inverted: Controlled Descent was 30 (panel ~13) and Grip Break and Face was 13 (panel ~26). The panel's actual workhorse was the site's near-tail; the elicitation re-centers the distribution on the hand fight and does not conform to the old numbers.

'Grip Break and Face' (lands clinch/top) and 'Turn In and Face' (lands open-guard/bottom) are near-duplicate concepts (both = break the lock, turn to face) and together own ~43% of attempts; possible consolidation candidate, distinguished only by resulting position.

'Standing up in Base' is semantically odd from an already-standing position; interpreted as base-out / anti-mat-return posture. It was the single largest Round-1 disagreement (gi range 4-14), splitting wrestlers (Craig/Danaher/Gordon/Kade high) from guard specialists (Marcelo/Lachlan low); converged to ~10-11 with residual dissent preserved.
'Hip Escape to Turtle' applies a ground-movement term (hip escape/shrimp) to a standing position; read as drop-and-shrimp-to-turtle. Marcelo's Round-1 outlier (10) softened toward the pack (~5-8).

containers.frame_rationale: Standing back control is a transit position in both rulesets — the shared imperative is to get the opponent to the mat while keeping the back, so Mat Return, Follow to Back Control, Takedown and Seatbelt consolidation dominate the attempt count identically in gi and no-gi (~65-70% combined). The frames diverge in three mechanism-driven ways. (1) The Bow and Arrow Setup is a collar line: real in the gi (~5-8) and a hard 0 in no-gi (availability ruling — no lapel). (2) The standing RNC and body-triangle tick up in no-gi because there is no collar for the defender to grip-strip the choking hands and sweat makes standing control looser, whereas gi grips let the top player hold longer and finish on the floor instead. (3) Gi grips lengthen the standing exchange, marginally boosting seatbelt/mat-return consolidation over impulsive standing finishes. All other moves exist in both frames; 'rare' is coded 1-3, never a false 0.

Head-mass: top-4 wrestling-transit core (Takedown 21, MatReturn 21, Follow 16, Seatbelt 16 = 74%) is appropriate for a STANDING back-control transit position whose entire job is 'get them down while keeping the back'. Attack on Takedown-21/MatReturn-21 as double-counting was answered by Marcelo/Danaher: they are distinct motor patterns (drag-them-back-down vs trip/lift-to-grounded-back) and separate state-machine edges, not one behavior split. The single hard zero (Bow and Arrow nogi) is a bulletproof ruleset-availability zero (same-side-lapel mechanism, no lapel in no-gi; Marcelo's token nogi-1 correctly overruled to consensus 0, mass flows to RNC nogi 11). Every gi/nogi divergence carries a named mechanism: Bow&Arrow 7/0 (lapel availability), RNC 7/11 (gi grips let defender strip hands + top consolidates to floor to finish, so standing RNC ticks up no-gi), Body Triangle 4/6 (sweat/looseness -> lock mechanical control no-gi), Truck 2/3 (minor). Rank order recognized by the position's own coach (Marcelo). All SANITY-DIFF site flags resolved in the panel's favor: site was RNC-inflated (30/30) and workhorse-deflated (MatReturn 7, Seatbelt 2) uncalibrated -> panel's head-heavy correction stands. Grounded-technique-on-standing-role oddities (Armbar/Crucifix/Truck) are already floored to 1-2 and logged as removal candidates, so they do not distort the head. Residual minor concerns (RNC gi 7 slightly low vs raw gym frequency; Snap Down 4/4 high-dispersion) fall within acceptable spread and are documented minority voices. Nothing survives as a correction.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move in Body Lock/Bottom is legal and mechanically available in both gi and no-gi, so there are no zero-availability rulings. The divergences are all small and mechanism-driven. Pummeling Escape is the clearest and most consistent divergence (~+2-3 no-gi): with no gi to grip, the escape reduces to a pure wrestling re-pummel of underhooks, so it earns more no-gi volume. Grip Break leans slightly gi (~+1-2): the gi provides more grips to break and a more secure lock to fight. Sitting Guard Pull is a genuine two-camp split rather than a clean divergence — the gi-habit camp (Roger, Mikey, Bravo) puts it higher in the gi because pulling guard is culturally ingrained IBJJF behavior, while the technical camp (Mendes, Lachlan) puts it higher no-gi because there is no grip to fear on the way down and seated leg-entanglement wrestling-ups are a live threat; these opposing pressures cancel to a near-symmetric aggregate (~14/14). All other moves (Turn In and Face, Whizzer, Rolling, Standing, Escape, Reversal) are effectively mirrored within +/-1 between frames.

A rolling reversal from a sunk body lock is a low-percentage panic answer that mostly gifts the back (Gordon, Danaher). Genuinely attempted by the population as a gamble, so it stays 1-3+ and is NOT zeroed — but it is the weakest candidate if the move list is ever trimmed.

containers.frame_rationale: The body lock top is a transport position, not a submission position: its two structural gradients are rotate-to-the-back and return-him-to-the-mat, with a cluster of near-equivalent 'dump him down' finishes (Body Lock Takedown, Kosoto Gake, Tani Otoshi, Double Leg) between them. The gi RAISES the Body Lock Pass (the jacket staples the hips once grounded, so it stays a co-workhorse) and RAISES hip-throw variants, especially Harai Goshi, because grips let you load the throw. The no-gi RAISES Back Take, the Kosoto/Tani trip family and Snap Down to Front Headlock (the slippery, fast scramble makes racing to the back or snapping the dropped head the highest-percentage payoff) and COLLAPSES Harai Goshi to a near-floor value because a real hip throw has no sleeve or lapel to load. No technique here is grip-locked to one ruleset, so nothing is fully unavailable in either frame; Harai no-gi is rare (2-4), not zero. Back Take is the unanimous mode in both frames.

removal_candidates.reason: In no-gi a true hip throw from a pure body lock is near-vanishing (panel 2-4) because it needs sleeve/lapel loading; it survives as a rare gi option only. Not removed now, but the no-gi occurrence is at the low-positive floor and it is the weakest attempt from this position no-gi.

Abandoning a high torso lock to change levels to the legs is generally a downgrade; most of the panel treats it as rare-to-situational (3-7). Overlaps heavily with Body Lock Takedown / Tani Otoshi as 'put him down' events.

Genuine held dissent (not smoothed): Marcelo/Bravo weight Body Lock Takedown ~15-16 as the modal dump while Danaher/Gordon/Mendes hold ~12; Mikey/Mendes weight Body Lock Pass ~16-17 (gi) while Marcelo/Bravo hold ~13.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a grip-agnostic scramble recovery (sit-out, roll, stand, turn, turtle-recover, back-door), so all seven are available in both rulesets — no per-frame zeros. Divergences are of degree, not availability. Sit to Half Guard leans no-gi (buggy is fundamentally a no-gi self-strangle, so the counter-recovery is more drilled there; calibrated anchor gi17/nogi20 confirms the +3 gap). Granby Roll to Guard leans no-gi because in the gi the top's grip on the far arm/lapel can catch the roll. Technical Stand-up is the sole gi-favored move — you can grip-fight your way to your feet in the gi, whereas no-gi sweat and buggy pressure make the stand slip. Turn In and Face, Turtle to Guard, Back Door Escape, and Roll to Deep Half Guard are effectively frame-neutral (differences within ±1, statistical noise).

containers.frame_rationale: The buggy-choke top role is a scramble-recovery / consolidation state, and the gi vs no-gi split is meta-driven, not legality-driven: no move is ruleset-illegal here, so there are no true zeros. No-gi is where the buggy ecosystem lives, so the Finish, Roll to Truck, and the front-headlock/darce/anaconda/guillotine family all tilt no-gi (the sweaty, ungripped arm slides through darce/anaconda and front-headlock chains that define the no-gi meta). The gi shifts weight the opposite way toward slow, grip-based consolidation: Grip Strip becomes a distinct and larger beat (a lapel/sleeve connection must be stripped before flattening) and Turtle Flatten to Side Control leads the gi distribution as the boring correct answer. Crucifix and the pin routes (side control, north-south) stay roughly frame-neutral with a slight gi lean from collar/sleeve control. Net effect: gi is head-heavy on flatten + grip-strip + pins; no-gi redistributes several points into finish, truck, and the front-headlock/leg-entry family.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal and mechanically available in the gi (arm-trap self-strangle needs no lapel), just far rarer than in no-gi where the buggy culture lives; scored low, not zero.
Available in the gi but suppressed: the dry, gripped arm makes the darce slide slower, so it sits well below its no-gi value; non-zero.
Available in no-gi (stripping wrist/arm connection) but a smaller share than in the gi where the lapel gives a stickier grip to strip; non-zero, gi>nogi.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency consolidation route from this scramble; the over-rotation off a failed buggy far more naturally feeds side control than a clean north-south, so real attempts here are marginal (~4-5). Kept for now, flagged as a thin-tail candidate.
Consistently the smallest branch in both frames (~4-5); the anaconda is a distant second to the darce off this entanglement and rarely the top player's chosen exit. Thin tail, not removed now.

Net: the same head-heavy shape in both frames, with roughly 8-12 points of mass sliding from gi sweep-fundamentals toward no-gi arm-drag/SLX/snapdown/guillotine.

containers.frame_rationale: Butterfly Guard/Top is the PASSER's perspective over a seated opponent whose hooks are live, so every value is set by hook-nullification, and all 12 moves are legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi (no lapel/collar pass, no gi-only grip pass, no heel hook) — hence there are NO ruleset-unavailability zeros and every frame value is >=3. The single large divergence is the Body Lock Pass (no-gi ~17, gi ~11-12): it kills hooks by torso friction with no grip required, so in no-gi it is the elite modern answer (Gordon honestly holds 20), whereas the gi offers faster pant/collar grip alternatives that make committing the whole torso relatively less attractive. Smaller, purely mechanistic (grip-vs-friction) gi lifts appear on grip-assisted redirects and pins — Toreando, Over-Under, X Pass, Butterfly Pass, and a slight Butterfly Smash edge each run ~1 point higher in the gi, with Mendes leaning the gi toreando/leg-drag a bit harder off standing pant grips; Knee Slice, Leg Drag, Long Step, Double Under, and both half-guard transitions are near-symmetric.

verify.rationale: Butterfly Guard/Top is the passer's perspective over a seated hooking opponent; all 12 moves are legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi (no lapel/collar pass, no gi-only grip pass, no heel hook), so the zero-free distribution with every frame value >=4 is correct and needs no availability rulings. Adversarial checks all held: (1) The why_selected L1 shift (gi 76 / nogi 80) is large but fully explained by removing the sealed-site's grotesque Butterfly Smash spike (49/49 -> panel ~11/10) and correcting two old-data-error zeros (both half-guard transitions 0/0 -> 5/4) -- the shift magnitude is the expected consequence of de-spiking and redistributing, not a red flag. (2) No zeros to defend. (3) The one large divergence, Body Lock Pass gi 11 vs nogi 16, has a bulletproof grip-vs-friction mechanism: torso-friction hook-kill needs no grips and is the elite modern no-gi answer (Gordon-era body-lock meta), while the gi offers faster pant/collar grip alternatives; smaller ~1pt gi lifts on grip-assisted redirects (Toreando, Over-Under, X Pass, Butterfly Pass) are consistent grip-vs-friction reads. (4) Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames: Knee Slice as the gi workhorse (14) and the no-gi co-leader (15) alongside Body Lock (16), with pressure/smash passes dominating over flashy standing passes against a hooking guard -- Mikey, Lachlan, and Roger each probed and endorsed the ordering. (5) Head-mass top-5 = 56 (gi) / 60 (no-gi), appropriate for a passing tree with no single dominant option. Sum coherence exact 100/100. Every proposed value is a defensible round of its panel_mean (all |prop-mean| < 1.0), rounding toward the anchor where one exists. The only mild tension -- X Pass 9/8 sitting 2 pts below its 11/10 anchor -- is a legitimate position-specific downweight (X-pass is less frequent vs a seated butterfly guard than vs open guard generally) and tracks the panel mean. Nothing is misallocated; the adversarial panel could not break the distribution.

containers.frame_rationale: Butterfly hook control (bottom) is a sweeping/elevation launchpad, and the core engine — the butterfly sweep plus hook/elevator sweeps — is essentially frame-invariant: it runs on underhooks and hooks, not grips, so it leads in both gi and no-gi. The real gi/no-gi fork is concentrated on the entry moves. In no-gi the position tilts toward Single Leg X Entry (the leglock on-ramp, the whole modern reason to sit in butterfly), Arm Drag to Back (back-take meta), and a slightly higher Guillotine threat (sweaty neck, no lapel-frame defense). In the gi, grips add friction and slow the scramble but keep Collar Drag from Open Guard alive as a genuine grip-driven entry that all but disappears in no-gi (dropping to a 1-2 wrist/neck residue). So gi and no-gi share the same head (butterfly sweep) and diverge in the mid-tail: no-gi redistributes the collar-drag volume into SLX, arm-drag-to-back and the guillotine; gi keeps a flatter, grip-fed spread.

availability_rulings.reason: Not illegal, but grip-dependent: without a lapel/collar the drag survives only as a neck/wrist version, so attempt frequency collapses to 1-2 in no-gi rather than zero. Panel keeps it alive (Marcelo/Gordon/Mikey at 2), not a genuine ruleset-unavailability, so no per-frame 0.
Fully legal both frames; weighted higher in no-gi (sweaty neck, no lapel-frame defense) and lower in gi. No availability 0 — both frames retain a real attempt rate.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently balloted 1-3 by every legend across both frames; a marginal named variant of the double-underhook/leg-drag sweep rather than a distinct high-frequency attack from this hook-control posture.
Mechanically redundant with Hook Sweep and Butterfly Sweep (same elevation-on-the-hook motion re-labelled); several legends flagged it as duplicate naming. Kept for now but a merge candidate.
Overlaps Arm Drag to Back — the arm drag from butterfly overwhelmingly seeks the back rather than a distinct sweep-to-mount; low, stable attempt weight suggests it is a near-duplicate edge.

flags: Named-sweep proliferation: Butterfly Sweep, Hook Sweep, Elevator Sweep, Butterfly Hook Sweep, John Wayne Sweep, Sumi Gaeshi and Arm Drag Sweep are seven labels for what is largely one elevation family — mass is fragmented across near-duplicates, artificially depressing the true head weight of 'the butterfly elevation sweep'.

Sanity-diff: SEALED site value put Butterfly Sweep at 41 (plays spammy as an opponent) and crushed Hook Sweep/Arm Drag Sweep/Butterfly Hook Sweep to 1-5 and Single Leg X to 5; panel deliberately did not conform — it lands the head at ~15-18 and gives the real sweep and SLX-entry volume back. No role misread found.
Guillotine appears twice (standalone choke + Butterfly Sweep with Guillotine hybrid); ensure they are not double-counting the same neck-attack attempt in downstream success modeling.
Single Leg X Entry carries the largest genuine gi/no-gi divergence (gi ~7 vs no-gi ~10-11) and the widest R1 spread — high-confidence direction, moderate-confidence magnitude.

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-unavailable — every entry is a guard pass that is legal and mechanically doable in both gi and no-gi, so there are no forced zeros. The gi/no-gi divergences are meta-driven, not legality-driven. No-gi tilts toward moves that don't need fabric to work: the Body Lock Pass surges (+3 to +4) because the seated bottom player has no pants/sleeves to stiff-arm the body-locker off his hips, the Toreando climbs (+2 to +3) off a whip on the naked ankle, and the Leg Drag ticks up around a clean, gripless leg. The gi tilts toward grip-and-stack passing — Pressure, Over-Under and Double Under lean gi because pinning the pants and cross-collar staples the hooks and lets you stack; the gi also lets the bottom player frame more, holding the body-lock back. Knee Slice leads the volume in both frames (it is the universal workhorse pass) and the Butterfly Smash / Smash-from-BHC hook-nullifying family sits just behind it, slightly privileged no-gi where you must kill a live hook without grips to help.

removal_candidates.reason: Semantically generic 'pass the position' entry that overlaps the concrete named passes (Butterfly/Knee Slice/Body Lock); panel consistently floored it at 4-5 both frames. Not a distinct attempt in practice — candidate for folding into the specific passes, but retained for now.

Genuinely rare from butterfly hook control — back-stepping into live hooks invites the sweep/back-take; every panelist held it situational at 4-5. Low-volume tail, flagged as a merge/removal candidate, not removed now.

flags: SEALED site value for 'Butterfly Smash' was 39 (gi/nogi) — almost certainly a leaked success-rate contaminating an attempt-frequency field; panel unanimously rejects it and lands ~9-10. Recommend auditing the source for a success-rate/occurrence swap.

Old site tail (Toreando 2, Over-Under 2, Pass Butterfly Hook Control 1, Smash from BHC 1, Leg Drag 4) was over-suppressed relative to the calibrated panel; the old distribution was Butterfly-Smash-spammy with a starved tail.

Persistent principled dissent on Butterfly Smash magnitude: Danaher (12, hook-nullifier = primary attempt) vs Mendes (7-8, it is a setup INTO the knee slice, not a distinct attempt). Real taxonomy disagreement, not noise.
Body Lock Pass no-gi magnitude spread (Craig ~11 skeptic vs Mendes/Kade ~11-12 staple) is the widest surviving no-gi dissent; direction unanimous, height contested.

'Pass Butterfly Hook Control' and 'Smash from Butterfly Hook Control' are position-named self-referential entries; the latter uniquely lands at half-guard/top (all other moves land at side-control/top) — keep that distinct outcome even if the former is folded.

containers.frame_rationale: Half Butterfly is an underhook-and-inside-hook elevation position, and every move in the pack is legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi — there are no availability zeros. The gi/no-gi divergences are all mechanism-driven, not availability-driven. Biggest fork: Half Butterfly to Dogfight rises sharply in no-gi (gi ~8-9, no-gi ~12) because there is no lapel or collar to stall the underhook come-up, so the wrestle-up is the modern no-gi answer; conversely Deep Half Entry leans gi (gi ~8, no-gi ~5-6) because burrowing under a wrestler in no-gi surrenders the underhook and the back, whereas the gi supports a controlled lapel/deep-half game. Hook Sweep shades slightly higher in no-gi (grip-free far-side dump is faster), and the Rolling Back Take ticks up in no-gi on the climbing lightweight shoulder-crunch meta. The gi rewards the clean fundamental sweeps (Roger holds Basic and Half Butterfly Sweep highest in the gi), while no-gi flattens the basic elevation slightly in favor of the hook sweep and the standing dogfight. Head-heaviness is moderate by design — a hybrid guard has no single dominant action, so Half Butterfly Sweep sits ~14 atop a genuine 10-13 cluster of the other elevation sweeps, reguard, and (in no-gi) the dogfight.

containers.frame_rationale: The single real gi/no-gi divergence here is the Body Lock Pass: unanimously ~8-9 in the gi but ~15 in no-gi. Mechanism is cloth-grip substitution — in the gi a passer pins the flattened half-butterfly opponent with lapel, belt and pants grips, so the body lock is redundant; in no-gi there is no cloth to staple with, so the hips-connected body lock becomes the primary grip-free way to kill the elevating hook and stop the underhook re-guard, making it the modern no-gi meta answer against butterfly-family guards. Secondary, smaller shifts all flow from the same cause: the grip-dependent moves (Knee Slice, Half Guard to Flattened, Leg Weave, Pass Half Butterfly) each dip a point or two in no-gi as body lock absorbs their share, while the hybrid-smashing moves (Smash Half Butterfly) hold or tick up no-gi. Everything from this node is a pass or positional advance — no submissions, no lapel/collar or leg-lock-legality issues — so no move is unavailable in either ruleset and there are no per-frame zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Weakest and most redundant option from this node — a pure half-guard pass is rarely played from half BUTTERFLY without first addressing the hook (flatten/smash/body lock), so it overlaps with the generic-pass moves. Real but marginal (~5-8), logged only, not removed.

flags: no_submissions: this is a passer-dominant top node; all nine moves are passes or positional advances, so the distribution is honestly head-heavy toward hook-killing passes with no finish attempts.

containers.frame_rationale: The clamp guard bottom is a submission-first, arm-trap position in both rulesets — the trapped-arm triangle-armbar chain dominates attempts regardless of frame, so the head (Triangle from Clamp Guard, Armbar, Triangle Setup) barely moves gi-to-no-gi. The divergence lives entirely in the sweep tail. The Scissor Sweep is collar-and-sleeve dependent: in the gi it is a legitimate ~13% fundamental sweep because grips load it, but no-gi it collapses to a rare 6-8% (available, never zero — hit off underhooks). That freed no-gi share redistributes to the grip-independent options: the generic frame-based Sweep from Clamp Guard (its 45% success rate makes it the go-to no-gi sweep) and the momentum-driven Hip Bump Sweep both lean up a few points no-gi. Conversely the Closed Guard to Omoplata leans slightly toward the gi where the sleeve grip secures the entry. No move is illegal or unavailable in either ruleset, so there are no per-frame zeros.
flags: SEALED site values were flat gi==nogi across all seven moves and inverted the two triangle entries (Triangle Setup 18 > Triangle from Clamp Guard 15); panel inverts this — the committed 'Triangle from Clamp Guard' leads (~20/21) and 'Triangle Setup' is the ~14/15 on-ramp. Old flat Scissor 12/12 confirmed as the error; no-gi must drop to ~7.

Two moves ('Triangle Setup' and 'Triangle from Clamp Guard') both land at triangle-control/bottom — they are the loose entry vs committed entry of the same submission; the ~34% combined attempt share is intentional, not a double-count.
Danaher is the standing dissent on the head, holding Armbar co-equal with the committed triangle (20/21) rather than clearly below it; Mendes/Kade push the no-gi frame sweep highest (18-19).

containers.frame_rationale: Clamp Guard/Top is a genuine two-answer position: free the trapped arm (Arm Extraction) or pass around it (Stack Pass), both grip-agnostic and fully available in gi and no-gi. Extraction leads in both frames because the clamped elbow is a live armbar/triangle emergency that must be retrieved before safe passing. The gi/no-gi divergence is small and its SIGN is genuinely contested: gi sleeve friction keeps the arm clamped, making extraction the clear priority (~55/45); no-gi sweat makes everything slipperier, and the panel splits on whether that pushes extraction UP (Bravo/Lachlan/Mendes/Kade: the arm reflexively rips free, ~57-58) or stacking UP (Danaher/Gordon/Marcelo/Mikey: the clamp bites less and impatient players power through, ~52). Net landing is roughly frame-neutral with a legitimate no-gi spread preserved, not difference-split away.
flags: Thin position: only 2 moves, so both are forced into workhorse tier and the distribution is effectively binary (~55/45). Craig flagged this explicitly.
Contested no-gi divergence SIGN (not magnitude): same physical fact (sweat/slippery arm) drives opposite behavioral reads; individual no-gi extraction ballots legitimately range 52-58.

Calibration anchor inversion rejected: the calibrated no-gi anchor (extraction 43 < stack 45) inverts the priority order; every legend keeps extraction ahead of stack in both frames on submission-emergency mechanism grounds. Old flat site value 55/55 also rejected as frame-flat.

containers.frame_rationale: The entire gi/no-gi divergence in clinch-bottom traces to a single mechanism: the collar and lapel make pulling guard immediately viable and stall-resistant in the gi, so the clamped (losing) clinch player rationally bails to a guard pull ~35% of the time. Strip the gi and that option becomes a fast track to being passed or leg-locked, so no-gi the guard-pull share roughly halves (~17) and the freed weight flows into the moves that let bottom re-fight the standing position on wrestling terms — underhook pummeling becomes the no-gi workhorse (~25 vs ~19 gi) and duck-under / arm-drag-to-back entries all tick up a few points no-gi. Break Clinch (a neutral disengage to standing) is essentially frame-symmetric. No move is legally unavailable in either ruleset, so there are no true zeros; the fork is behavioral, not rules-based.

availability_rulings.reason: Available, not zeroed: guard pulling is legal and does happen no-gi, but it is far less advisable against wrestlers, so the share halves from the gi (~35) to ~17 rather than disappearing.

removal_candidates.reason: Near-redundant with 'Arm Drag from Clinch' — the same physical arm drag modeled at greater depth (lands back-control/top vs standing-rear-clinch/top). Panel judges it a modeling split of one action, not a distinct decision; the deeper to-back variant is the rarest move here. Log only, do not remove.

flags: Two arm-drag entries ('Arm Drag from Clinch' -> standing-rear-clinch/top and 'Arm Drag from Clinch Bottom' -> back-control/top) are near-redundant representations of one action at different depths; kept but flagged as a modeling artifact (see removal_candidates).

Round-1 ballots were unusually tight (r1_mean_cv 0.037); advisors verified this is genuine agreement anchored to lived experience for this well-understood position, not fake consensus or over-anchoring on the calibrated occurrence anchors.

Sanity-diff: sealed uncalibrated site values were 40/40 across gi and no-gi for Guard Pull and 15/15 for Underhook Pummeling — they missed the collar-driven gi/no-gi fork entirely (overstated no-gi guard pull, understated the no-gi underhook-pummel staple). Panel deliberately does not conform.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi does not change WHAT wins from Clinch/Top — the leg-attack trio (single leg, double leg, snap-down to front headlock) is the head-heavy backbone in both rulesets, carrying roughly 35-42% combined. What the gi changes is the MENU around that spine. Collar-and-sleeve grips load the classic judo throws, so uchi mata (~7-8 gi vs ~3 nogi) and kouchi gari (~6 gi vs ~4 nogi) are genuine gi weapons that shrink to grip-reduced situationals without the jacket — reduced, never unavailable, so no per-frame zero. Conversely, no-gi rewards skin-on-skin wrestling and neck exposure: the body-lock takedown climbs from a gi common (~6) to a near-workhorse (~8-9 nogi), the snap-down-to-front-headlock and its guillotine both tick up no-gi (sweat and no collar to defend the neck), and high crotch rises as a pure wrestling entry. Every move is legal and attempted in both frames, so there are no availability rulings — only mechanism-driven grip-vs-friction shifts.

removal_candidates.reason: A body-lock PASS is a guard-passing action, not a standing-clinch takedown; from a neutral standing clinch it is rarely the actual attempt (you body-lock TAKEDOWN, then pass later). Consistently the lowest situational (~3 gi / 3-4 nogi). Kept for now but flagged as a near-never from this specific state.

Real technique but from a bare clinch it is a low-frequency setup rather than a primary attempt; sits at the situational floor (~5/6). Candidate for consolidation into the two-on-one/arm-drag family rather than a standalone clinch-top attempt.

flags: Sealed site values badly under-weighted the three true workhorses (Double Leg 11, Single Leg 10, Snapdown 10 vs calibrated anchors 13-16) and the no-gi body-lock takedown (site 2 vs panel ~8-9 nogi); they also over-smeared Duck Under and Fireman's at a flat 10. Panel corrected all of these and did not conform to the old flat gi==nogi numbers.

Guillotine Choke from Clinch is the only submission in this move set; it is scored as an ATTEMPT frequency from a neutral standing clinch (kept modest, 3-5 gi / 5-7 nogi) — do not confuse this with its finish/success rate.
Uchi Mata's gi>nogi divergence (~7-8 vs ~3) is the largest ruleset split in the set and is mechanism-justified (collar/sleeve grip loads the throw); it is a reduction, not an availability zero.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split here is driven entirely by grips. In the gi, closed-guard bottom is a collar-and-sleeve offense: the cross collar choke is a top-3 attempt, the scissor sweep is the single highest-volume move (grip on collar + sleeve), and the loop choke and climbing collar attacks are live — so gi mass concentrates on Scissor, Triangle Setup, Cross Collar, Hip Bump, Armbar and Triangle Choke. Strip the cloth and two moves become mechanically impossible (Cross Collar Choke and Loop Choke -> hard 0, logged as availability rulings), while the grip-dependent gi sweeps (Scissor, Pendulum, Flower, Omoplata Sweep) lose roughly half their volume without sleeve/collar control. No-gi redistributes that freed mass into the neck-and-frame economy: the Guillotine Setup becomes the dominant single attempt, Hip Bump and Kimura chains rise, the Triangle Setup stays high, and overhook/rubber-guard transitions pick up (Bravo's genuine upward outlier on rubber guard). Both frames stay head-heavy over ~6-7 moves with an honest long tail; no smearing.

Extremely niche 10th-Planet-adjacent transition; essentially never seen at floor volume in either frame. Old site value of 5 was a gross over-weight.

Rare submission entry; consistently at floor, tail candidate.

flags: Flying Armbar from Closed Guard is mechanically questionable from a closed guard; Gordon and Craig argued for a true 0 on plausibility grounds. Panel held it at floor 1/1 because the objection is mechanism-based, not ruleset availability — flagged for content review / possible removal.

Old SEALED site values were flat (gi==nogi) and badly compressed: Hip Bump 15 (over), Scissor 6 (under for gi), Tarikoplata 3 and Closed Guard to Hindulotine 5 (grossly over-weighted near-never moves), Cross Collar 5 no-gi (should be 0). Panel did NOT conform; calibrated distribution supersedes them.

Two submissions (Wrist Lock, and the whole spinning/rolling armbar tail) plus several guard transitions sit at floor 1-2; distribution is intentionally head-heavy per statistician/game-designer guidance so the in-browser opponent plays a recognizable closed-guard-bottom game rather than a mushy smear.
Cross Collar Choke and Loop Choke drop from live gi attempts to hard 0 no-gi — the only two ruleset-driven zeros; every other move retains a >=1 floor in both frames.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Giles/Roger + Statistician) tried to break the distribution and failed to find a calibration-grade fault. Sums are exact (gi 100 / nogi 100). Head-mass is defensible for the widest guard in BJJ: gi top-5 = 37%, no-gi top-5 = 41%, top-7 = 48%/52% — head-heavy but not smeared. The two zeros (Cross Collar Choke, Loop Choke, both no-gi) are collar-mechanism-dependent with unanimous panel_mean 0.0 and explicit availability rulings — bulletproof; every other move keeps a >=1 floor in both frames. Every gi/no-gi divergence has a stated grip mechanism: Scissor/Pendulum/Flower/Omoplata sweeps shed ~half their gi volume without sleeve/collar; Guillotine Setup rises to co-top no-gi (10); rubber-guard/overhook transitions rise no-gi (Bravo outlier); Cross Collar and Loop go to 0. Rank order is a coach-recognizable closed-guard-bottom game (Scissor 9, Triangle Setup 8, Hip Bump 7, Cross Collar 7, Armbar 6, Pendulum 6, Kimura 5, Triangle Choke 5 in gi). Two objections surfaced and were resolved as CONTENT-DEDUP flags, NOT calibration corrections: (1) the triangle family spans four near-synonymous nodes (Setup 8/10, Choke 5/6, CG-to-Triangle 3/4, Switch 2/2) aggregating to gi 18 / nogi 22 — but the aggregate is correct for elite closed guard and the within-family allocation is strictly monotone with no inversion; (2) nine junk/redundant tail nodes (Rolling/Spinning/Flying Armbar, Monoplata, Omoplata to Back, Muscle Sweep, Diamond Guard, Tarikoplata, Hindulotine) sit at flat gi=1 (dispersion 0.03, floor artifact) — this is correct head-heavy flooring of an over-populated hub, not a smear, since each is a real graph node needing nonzero mass and none deserves more. Every proposed_final is within ~1 of its panel_mean. All 33 moves accepted; the 'over-populated hub' why_selected concern was handled correctly by flooring the redundant tail rather than smearing.

containers.frame_rationale: The single dominant gi/no-gi axis here is HOW you open the guard. In no-gi there is no collar to pin the top player down, so the standing guard break becomes the default opening (Stand Up nogi ~22-25 vs gi ~17-19), and the mass it gains comes directly out of the kneeling, grip-based Guard Opening Sequence (gi ~23 vs nogi ~19), which is a cloth-dependent mechanic. Two secondary rules/grip divergences: the Ezekiel Choke is a sleeve-assisted gi trick (gi ~4-6, nogi floor 1-2 via the bare-arm variant), and the Can Opener flips the other way (gi ~2-3, nogi ~5-7) because IBJJF effectively restricts aggressive neck-cranking from closed guard while ADCC/EBI-style no-gi rules leave it live as an opener. Posture Recovery, Stack Pass, and Knee Slice are essentially frame-neutral. No move is unavailable in either ruleset, so there are no per-frame zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: No-gi occurrence lands at the 1-2 floor across the panel — inside-the-guard Ezekiel is a gi-sleeve trick that only barely exists no-gi (wrist/forearm variant). Legal both frames so not removed, but flagged as near-vestigial in no-gi.

A neck-crank guard-opener the panel judges genuinely rare from here (gi ~3, nogi ~5). IBJJF effectively restricts it and it is widely considered a low-percentage/discouraged action; kept because it is a legal, occasionally-used no-gi opener, but a candidate for removal if the move roster is ever trimmed.

containers.frame_rationale: All six moves are grip-agnostic in this overhook-plus-head-control frame, so no move is ruleset-unavailable (no zeros). The divergences are mechanism-driven: the omoplata attempts higher in the gi because cloth friction pins the trapped arm and preserves the shoulder-lock finish, whereas in no-gi it slips and gets shaded down; both triangle entries tick up in no-gi because the overhook itself replaces grips as the primary control, so players commit to the triangle clamp harder; the kimura runs slightly higher in no-gi because grip-fighting and posting scrambles expose the kimura grip, while in the gi the collar offers competing options. Hip bump and the frame-preserving sweep are essentially frame-neutral, with the sweep marginally lower in no-gi where the triangle chains absorb more of the attention.

removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically fights the frame — sitting up to hip-bump surrenders the overhook and head control that define Diamond Guard. It is the lowest-attempt move and largely redundant with the frame-preserving 'Sweep from Diamond Guard' as the posture answer. Kept for now, but a candidate for pruning if the move list is trimmed.

flags: Two moves ('Triangle Setup' and 'Triangle from Diamond Guard') both land at triangle-control/bottom and split the triangle-entry load; combined they carry ~42-46% of attempts, which is head-heavy but authentic to this frame — verify they are not double-counting the same physical entry in the graph.

SEALED old site values inverted the two most diagnostic moves: 'Triangle from Diamond Guard' was 13 (should co-lead) and 'Hip Bump Sweep' was 18 (should be tail). The panel corrected this ranking and did NOT conform to the old numbers.

containers.frame_rationale: Diamond Guard/Top is a trapped-man position: the top player's posture is broken and one arm is overhooked with head control, so gi and no-gi mechanics are nearly identical — none of the four moves is a grip-dependent (collar/lapel) technique, so no availability zeros apply. The only honest divergences are small and mechanism-backed: Overhook Strip ticks up ~1-2 points in no-gi because sweat lets the trapped arm slip free more easily, and Guard Opening Sequence drops ~1 point in no-gi because gi stalls afford the top player an extra beat to begin opening. Guard Pass is frame-flat and floored in both because you cannot pass a locked diamond before dismantling the frame.

removal_candidates.reason: Not a removal, but flagged as the weakest attempt: passing a fully locked diamond frame is mechanically premature and near-always fails until the overhook is stripped. Panel floored it (~13-19) rather than zeroing because the premature-pass impulse is real; kept for graph continuity to side-control/top.

flags: Old site value overweighted Posture Recovery (42) as a single dominant peak and underweighted Overhook Strip (18); panel unanimously reads Strip as the co-lead workhorse and split the two workhorses (~32/30) rather than one 42-spike.
Tight R1 seed (mean CV 0.086); primary residual dissent is Strip-vs-Posture lead ordering (Lachlan holds them near co-equal; Kade pushes Strip to 38 / Pass to 13).

containers.frame_rationale: In the gi, collar-sleeve is a control-first distance guard: the collar-and-sleeve leash makes it a triangle/omoplata factory whose secondary spine is the collar drag, the eponymous collar-sleeve sweep, and grip-driven conversions (DLR, spider, lasso). Classic closed-guard sweeps (scissor/pendulum/flower) are present but geometrically strained and the raw anchors over-credit them, so the panel trims them into the mid-tail. No-gi the whole cloth layer collapses: Collar Drag, both Lapel entries, the Collar Sleeve Sweep, and Collar Sleeve to Spider are ruleset-unavailable (zeroed with rulings), and their ~30+ points redistribute into the grip-agnostic survivors — Arm Drag to Back and Standing up in Base surge (a seated wrist/head-control wrestle-up guard), Triangle rises as the concentrated head, and Hip Bump ticks up as the sit-up into a front headlock. Collar Sleeve to De La Riva is the key non-obvious survivor: despite the 'collar sleeve' label its entry (foot on hip/bicep, off-balance into a DLR hook) and destination are grip-agnostic, so it stays live in both frames (Kade genuinely updated it off a literal zero on mechanism grounds; Craig alone holds it low both frames, unconvinced the entry works without the collar off-balance).

availability_rulings.reason: Requires a collar grip to drag the opponent past. No-gi the equivalent action is the arm drag (a separate move already in the pack), so this named move is unavailable no-gi. Zeroed.

Lapel-dependent entry into lasso; no cloth to feed no-gi. Unavailable, zeroed (also the lowest-success no-gi move, 10%, reflecting near-nonexistence).

Panel majority zeros it no-gi; the sleeveless-overhook analog Marcelo/Lachlan/Mikey describe is a different action, so the named move is ruled unavailable no-gi. A minority (Marcelo 4, Lachlan 4) logged a tiny residual share for that analog rather than a hard zero.
Requires the collar-and-sleeve grips to feed the spider-guard entry; unavailable no-gi. Majority zero; a small minority keep 1-2 for a wrist-control-to-foot-on-bicep analog.

removal_candidates.reason: Deep gi tail (~5) and effectively 0 no-gi; heavily overlaps 'Lapel to Spider Guard' as a redundant spider-guard entry from the same seat. Rarely a distinct attempt in practice — candidate for folding into the lapel/spider entries. Logged only, not removed.
Lowest-success move in the pack (nogi 10%), gi tail (~5), 0 no-gi. Lasso from collar-sleeve is an uncommon distinct attempt versus the DLR/spider conversions. Logged only, not removed.

flags: Five of fourteen moves are ruleset-zeroed no-gi (all cloth-dependent), forcing heavy no-gi redistribution into 3 survivors (Triangle+Arm Drag+Standing ≈ 50%) — head-heavy by design, but verify downstream renorm keeps the no-gi distribution from over-spiking any single move past ~23.

'Collar Sleeve Sweep' has a split no-gi ruling: majority hard-zero (named move needs cloth) vs. a 3-4 minority for a sleeveless-overhook analog. Aggregation will land it near-zero no-gi; treat any residual as the analog, not the named gi sweep.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel could not break the distribution's core shape. Both frames sum to 100. All five no-gi zeros carry bulletproof cloth-dependency rulings (Collar Drag -> arm-drag analog, both Lapel entries, named Collar Sleeve Sweep) and the soft residuals (Collar Sleeve->Spider nogi 1) are correctly flagged as sleeveless analogs, not the named cloth move. The heavy no-gi redistribution (Arm Drag 5->20, Standing 3->16, Triangle 13->15 absorbing ~30 freed cloth points) initially looked like dump-bucketing, but Roger + Rafael converged on a decisive mechanism defense: losing the collar-sleeve leash SUPPRESSES the triangle's best enabler and ELEVATES the grip-agnostic wrestle-up/arm-drag, so the no-gi head (Arm Drag + Standing + Triangle = 51%) is forced and honest, not sloppy. Arm Drag 20 is the hottest cell but stays under the ~23 ceiling and was mechanism-unanimous. The Collar Sleeve to De La Riva live-in-both-frames ruling (gi 8, nogi 9) is correct and the name/mechanism mismatch is already flagged for the apply step. Raise gi 7->8 (its own panel_mean 8.02) so the guard's eponymous sweep sits in the top tier instead of below two generic sweeps that were rounded above their means. Rank-order fix funded by Scissor 10->9. No-gi stays 0: named cloth sweep is ruled unavailable (majority hard-zero); any minority residual is the sleeveless-overhook analog, not this move.

containers.frame_rationale: Collar-sleeve guard is a gi-native guard, but every listed move here is a PASS, and passes are legal in both rulesets — so there are no availability zeros, only magnitude reweighting. The single cleanest gi/no-gi divergence, agreed by all 10 legends, is the Toreando Pass: in the gi the bottom player's sleeve grip anchors the passer's arm and the collar grip breaks his posture, suppressing the toreando to ~10; in no-gi there is no sleeve to anchor that arm, so once the bicep-foot is cleared the passer can run the legs and the toreando jumps to ~14, becoming a co-leader with the knee slice. Secondary, smaller divergences follow the same grip-dependence logic: the grip-strip verbs (Headquarters, 'Pass Collar Sleeve Guard', Bull Pass, Double Under) shed a point or two in no-gi because there is less to grip and strip, while the other speed pass (Leg Drag) ticks up; the Knee Slice stays flat as the ruleset-agnostic king. The distribution is deliberately head-heavy — four co-leaders (Knee Slice, Headquarters, Toreando[no-gi], Leg Drag) at 11-14, a defined second tier led by 'Pass Collar Sleeve Guard', then an honest 5-9 tail — correcting the old site's role misread that spiked Headquarters to 34 (HQ is a control HUB you pass FROM, not the pass itself) and nearly deleted the two position-specific named passes (Bull / Pass-Collar-Sleeve at 1).

availability_rulings.reason: AVAILABLE (non-zero). The named generic grip-strip pass is a gi-flavored verb (strip the collar/sleeve then clear), so it is reweighted DOWN in no-gi where there is little to strip — but it remains a live action (clear the 2-on-1/bicep-foot and pass), never a 0.
AVAILABLE (non-zero). Position-specific plow that leans on the lapel/collar break in gi; still executes in no-gi via underhook stacking, so it is reduced but not unavailable.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-volume tail move from THIS specific position: the collar grip actively breaks the passer's posture into the very stack the double-under seeks, so it is rarely the chosen entry against a live collar-sleeve. Kept (5-8 band) as texture, but the weakest structural fit; logged for review, NOT removed.

Niche named plow variant; overlaps mechanically with the stack/pressure family and is higher-risk. Panel keeps it at 4-8 for flavor but it is a candidate if the move list is ever trimmed. Logged, NOT removed.
