SANITY-DIFF: old site spiked Headquarters Pass to 34 (gi=nogi), a role misread treating a control HUB as the pass — panel lands it at ~11-13; did NOT conform.

SANITY-DIFF: old site set Bull Pass and 'Pass Collar Sleeve Guard' to 1 (effectively removed); panel restores them to 5-10 on mechanism (real named position-specific passes). Divergence from site is intentional.

Move list is pass-heavy with several mechanically overlapping speed-pass verbs (Toreando / Leg Drag / X Pass / Long Step) plus overlapping pressure verbs (Stack / Pressure / Double Under) — some double-counting risk across the tail; see removal_candidates.

containers.frame_rationale: All three moves are legal and mechanically available in both gi and no-gi from the bottom of a combat-base passer, so there are no zeros or availability rulings. The gi/no-gi split is grip-driven. Pull Guard relies on collar and sleeve grips to sit cleanly into full closed guard, so it sits roughly 3-5 points higher in the gi; without those grips no-gi the 'pull' collapses toward a plain guard recovery, and that share migrates to Guard Recovery (which is therefore a few points higher no-gi). Sweep is marginally higher in the gi because grips help off-balance a posting passer, but it is the lowest-success action (24%) and stays the honest tail in both frames. Guard Recovery is the head-heavy workhorse in both rulesets as the lowest-risk reset from a reactive, defensive position.
flags: Only 3 moves and all defensive/re-guarding; distribution is intentionally head-heavy on Guard Recovery (~42) rather than uniform.

SANITY-DIFF: sealed site values (Recovery 35 / Sweep 35 / Pull 30, same both frames) overweighted the lowest-success move (Sweep, 24% SR) into a near-uniform smear and underweighted Guard Recovery; panel deliberately did NOT conform and holds the head-heavy, anchor-consistent distribution.
Very high R1 consensus (r1_mean_cv=0.042); final ballots differ only at the noise level, with Bravo (10th-Planet pull-guard bias) and Kade (higher sweep) as the mild dissenters.

containers.frame_rationale: No move in Combat Base/Top is ruleset-unavailable - there are no lapel/collar techniques and no heel hooks in this pack, so every pass and both stand-ups are legal and physically available in gi and no-gi alike; there are zero availability zeros. The gi/no-gi differences here are purely stylistic frequency shifts with concrete mechanisms: in the gi you can grip the collar and belt to kill the sweep and pass patiently, so the knee slide and the route to Headquarters carry marginally more weight and stand-ups drop to the floor; in no-gi you cannot slow the exchange with grips, so grip-independent, hip-and-leg passes (toreando, leg drag) and committed scoop passes (double under) tick up, and standing up to clear a leg-entanglement threat becomes a slightly more real no-gi option. Knee slide is the unanimous head-heavy workhorse (~21-22) in both frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Near-exact duplicate of 'Standing Up from Combat Base' - the same disengage-to-standing action under a second label. The panel is forced to split one behavior across two rows, which double-counts a phantom degree of freedom. Merge/remove candidate; kept low (2-4) for now.

Duplicate-label sibling of 'Stand Up from Combat Base'; together they represent a single ~7-9 combined 'disengage to standing' slice. UX-wise two stand-up rows read like an indecisive coach. Merge the pair into one entry in a future pass.

flags: Duplicate move labels: 'Standing Up from Combat Base' and 'Stand Up from Combat Base' are the same action; panel forced to split one behavior across two rows (see removal_candidates).
Old SEALED site values over-weighted Toreando (18) and Leg Drag (15) and under-weighted Smash (7); the panel's calibrated shape corrects these and the panel declined to conform down.

Live dissents preserved (genuine holds, not difference-split): Mikey holds Double Under high (gi 12 / nogi 15); Bravo holds Smash high (gi 13); Craig holds Leg Drag nogi 14; Roger weights the gi HQ route highest (gi 16).

containers.frame_rationale: The only genuine gi/no-gi fork in bottom crab ride is elevation vs re-guarding. In the gi, the top player's pant-cuff and belt-line grips pin the bottom player down and re-load the hooks, so defenders are funneled into the clear-the-hooks-and-recover-guard family (Crab Ride Escape to Guard, Hip Escape, Sit Through) — these run slightly higher in gi. In no-gi, no grips hold you and the sweat lets you build to the feet, so Turtle to Standing jumps meaningfully (from ~13-14 gi to ~16-18 nogi) as the modern wrestle-up answer, and Granby re-inversion takes a modestly larger share no-gi as well. Everything else is a positional escape legal and mechanically identical in both frames, so no per-frame zeros and no availability restrictions apply.

removal_candidates.reason: Panel-wide agreement it is a wrestler's specialist counter that is very rarely actually attempted from bottom crab ride (Bravo/Lachlan: 'you barely ever see it'). Kept as a situational tail at 8-9, not removed, but the lowest-frequency real move here.

flags: NAMING OVERLAP: four moves ('Crab Ride Escape to Guard'→closed, 'Hip Escape to Guard'→open, 'Sit Through Escape'→open, 'Escape from Crab Ride'→half) are near-synonymous 'clear hooks and recover guard' actions differentiated only by landing position; they share one behavioral population, which caps how high the workhorse (Crab Ride Escape to Guard) can go and warrants review for possible consolidation.

SANITY-DIFF GROSS MISS: sealed site values had 'Crab Ride Escape to Guard' at 4 and 'Hip Escape to Guard' at 40 — the old uncalibrated numbers named the wrong workhorse. Panel deliberately corrects to ~19-21 for the named clear-hooks reguard and ~14-15 for Hip Escape; did NOT conform to the sealed values.

Sealed site also had Granby at 22 (panel ~11 gi / ~13 nogi) and Sit Through at 10 (panel ~13); old distribution was a two-move smear, replaced by a head-heavy workhorse + common-cluster + situational-tail shape.

containers.frame_rationale: All ten moves are legal in both the gi and no-gi, so no availability zeros apply — divergence here is meta-driven, not rules-driven. The back take (and, in the gi specifically, the Rolling Back Take) skews GI-higher because lapel/belt grips lock the turtle's hips and kill the granby escape, making the seatbelt more inevitable; Mendes/Mikey push the gi back take toward 31 for exactly this reason. The Truck Entry and the front-headlock sub trio (Darce, Anaconda, Guillotine) skew NO-GI-higher because without lapel friction the head and legs expose faster on the turn-in and the downstream leg entanglements the truck feeds into are competition-legal, whereas in the gi the ride is slowed and those chokes are even more marginal. Crucifix, Cross-Body Ride, Rodeo Ride, and Kimura are essentially frame-neutral ride-family branches.

removal_candidates.reason: Front-headlock choke that requires being on the near side of the head; from crab ride your hands are on the far hips, so it is a rare turn-in mistake-punish, not a real crab-ride line. Panel floor ~2-5. Log only, do not remove.
Same wrong-side geometry as anaconda/darce — opportunistic when the opponent turns in to escape, never a systemic crab-ride attack. Bravo is the only voice holding it above floor. Log only.

flags: Distribution is correctly head-heavy: one workhorse (Crab Ride to Back ~27-29) plus a strong no-gi-boosted #2 (Truck ~12-17), a mid band of ride-swaps (Cross-Body/Rodeo/Crucifix ~8-11), and a low sub tail — no uniform smear.

Front-headlock trio (Darce/Anaconda/Guillotine) sits below its calibrated occurrence anchor by unanimous mechanism reasoning (wrong side of the head from behind the hips); this is a deliberate calibrated-down, not an oversight.
SEALED site value for Crab Ride to Back was 40/40 (uncalibrated over-weight); panel + calibrated anchor (26) land it at ~27-29 and the panel did NOT conform up to 40.

Residual honest dissent left un-smeared: Danaher/Bravo/Kade hold Darce+Guillotine higher no-gi; Mendes/Mikey push gi back take to 31 and subs to floor; Roger holds Rolling Back Take high in the gi; Mikey holds Rodeo high.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a grip-agnostic escape (stand-ups, rolls, spins, frames), so nothing is ruleset-unavailable — there are no per-frame zeros. Divergences are friction/slickness-driven, not legality-driven. Posture Recovery to Closed Guard is the clearest gi>nogi move: the collar and mat friction let the bottom player stiff-arm, frame, and rebuild directly into closed guard, whereas no-gi the slickness pushes people to spin or roll out instead. Conversely Sit Through Escape is nogi>gi: with no collar to pin the hips and sweat aiding the spin, it slips out more freely no-gi. The Granby Roll leans faintly nogi (slicker roll) and Standing up in Base leans faintly gi (collar/belt handles make the posture-rebuild the trusted safe answer), while the Peterson Roll is roughly frame-neutral. The overall shape is two near-tied leaders (Standing up in Base ~23-24, Granby ~22-24), a mid pair (Sit Through ~18gi/21-22nogi, Posture Recovery ~19-21gi/15-16nogi), and an honest Peterson tail (~14-16) — moderately flat because turtle-bottom escape choice genuinely branches on the top player's grips and weight rather than collapsing to one reflex.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency option (~14-16 both frames) and the only escape that lands the bottom player on top (side-control/top) rather than re-guarding — a genuine but situational reversal. NOT recommended for removal: it is the sole distinct top-reaching outcome and the panel tiered it common/situational, never near-zero; logged only as the honest tail.

flags: R1 already near-converged (r1_mean_cv=0.029); the only material Round-1 disagreement was Posture Recovery gi (Roger/Mikey 20-22 vs low camp 19), resolved by Roger updating 22->21 on mechanism (gi premium kept, co-leader claim dropped).

SANITY-DIFF: SEALED site values were grossly off — Standing up in Base was under-weighted at 16 (it is the surest, most-attempted turtle escape; panel promotes to ~23) and Sit Through was over-weighted at 30 (made a false leader; panel lands ~18gi/21nogi). Old values had zero gi/no-gi divergence (all X/X); panel does not conform.

Peterson Roll is the only move whose lands_at is a top position (side-control/top) — a reversal rather than a re-guard; structurally distinct from the other four escapes but retained as the honest low tail.
All five moves have similar success rates (33-46%), so attempt-frequency here is driven by availability/habit, not success asymmetry.

containers.frame_rationale: Crackhead Control is a 10th-Planet turtle-top system whose entire purpose is to harvest the back, so Back Take is the head of the distribution in both frames. The gi/no-gi split runs along two mechanisms. No-gi tilts the 10P-native entries and the front-headlock lane upward: Turtle to Truck (leg-entanglement gateway), Crab Ride, and the darce/anaconda/guillotine chokes are all more available with no collar to frame the neck and sweat aiding the front headlock — no-gi is the position's native habitat. The gi tilts the straight, grip-heavy routes upward: the seatbelt-and-collar straight Back Take is cleaner and slightly higher-volume in the gi, Rolling Back Take leans gi, the Crucifix gets a small gi bump from the jacket's trapping surface, and gi grips enable the arm-peel passes (Arm Extraction, Double Underhook) somewhat more than the no-gi scramble. No move is ruleset-exclusive — there is no lapel/collar-only technique and no heel-hook here — so every move carries a positive integer in both frames and no availability-zero rulings were issued.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in both rulesets. The Truck is a leg/ashi entanglement to the back, not a heel-hook finish, so it is legal and used in the gi — just less frequent than no-gi where it is the native 10th-Planet route. No zero: gi 9-12.
Available in both. A back-take mechanic, not gi- or no-gi-exclusive; Roger trims it in the gi (10P flavor) but it remains a workhorse in both frames. No zero.
Available in both. Front-headlock choke is legal in the gi; simply more available no-gi (no collar frame, sweat). Never zero — 5-7 gi.
Available in both. Front-headlock arm-in choke, legal in the gi, minor no-gi tilt. No zero.
Available in both. Legal front-headlock finish in the gi, slight no-gi tilt. No zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-conviction move on the board (panel ~5/4-5, several R1 ballots at 4). It is a pass-out concession that only happens when the back is fully defended; from a back-hunting turtle-top system it is close to the never-happens floor. Not removed now, only logged — it is still a genuine, if rare, exit.

Same concession logic as Double Underhook Pass — you pass because the back defended, not by plan. Kept alive by Roger's gi-grip argument (gi 6-9) but skeptics (Craig, Marcelo) floor it at 4-5. Logged as a low-conviction tail candidate, not removed.

flags: Old site value for Crab Ride to Back (10/10) materially underweighted a unanimous workhorse; panel + calibrated anchor (15/14) corrected it upward to ~13/14 — the single largest sanity-diff move.

R1 consensus was already very tight (mean CV 0.132) and closely tracks the calibrated occurrence anchors in the pack; panel updates in Rounds 2-16 were refinements (gi/no-gi tilts) rather than large moves, so confidence is high but the tightness partly reflects shared anchoring on the same calibrated priors.

Success rate and attempt frequency diverge sharply here: Guillotine (60% success) and the two passes (58%) are the highest-success, lowest-attempt moves — kept in the tail deliberately so the distribution reflects what is attempted, not what works.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a mechanical escape/recomposition of the bottom player under a wrestling leg-ride, so nothing is grip- or ruleset-gated — no move is unavailable in either frame (no availability rulings). The gi/no-gi split is purely meta- and mechanism-driven and it forks on one axis: standing up out of the ride. In no-gi the modern answer to a leg ride is to wrestle up, so Turtle to Standing (and to a lesser degree Rolling to Guard, Sit Through, Peterson Roll) climb — the no-gi wrestling meta rewards building to base and standing rather than waiting under the ride. In the gi the opponent's grips (and your own) punish the standing exit — the ride man re-clamps as you post — so weight shifts off Turtle to Standing and onto patient guard recovery (Turtle to Guard, Hip Escape to Guard, Hip Escape from CBR), where gi grips actually aid the shrimp-and-reframe. Net: no-gi is stand-and-scramble heavy, gi is re-guard heavy, but both share a genuine five-way recomposition head (no single escape dominates because none dominates on success rate), with the three generic 'from Cross Body Ride' escapes forming an honest low-common tail.

removal_candidates.reason: Generic catch-all escape that overlaps the named reversal Peterson Roll (both land at side-control/top). Content-redundant re-label; panel rates it low-common (~5-7), not a distinct motor pattern. Flagged for future consolidation, not removed now.

containers.frame_rationale: The cross body ride is a back-harness delivery position, so its distribution is head-heavy in BOTH frames: one workhorse (Turtle to Back Control ~20-23) plus a clear second/third tier of back-and-side conversions (flatten, crucifix, the two direct cross-body conversions, crab ride). The single rule-driven gi/no-gi divergence is the Twister and its entry — a spinal lock illegal in IBJJF gi, so both collapse to a rare-attempt floor (2-4) in the gi and rise to real weight (8-11) in no-gi; this is logged as an availability ruling, not a hard zero. The remaining gi<nogi gaps (Turtle to Truck, Darce from Turtle) are meta-driven, not legality-driven: the truck ride and the front-headlock darce are larger slices of the current no-gi ride meta, while the gi population leans slightly more toward the points-scoring flatten and the straight back take. No collar/lapel move exists in this pack, so grip legality otherwise leaves the two frames close.

availability_rulings.reason: The twister is a spinal lock, illegal in IBJJF gi at every belt and banned in most mainstream gi rulesets. Attempts are NOT zeroed — it is still drilled and attempted in gi training and non-IBJJF sub-only gi events — so it floors at 2-4 (rarely attempted), not 0.

The twister entry (setting up the spinal lock) inherits the same IBJJF-gi illegality as the twister finish. Kept at a rare 2-3 rather than 0 because the entry itself is a legal positional movement often drilled toward the truck even in the gi.

removal_candidates.reason: Heavily overlaps 'Turtle to Truck' and 'Twister from Cross Body Ride' — the panel reads it as a redundant sub-step of the truck-to-twister chain rather than a distinct attempt, landing in the 2-7 tail in every ballot. Flag for possible fold, not removal now.
Consistently the lowest legal submission attempt from this position (3-6 in both frames); a niche arm-choke variation off the ride. Genuine but marginal — logged for review, not removed.

flags: The sealed old site value for 'Turtle to Back Control' (50/50) is a gross over-weight — half of all attempts on one move; the panel corrected to ~20-23 to keep the branched distribution realistic and avoid a one-note opponent.

The sealed old site values buried 'Cross Body to Back Control', 'Cross Body to Side Control', and 'Darce from Turtle' at 2 each; the panel judges the two direct cross-body conversions genuinely central (~7-11) and lifts darce to a moderate no-gi tail (~7-11) — an upward correction the process caught.
'Twister from Cross Body Ride' calibrated gi anchor of 7 conflicts with unanimous panel + stage-1 notes that it is an IBJJF-illegal spinal lock; panel overrides the anchor down to 2-4 in the gi.
'Darce from Turtle' has a large no-gi ballot spread (7 to 11) driven by Kade's front-headlock specialty vs the traditionalists; left as authentic dissent within tolerance.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is available in both gi and no-gi, so there are no zeros and no availability rulings. The only structural gi/no-gi difference is the strangle mechanism: in the gi the finishing threat is a COLLAR choke that is persistent and never slips, so the bottom player spends more of each exchange on Crucifix Choke Defense (gi ~13-14 vs no-gi ~11-12) and the top player's grips anchor the hips, making the big athletic bailouts slightly less available. In no-gi the strangle is a forearm/gable-grip that can slip when sweaty and there is far less friction pinning the body, so the explosive escapes (Explosive Bridge to Turtle, Shrimp Escape, and to a lesser extent Defensive Roll / Roll to Guard) run 1-2 points higher. Arm Recovery is the head in both frames (~18) because the crucifix IS the trapped arm and every other escape is downstream of freeing it; it stays capped near 18 rather than dominating because each failed attempt resets the exchange into a bail or neck-defense rather than an infinite re-try.

removal_candidates.reason: True tail (~8): a situational in-tight hip-out that only opens when top control is loose, with no calibrated occurrence anchor in the pack. Heavily overlaps Shrimp Escape and Hip Escape to Guard (all hip-out variants). Content-consolidation candidate, NOT an attempt-removal - it still happens, just rarely; keep for now.

Lowest of the three roll/bridge bailouts and overlaps Defensive Roll + Explosive Bridge (all roll/bridge-to-bail motions). Rolling all the way to a recovered guard from a crucifix is ambitious vs the smaller turtle bail. Redundancy/consolidation flag only - genuinely attempted, not removable.

flags: Survival position: distribution is intentionally less peaked than an attacking position - a fan of near-equivalent escapes with Arm Recovery (~18) as the clear head and Choke Defense/Shrimp (~13-14) as runners-up. This is head-defended but flat by nature, not a smear.

SANITY-DIFF: old site values had two gross errors, both already corrected by the panel - Arm Recovery grotesquely over-peaked at 43 (de-peaked to ~18), and Crucifix Choke Defense + Hip Escape from Crucifix each at 1 (neck defense is actually the #2 action; restored to ~13 gi / 11 no-gi). Panel does NOT conform to the old numbers.

Two moves (Crucifix Choke Defense, Hip Escape from Crucifix) have no calibrated_occurrence_anchor in the pack - these are the reflexive in-tight actions the calibration underweighted; Choke Defense in particular is near-continuous and should not be allowed to drop to the tail.

High taxonomic redundancy: three roll/bridge moves (Defensive Roll, Explosive Bridge to Turtle, Roll to Guard) and three hip-out moves (Shrimp Escape, Hip Escape to Guard, Hip Escape from Crucifix) are conceptually close - logged as removal_candidates for content consolidation, not attempt-removal.

containers.frame_rationale: Crucifix top is a strangling seat where both of the opponent's arms are trapped, so the position is a submission-hunting ride first and foremost. The dominant gi/no-gi divergence is a strangle handoff between two adjacent nodes: in the gi the collar is the best available tool, so 'Choke from Crucifix' (the collar/cross-choke) leads at ~20-24 and the one-arm RNC drops to ~13; in no-gi there is no collar, so 'Choke' degrades to a shoulder/arm-triangle pressure strangle and falls to ~16-18 while the 'Rear Naked Choke from Crucifix' (short one-arm strangle on the exposed neck) takes over as the primary kill at ~18-22. Secondary gi/no-gi shifts follow the same grip logic: Kimura is slightly higher in no-gi (slick arm, no sleeve to grip back), Armbar and Back Control Maintenance a shade higher in the gi (fabric assists isolation and re-gripping). Crucifix Maintenance sits ~15-16 in both frames - a genuine control-volume action the calibrated anchors under-count - and the two 'advance to mount' moves plus the bicep slicer form an honest tail. No move is ruleset-illegal to a blanket zero; every divergence is mechanism-driven by collar presence and grip friction.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal but belt-restricted in IBJJF gi (brown/black only) and banned in many lower-belt/beginner rulesets. Not blanket-illegal, so it stays at the rare floor (2) rather than being zeroed.

Legal under ADCC and most advanced no-gi rulesets but a genuine novelty rarely drilled or hit. Restricted in some sub-only/beginner formats but not blanket-illegal, so it holds the rare floor (4), not zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Consensus 'rare' across all 10 legends (2 gi / 4 nogi). A legality-gated party trick even under ADCC rules; it happens but is near the bottom of every ballot. Logged for review, not removed - it remains a real, if fringe, attack from the position.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site values are a two-move smear (Choke 38 + Back Control Maintenance 18 = 56% on two moves) with a near-dead RNC (8) and Crucifix Maintenance (3). The panel corrects this - Choke down to ~17-24, RNC up to ~18-22 no-gi, Crucifix Maintenance up to ~15-16 - and deliberately does NOT conform to the old numbers.

Choke from Crucifix was the largest R1 disagreement and it was a DEFINITION dispute (collar-only bucket vs generic-strangle bucket), resolved as: Choke = collar/cross-choke (gi-native) that degrades to shoulder/arm-triangle pressure in no-gi; RNC = the one-arm short strangle. This ruling drives the entire gi/no-gi share split.

Two overlapping strangle nodes (Choke from Crucifix + RNC from Crucifix) are partial substitutes across rulesets - node semantics should be kept distinct in content to avoid double-counting the neck attack.
Bicep Slicer is legality/belt-restricted, not fully available in all rulesets; kept at the rare floor (never zeroed) and logged as a removal candidate.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a body-mechanics escape from a front-headlock darce, so all 8 are available in both frames — no zeros, no availability rulings. Divergences are small and mechanism-driven. The gi's added friction makes the darce itself rarer to enter and slightly holds the caught player in place, so the gi marginally favors grip-posted lanes like the Back Door slide in the majority read (anchor gi 16 > nogi 13); no-gi's slipperiness modestly raises Counter Roll and, per the Lachlan/Mendes dissent, the Back Door slide-out (sweat lets you slip what gi friction holds). Frame Escape and Arm Extraction — the two core defensive beats — are essentially frame-agnostic. Net: gi/nogi are MIRRORED within noise on every move; the only honest directional splits are a couple of points on Back Door (directional dissent), Counter Roll (nogi-favored), and Frame/Step Over (nogi-favored friction).

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency move from this position — rolling into a set or nearly-set darce feeds the finish; panel keeps it live (5-7) only as an early-window scramble, but it is the clear removal candidate if the position's move list is ever trimmed.

flags: Old SEALED site value had Frame Escape from Darce at 4 (gi/nogi) — a genuine underweight of a core defensive beat; panel corrects it upward to ~13-14. Old site also over-weighted Arm Extraction (27) and Granby Roll (14) vs the calibrated head-heavy distribution.

Residual dissent on Counter Roll to Top magnitude: Craig/Lachlan/Marcelo hold higher no-gi (6-8) as a live scramble; Gordon/Bravo hold lowest (4-5) as feeding the finish. Genuine hold, not difference-splitting.

Residual dissent on Frame Escape tier: Bravo/Kade/Gordon treat it as a distinct workhorse (15-17); Danaher/Lachlan/Mendes/Roger fold it near extraction to avoid double-counting the same first beat (12-13).

containers.frame_rationale: Every move from locked Darce Control is legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi (the darce is a same-side gable-grip strangle, not a collar/lapel move, and nothing here is gi-illegal), so there are no availability-zeros and the structure is mirrored. The only real divergence is friction-driven frequency shift: no-gi sweat and a friction-free arm make the choke slide finish easier, so the finish attempt runs ~3 points higher no-gi (~35 vs ~32 gi); conversely the gi lapel/collar jams the arm slide and rewards points, so gi attackers bail into positional conversions (Side Control to Mount, Side Control to North-South) a couple points more often. Maintenance and the turtle back-take are essentially identical across frames. frame_confidence is mirrored on structure, forked only on the friction-driven choke/mount/north-south trio.

removal_candidates.reason: Duplicate of 'Switch to Anaconda Configuration' - both encode the same front-headlock switch from darce to anaconda control and land at the same node (anaconda-control/top). The panel (Craig, Bravo, Mikey, Lachlan, Gordon) unanimously flagged them as one move splitting one budget. Retained-but-lowest for now; this entry is the redundant one and should be merged/removed in a schema pass.

flags: DUPLICATE_MOVE: 'Switch to Anaconda Configuration' and 'Darce to Anaconda Switch' are the same darce->anaconda front-headlock switch (identical lands_at anaconda-control/top); they split one occurrence budget and should be consolidated.
MISSING_LANDS_AT: 'Darce to Anaconda Switch' has no lands_at in the pack (the duplicate is under-specified), reinforcing that it is the redundant entry.

SANITY_DIFF_GROSS_MISS: SEALED site value put 'Darce Control Maintenance' at 2 and 'Darce to Anaconda Switch' at 1 while over-weighting 'Darce Choke' at 54; the old site had no maintenance/adjustment bucket. Panel corrects maintenance up to ~19 and redistributes; combined squeeze+adjust (~51-54) coheres with the old choke-only 54, so no role misread - the panel does not conform to the 54.

containers.frame_rationale: De La Riva bottom is effectively two different positions depending on the fabric, and the divergence is grip-driven rather than stylistic. In the gi it is a genuine sweeping and back-taking guard: the belt-and-pants berimbolo is a real workhorse (~13-15), the signature DLR sweep dominates off the sleeve-and-ankle grips (~16), and lapel/worm-guard is a serious modern channel (~6-10). Strip the fabric and three attack channels either die or shrink — lapel guard goes to a structural zero (no lapel to wrap), the berimbolo collapses to ~5-7 because a shallow hook with no sleeve/belt anchor exposes the heel to inside heel hooks, and the classic sweep degrades (~11-14) because you lose the sleeve-drag finish while keeping the foot-on-hip off-balance. That deleted probability mass re-homes onto the leg-entry channels: no-gi DLR becomes an entry hub where single-leg-X entry (~20-25, the biggest disagreement, Craig/Gordon/Danaher/Kade high, Mikey/Marcelo lower) and the X-guard transition (~16-19) own roughly 40% of attempts, with the tripod sweep rising slightly (~11) as the safe non-heel-exposing option. Gi is head-heavy across four moves (DLR Sweep, Berimbolo, X-Guard, SLX); no-gi is head-heavy across three entries (SLX, X-Guard, DLR Sweep).

availability_rulings.move: De La Riva to Lapel Guard
availability_rulings.reason: Requires a gi lapel/skirt to feed and wrap; there is no fabric analog in no-gi, so the transition is structurally unavailable. Genuine ruleset-unavailability zero, not merely rare. Unanimous panel.

removal_candidates.move: De La Riva to Grasshopper Guard
removal_candidates.reason: Grasshopper guard is a gi-grip construct (feet-on-biceps plus a sleeve anchor). In no-gi it is nearly non-existent (panel floors it at 1-2) and even in gi it sits at the bottom of the tail (~1-2). A gripless version technically exists so it is NOT a hard availability zero, but it is the weakest DLR channel and a candidate for later consolidation.
Consistently the rarest actual sweep from DLR (gi ~2, no-gi ~1-2). It happens but at population level it is a niche entry; logged as a thin-tail move to watch, not removed now.

flags: SEALED sanity-diff: site values are flat gi==nogi and grossly underweight the signature De La Riva Sweep (9 vs panel ~16 gi) while overweighting X-Guard as the single dominant move (19 vs panel ~12 gi). The panel's calibrated split corrects both; we did not conform to the site's uncalibrated numbers.

No-gi ballots naturally sum low (90-95) even after re-homing because real DLR-bottom no-gi activity is modestly less 'productive per exposure' than gi (a doorway you pass through), and the lapel-zero mass does not fully transfer; kept within the 10-point tolerance rather than force-padding the tail.

Single Leg X Entry no-gi carries the position's largest residual dissent (Craig 25 / Mikey 21) — resolved on the mechanism that the DLR hook is already an SLX shell (near-free transition), but flagged as the one number most sensitive to meta drift.

Tripod Sweep is deliberately higher in no-gi than gi (~11 vs ~8) — a defensible inverse divergence: it is the safe sweep chosen precisely to avoid the heel exposure that punishes bolo/inversion no-gi.

calibrated_occurrence_anchor present for 5 of 14 moves; the panel sits on or modestly above anchors for X-Guard/SLX/DLR-Sweep and pulls the no-gi Berimbolo (~6) below its anchor (9), judging the anchor to overrate the population beyond a handful of elite inverters.

verify.rationale: Hostile 4-round review by Musumeci (gi precision/legs), Roger Gracie (gi fundamentalist), Rafael Mendes (modern gi guard) + The Statistician. Both frames sum to exactly 100. why_selected concerns survived: (1) the 'De La Riva to Lapel Guard' nogi zero is a structural ruleset-unavailability zero (no fabric to feed/wrap), unanimous, not a merely-rare zero; (2) the Berimbolo gi 14 / nogi 8 spread carries the strongest mechanism on the board (shallow hook + no belt/sleeve anchor exposes the heel to inside heel hooks no-gi, so the population inverts far less). Rank order is recognizable to a specialist coach in both frames: gi is DLR-Sweep-led (17, correctly restoring the signature move the site grossly underweighted at 9), no-gi is an entry hub (SLX 22 > X-Guard 18, ~40% of attempts on the two leg entries per the stated doorway thesis). Head-mass sane: gi top-5 63%, no-gi top-5 73%; no-gi being more concentrated is consistent with fabric-dependent channels (lapel, deep bolo) dying. SLX no-gi 22 sits below its mean 23.88, correctly pulling toward the skeptical (Mikey) end of the position's largest dissent rather than the aggressive (Craig 25) end. Tripod above Berimbolo no-gi is the deliberate, correct inverse divergence (safe non-heel-exposing sweep). Every divergence over 2 points has a stated valid mechanism; sub-2 divergences are within noise. No move required correction.

containers.frame_rationale: De La Riva is a gi-native position (hook plus sleeve/collar grips), and both frames share the same job-one mechanic: kill the DLR hook, then leg-drag or knee-slice the knee across the centerline — those two are the co-workhorses in the gi (leg drag ~14, knee slice ~13), with the generic toreando ~10-11 and a long honest tail. The single decisive gi/no-gi divergence is the Body Lock Pass: in the gi it is a secondary option (~7-8) because grip-fighting gives the passer other, stickier grip-driven answers (leg drag, toreando, the DLR-native re-passes), but in no-gi the hook is slippery and grip-strips are unavailable, so chest-wrap body-lock passing nearly doubles (~13-16) — it erases the DLR entanglement, the berimbolo entry, and every off-balance in one move and becomes the modal no-gi attempt. Secondary no-gi lifts: the Back Step Pass (~9-10 vs ~7-8 gi) and Long Step rise slightly because the passer is actively managing the leg-entry threat underneath, and Smash Pass drops a touch no-gi. Grip-dependent moves (X Pass, Knee Slice from DLR, Leg Drag from DLR) tick marginally lower in no-gi. No move is ruleset-unavailable — every pass in this pack is legal and mechanically executable in both frames, so there are no per-frame zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically wrong answer to De La Riva — the active DLR hook and the passer's forward posture make it very hard to stack/smash a DLR player before killing the hook. Consensus floor (gi 3-4, nogi 2-3); it basically never happens as a first-choice pass from here. Logged, not removed.

flags: Body Lock Pass is the largest gi/no-gi divergence in the pack (gi ~7-8, nogi ~13-16) and the sole structural fork of this position — well-justified by grip absence, not noise.

SANITY-DIFF: the sealed old site values grossly overweighted the generic Toreando Pass at 25 while pinning the true workhorses (Knee Slice, Leg Drag) at only 10 each — an inverted priority list. The calibrated panel correctly demotes Toreando to ~10-11 and promotes leg drag/knee slice to ~13-14. Also, the old flat Body Lock 7/7 missed the entire no-gi divergence. Panel did not conform.
calibrated_occurrence_anchor for Knee Slice Pass (14) and Leg Drag Pass (14-15) aligns with the panel; the Toreando Pass anchor (12) sits slightly above the panel's ~10-11 landing but within noise.

containers.frame_rationale: This is the single largest gi/no-gi fork in the batch, and the divergence is entirely grip-driven. In the gi, RDLR keeps its classic identity as a berimbolo and back-take launcher: pant and belt grips let you spin under to the bolo (~13) and stabilize the inverted crab-ride hook, so the flashy back-take options hold real attempt share. Take the gi off and the berimbolo collapses (~5) because you cannot anchor the spin without grips, and that share migrates almost entirely to Single Leg X Entry (~22, the clear no-gi workhorse and the front door to leg entanglements) plus the De La Riva to X-Guard transition. Kiss of the Dragon functionally replaces the berimbolo as the no-gi back-take path but sits behind the leg entries. Retention (Reverse De La Riva Recovery) is a large, honest, near-symmetric share in both frames because RDLR is a junction, not a destination. Waiter Sweep, Tripod, Omoplata, and Crab Ride round out an honest tail with only minor frame drift.

removal_candidates.reason: The closest thing to a non-event from RDLR: it requires a specific arm exposure that rarely presents from the inverted hook. Panel floored it at 4 gi / 3 nogi (rare tier) rather than zero, since it is mechanically available in both frames, but it is the weakest genuine attempt in the pack.

flags: SEALED site value for Kiss of the Dragon (2/2) was a gross underweight -- panel lands it at ~13 gi / ~12 nogi; it is a live back-take threat, not a ghost.
SEALED site value for Waiter Sweep (26/26) was grossly overweighted and flat -- classic uncalibrated smear; panel lands ~9 gi / ~8 nogi.
SEALED site values had zero gi/no-gi divergence on every move, which misses the defining feature of this position (the berimbolo grip fork); panel confirms a real fork rather than conforming.
SEALED site value for RDLR to Crab Ride (1/1) was underweight; panel lands ~9/~9 with Bravo/Craig arguing for a higher no-gi share.

containers.file: content/Positions/De La Riva Guard/Reverse De La Riva Guard.json
containers.frame_rationale: Every move in this pack is a guard pass or passing counter, all legal and available in both gi and no-gi, so there are no availability zeros — the divergences are purely meta-driven. Gi grips (sleeve/pant/collar) let the passer methodically pin the RDLR hook and force the classical answers, so Knee Slice, Leg Drag, RDLR Pass, Smash and HQ passes sit slightly higher in the gi. No-gi removes those grips: the Body Lock Pass surges (roughly doubles) because clamping the hips is the only way to kill the inversion without cloth, and the Back Step Pass / RDLR Backstep Counter rise as players bail early to deny the SLX entry, crab ride, and kiss-of-the-dragon back-take that the inverted hook threatens. Toreando ticks slightly up no-gi (no cloth drag) but stays a weak tail either way. The distribution is head-heavy in both frames: Knee Slice is the undisputed workhorse (~18-20 gi, ~15-16 no-gi) because RDLR is defined precisely as a counter to the knee cut, with Leg Drag the clear #2.

removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically weak from RDLR top because the passer's lead leg is trapped by the inverted hook, so the toreando double-grip pass is hard to initiate. It is still occasionally attempted (kept in 5-8 range, not zeroed), but it is the closest thing to a non-event from this position and a candidate for future pruning.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: the sealed old site values inverted the top two — Knee Slice at 7 (panel: ~18-20, the workhorse) and RDLR Pass at 20 (panel: ~10, a specialized common pass). RDLR is defined as a counter to the knee slice, so a low knee-slice weight is a role misread. Panel did not conform.
SANITY-DIFF: old RDLR Backstep Counter at 3 badly undersells it (panel ~9-11, rising to ~12 no-gi) and old Headquarters at 14 overweights a staging pass (panel ~9).

NAMING: two distinct backstep entries in the pack — 'Back Step Pass' (general backstep pass, lands side-control/top) and 'RDLR Backstep Counter' (specific counter to the RDLR hook, lands headquarters-position/top). Panelists treated them as separate; verify downstream consumers do not conflate them.

containers.frame_rationale: Dead Orchard Control is an anaconda-family front-headlock trap, and its escapes are grip/arm/hip mechanics that are fully legal in both rulesets, so no move is frame-illegal (no zeros). The divergence is mild and mechanistic: no-gi is the native frame for the anaconda, and without a jacket the scramble-out escapes (Shrimp, Granby, Hip Escape) tick up a point or two because there is nothing to grip you in place; conversely, the moves that keep you inside the front-headlock exchange (Escape Dead Orchard Control, which lands back at front-headlock/bottom) drop a point or two no-gi because skilled no-gi players will not loiter in a front headlock where the Darce/back-take is one beat away. In the gi the jacket's friction slightly slows the escape and marginally raises the chance you stay in the pin, nudging the front-headlock-retaining and slower guard-recovery options up relative to no-gi.

removal_candidates.reason: Generic-named residual bucket landing at open-guard/bottom that duplicates Hip Escape to Guard (same open-guard destination) and overlaps Escape Dead Orchard Control; retained only as an honest low-weight tail entry. Candidate to fold into Hip Escape to Guard.

Roll to turtle/bottom against a front-headlock/anaconda specialist is largely mistake-driven (donates the Darce/back-take per the opposite-role move list); genuinely happens but is a low-frequency, high-risk reset rather than a core escape. Candidate to fold or downweight further.

flags: Redundant escape set: four moves (Rolling to Guard, Hip Escape to Guard, Granby Roll to Guard, Escape from Dead Orchard) all recover to a guard, and two generically-named moves (Escape from Dead Orchard, Roll from Dead Orchard) overlap the mechanically-named escapes — the distribution is honest only if these stay in the tail and do not collectively out-weigh the head-clearing core (Shrimp + Arm Extraction + position-named escape).

SEALED sanity-diff: old uncalibrated site values over-spiked Shrimp Escape to 38 (~2x panel) and under-weighted Escape Dead Orchard Control to 4 and the two generic escapes to 1 each; the panel does not conform — Shrimp is correctly #1 but near 17-19 not 38, the position-named escape is genuinely central (~15 gi), and the two tail escapes are situational-real (7-8) not near-zero.

Tail dissent persists to final ballot: Danaher and Mendes hold Roll from Dead Orchard at 11 (distinct roll-to-turtle reset) while Kade/Craig hold 7 (mistake-driven, donates the back); this 4-point spread is a genuine mechanism disagreement, not noise.
Very low R1 dispersion (mean CV 0.067) — panel arrived near-unanimous in Round 1; final ballots reflect real held positions, not manufactured divergence.

containers.frame_rationale: Dead Orchard Control (top) is a front-headlock/anaconda terminal control whose engine is head-heavy and nearly frame-symmetric, so no move is gi-only or no-gi-only and there are no availability zeros. The divergences are meta/mechanism, not legality. No-gi tilts toward chasing the back (Front Headlock to Back ~20 vs gi ~17) and the darce re-grip (~12 vs ~10) because sweat defeats the neck seal and the opponent bails the choke, so the top player follows to the exposed back or switches grips. Gi tilts toward the anaconda entries — both the control build (~18 vs nogi ~16) and the direct finish (~20 vs ~18) — because the collar/lapel gives the defender stalling frames and slows the escape, letting the top player spend longer completing the roll-and-squeeze; the gi pin (Side Control to Mount) is also marginally more legitimate since it holds without slipping. The head is two-to-three workhorses (anaconda finish, back-take, anaconda-control) around 16-20, a common cluster (darce from turtle 13, mount 11, north-south 10) and a situational tail (darce switch 10-12), which reads as a coherent coach's priority list in both frames.

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in both frames; no lapel/collar dependency. Skews slightly gi because the defender is slower to explode out, giving a longer control-build phase before the finish.

containers.frame_rationale: Double sleeve guard bottom is a transit hub in both rulesets, but its exits diverge sharply by grip legality. In the gi the two sleeve grips are a launchpad: the tripod and sickle fire immediately off the push-pull, and a large slice of attempts convert the sleeve grips into stronger open guards by feeding the feet to the biceps (spider, lasso, De La Riva) - so the gi distribution spreads across sweeps AND grip-upgrade transitions. In no-gi there is no sleeve, only a double-wrist tie held for a fraction of a second, so the sleeve-dependent conversions collapse: lasso and both spider transfers drop to a 0-2 availability floor. The freed weight redistributes to the moves that need no fabric - guard recovery becomes the single largest no-gi outcome (~15-19), the triangle setup rises (~12-16, wrist control funnels straight to it), and tripod off the push stays the top off-balance. De La Riva is the lone transition that survives no-gi because the DLR hook needs no sleeve. Net: gi is sweep-plus-conversion and broad; no-gi is retain-tripod-triangle and head-heavy.

availability_rulings.reason: The lasso wrap locks by pinning the opponent's sleeve/wrist against the wrapping leg; with no sleeve fabric to anchor, the classic lasso entry as named is genuinely unavailable no-gi. Purists (Craig, Bravo, Roger) rule a hard 0; others allow 1 for a wrist-control leg-wrap approximation - hence the floor 0-1, never a smear.

Spider guard as named requires feeding the foot into the sleeve and holding via the cuff grip; no-gi has no sleeve to hold, so the named entry is largely unavailable. A no-gi 'foot-on-biceps push' exists but is not the named spider transfer, so this sits at the 0-2 floor with a per-legend split between hard 0 (Roger/Bravo/Craig) and rare 1-2 (Kade/Lachlan/Marcelo).
Duplicate name of 'Double Sleeve to Spider' (both land at spider-guard/bottom); same no-gi unavailability applies - sleeve-cuff-dependent, so 0-2 floor, split hard-0 vs rare-1-2 across legends.

The panel (led by Mendes) treats them as one real technique split across two names; the two entries should be merged into a single spider-conversion node. Logged only, not removed now.

Sits at the submission floor (~3-4) and could be folded into the omoplata-sweep line, but it is a legitimate distinct outcome, so logged only.

The gi/no-gi divergences are small and mechanism-driven: (1) 'Pass Double Sleeve Guard,' the generic grip-break bucket, shrinks in no-gi because there is no sleeve to strip — Marcelo pushes it lowest (6) while most hold ~10-13; (2) Toreando Pass and Leg Drag tick up in no-gi because without a sleeve anchor the guard collapses faster and passers run to the toreando/leg-drag lanes; (3) Knee Slice edges down slightly in no-gi since a sweaty limb without a sleeve is harder to trap in the lane. Overall the frames barely diverge (r1 mean CV ~0.08) because passing footwork is ruleset-agnostic once the grips are broken.

containers.frame_rationale: Double Unders (top) is one mechanical commitment -- both arms threaded under the legs -- so the attempt distribution is grip-locked into the double-under family regardless of ruleset, and gi/no-gi are near-mirror on the headliners (Double Under Pass ~27, Stack ~18). Over-Under leans slightly no-gi for the same no-cloth reason (the hip-walk doesn't stall), while Leg Weave and Knee Slice lean slightly gi where cloth aids weaving/pinning the far leg. Everything else stays mirrored because no cloth-based mechanism distinguishes the frames.

containers.frame_rationale: Estima Lock Control is a specialized inverted-footlock trap, and the gi/no-gi split is driven almost entirely by foot friction plus heel-hook legality. In the gi the pant fabric gives the gripping hands real friction, the trapped foot sticks, and the downstream heel hook is illegal in most competition — so the correct behavior is to commit to the now-or-never estima finish (~38) and chain to the same-grip toe hold (~18), while the saddle conversion sits near the floor (~12) because rotating away from a locked finish buys nothing. In no-gi the bare foot sweats and slips, the estima grip fails, and the inside heel hook is legal and high-percentage — so the rational play converts: the saddle transition roughly doubles (~23) to nearly co-lead with a reduced direct finish (~27), and the toe hold demotes (~14) because the bare foot slips out of it too. Ashi rises slightly no-gi (heel platform) and the kneebar edges higher gi than no-gi (no-gi it competes with the heel). No move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame — every entry is a foot/ankle lock or a leg-position transition legal in both gi and no-gi — so there are no availability-forced zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Smallest tail move and the panel split on tier (situational vs common); it is a genuine same-position leg attack that lands ~13-14, never zero, but the whole Estima Lock Control position is niche enough that the kneebar branch is a candidate to fold if the graph is ever pruned. Logged only — NOT removed.

containers.frame_rationale: Feet on Hips Guard is a distance-management open guard (soles on the hip points against a kneeling/standing opponent) that functions as a transit hub, not a finishing position, so the gi/no-gi split is driven entirely by grips rather than by legality — no move is ruleset-unavailable here. In the gi, sleeve and pant grips let the bottom player pump the opponent forward and convert cleanly into De La Riva (the 'Feet on Hips to De La Riva' conversion and the collar-assisted Tomoe Nage rise), so the gi distribution is tripod/sickle core plus a strong DLR feed. In no-gi, stripping the grips removes the DLR/Tomoe leverage and turns the position into a wrestling launchpad: Single Leg X entries, the Push Sweep to stand, and the Arm Drag to the back all rise while the grip-dependent DLR conversion, DLR Sweep, and Tomoe Nage fall. Tripod and Sickle remain the grip-agnostic universal workhorses and lead in both frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Near-duplicate of the canonical 'Tripod Sweep' — same mechanic re-labeled with the position prefix. The panel treats it as a low-weight residual, not a distinct action; it dilutes the attempt distribution and should be reviewed for merge into 'Tripod Sweep'.

Near-duplicate of the canonical 'Sickle Sweep' — same mechanic re-labeled with the position prefix. Consistently bottom-tier across all ten legends; candidate to merge into 'Sickle Sweep' (note it lands at side-control/top vs the generic sickle's mount/top, so verify the outcome target before merging).
Old-school high-elevation sweep requiring a specific over-committed posture; unanimously rare (1-3) in both frames from this distance-management guard. Genuinely low-frequency — logged, not central.

flags: Duplicate-family nodes: the pack lists BOTH generic 'Tripod Sweep'/'Sickle Sweep' AND position-prefixed 'Feet on Hips Tripod Sweep'/'Feet on Hips Sickle Sweep'. verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Giles/Roger + Statistician) failed to break the distribution across all five attack vectors. Sums are coherent (100/100 both frames). No illegitimate zeros: the two prior-zeros (Feet on Hips to De La Riva, Feet on Hips Sickle Sweep) were correctly lifted off zero with mechanisms (a real gi guard-to-guard conversion; a graph residual). Every gi/no-gi divergence is grip-mechanism-backed and consistent with the frame_rationale: SLX 9->12, Push 8->10, Arm Drag 4->7, X-Guard 5->7 all rise no-gi as grip-stripping turns the position into a wrestling launchpad, while grip-dependent actions (FoH-to-DLR 10->5, DLR Sweep 6->3, Tomoe 7->5) fall no-gi. Rank order is coach-recognizable for a distance-management open guard: Tripod and Sickle lead as the grip-agnostic off-balance workhorses in both frames, then the DLR conversion and modern SLX/Push. Head-mass is appropriate for a fan-out transit hub (top-5 = 59% both frames) rather than a finishing funnel. The proposed_final values sit on their panel means to an average of 0.46/cell (pure integer rounding), confirming a faithful aggregate. The only genuinely contestable number is Feet on Hips to De La Riva at gi 10 -- a non-scoring conversion ranked #3 with the widest dispersion (2.02) and a standing Bravo dissent that it should sit below actual sweeps -- but its panel_mean is 10.73, which rounds to 10, so nudging it to 9 would substitute the verifier's judgment for the panel's inverse-variance aggregate on its single-highest-uncertainty estimate: preserved dissent, not an error. The duplicate-family split (generic Tripod/Sickle alongside prefixed Feet on Hips Tripod/Sickle variants) is a conscious graph-node-preservation artifact the panel deferred to removal_candidates; it does not distort rank (Tripod/Sickle still lead even split) and merging is a structural decision out of scope for a weight verdict. containers.frame_rationale: Feet-on-Hips is a linear distance frame, and passing it is a strip-and-redirect problem in both rulesets — the workhorse trio of Toreando, Knee Slice and Leg Drag carries ~45-48% of all attempts regardless of ruleset. The gi/no-gi fork is entirely mechanism-driven, not legality-driven (no move in this set is ruleset-illegal, so there are no hard zeros). In the gi, pant grips let the passer pin the redirected legs, which inflates the Toreando (peaking ~20-22 gi) and gives a small edge to the compression finishes (Double Under, Stack) that rely on controlled pants. In no-gi, sweat degrades the toreando hold (falling to ~15-18) and the share migrates to the Body Lock Pass — the grip-free hip clamp that shuts the distance game once the feet are deflected — which roughly doubles from ~6-7 gi to ~9-14 no-gi (Gordon and Kade hold the high end, the room lands ~10-11); the Leg Drag also ticks up slightly no-gi as the most direct grip-independent redirect. All divergences are 3-5 points and confined to those four moves.

containers.frame_rationale: Bottom gift wrap is a back-control derivative with one trapped arm: the bottom player is one RNC/short-choke from losing, so every attempt is an escape subordinate to freeing the wrapped arm. The gi/no-gi split is driven by two mechanisms. First, no-gi makes the trapped-arm control stickier — there is no friction-breaking grip to strip, the forearm is glued by sweat and pressure — so active Arm Recovery is the single most-contested item and peaks no-gi (~22 vs ~18 gi); Roll to Turtle and Granby also nudge up no-gi with the higher inversion/turtle culture. Second, the gi supplies frames: the bottom player can anchor on sleeve/lapel, so the hip-movement escapes (Shrimp to knee-shield, Hip Escape to open guard) are marginally more attemptable in the gi (Shrimp ~18-19 gi vs ~16 no-gi). No move here is grip-dependent (no lapel/collar techniques) or ruleset-illegal (no heel hooks/reaping), so every move is available in both frames and no availability zeros apply. Shrimp and Hip Escape are the same hip-escape motor to two destinations, so they share the second tier rather than one dominating; Arm Recovery leads but caps ~18-22 (not 30) because much arm-freeing is folded into those escapes.

Available. Inversion escape is legal and used in both frames; no ruleset restriction. Frequency is low (~10-12), not zero — 'rarely leads' is not 'unavailable'.

Genuinely rare from a locked gift wrap; a candidate to watch for removal if the graph trims tail nodes, but it is a real technique and stays for now.

containers.frame_rationale: Gift wrap is a purpose-built conduit to the strangle: one arm is trapped, so the neck is undefended on that side and attempt frequency is genuinely head-heavy (RNC + technical-mount ride + maintenance ~= half the mass). The single decisive gi/no-gi difference is the collar. In the gi you gain a second high-value handle that spawns the Bow and Arrow Choke Setup (~9-12 gi); with no cloth that move is mechanically impossible (0 no-gi), and its entire attempt share migrates onto the Rear Naked Choke — which is why no-gi RNC (~26-27) sits several points above gi RNC (~16-19). A secondary, smaller divergence: the Body Triangle Lock is higher no-gi (~10-12) than gi (~6-8) because, absent cloth friction, you lock the legs to retain the back rather than relying on grips. Everything else (armbar, crucifix, kimura variants, short-choke variants) is near-mirrored across frames and lives in an honest tail.

containers.frame_rationale: All four moves are legal and available in both gi and no-gi, so no per-frame zeros apply. The gogoplata is a shin/arm choke with no collar dependency, so it is the workhorse in both frames, running a couple points higher no-gi because the gi defender can use collar and lapel to build an alternate frame and clear the shin before the attacker fully commits (a defender-clears-faster effect that produces slightly more early bailouts in the gi). Closed Guard to Omoplata skews a point or two higher in the gi because sleeve and collar grips aid the arm isolation that sets up the omoplata. High Mount Transition and Mission Control Recovery are near frame-invariant: mission control is a pure re-framing of the attacker's own guard with no grip dependency, and high mount is a position-advance that a couple of voices (Roger, Marcelo) lean marginally gi on the logic that gi players prefer advancing position over committing to the flexible choke. All divergences are small (<=4) and mechanism-grounded rather than cosmetic.

Only three small, mechanism-backed divergences survive: (1) Head Extraction ticks slightly higher in the gi because the attacker's collar/head grip is firmer, giving the top man more reason to actively pry; (2) Angle Change Escape is a few points higher no-gi because sweaty, gripless scrambles favor the slithering angle change; (3) Posture Recovery ties or edges up no-gi. Critically there are NO ruleset-unavailable moves here - gogoplata, armbar, passing, and posture are all legal in both gi and no-gi - so no move is forced to zero; the two offense entries stay at the rare floor because they are misfiled attacker moves, not because a ruleset bans them.

containers.frame_rationale: Grasshopper is an inverted leg-entry / elevation guard, and the gi/no-gi split is driven by two levers: leg-lock legality and grips. No-gi, the guard's entire purpose is funneling into ashi garami, so Single Leg X and Inside Ashi are the workhorses and the Heel Hook is a live (if downstream) finish — it is unavailable and balloted 0 across the board in the gi because heel hooks are illegal there. In the gi, knee-reaping rules and behavioral self-censorship suppress the Inside Ashi entry (gi ~5-9 vs no-gi ~13-15), and that displaced frequency migrates to the grip-driven Berimbolo (gi ~7-10 vs no-gi ~1-3), 50-50, Reverse DLR and Granby recoveries, plus the always-legal Straight Ankle Lock. Single Leg X and the namesake Grasshopper Sweep are frame-agnostic top attempts in both. Everything else is available in both frames; only the heel hook carries a hard availability zero.

availability_rulings.reason: Heel hooks are illegal in IBJJF and virtually all mainstream gi competition rulesets, so the direct heel-hook attempt is unavailable in the gi frame — a genuine ruleset zero, unanimously balloted 0 by all 10 legends.

(4) Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames: nogi co-leads Single Leg X 13 = Inside Ashi 13 (ashi entries) then sweep then finishes; gi leads with the two sweeps (Single Leg X 13, Grasshopper Sweep 12). containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi divergence in grasshopper-guard top passing is driven almost entirely by leg-lock legality and grips. In both rulesets the head of the distribution is identical — leg drag and knee slice are the universal anti-inversion workhorses, followed by back step, toreando and stack — because nobody drills a grasshopper-specific pass and the population defaults to the standard elevation-guard toolkit. The single large fork is Counter Ashi Entry: in no-gi, with heel hooks legal, sitting into the elevating leg is the correct counter to being elevated, so it roughly triples (gi ~3 to nogi ~8-9); Danaher's entanglement-avoidance thesis also nudges back step and sprawl-and-disengage slightly upward in no-gi because the real threat is the legs, not the sweep. Conversely gi grips modestly favor grip-dependent passes — stack, toreando, and double under sit a touch higher in the gi where you can pin the inverted legs, while knee slice edges up in no-gi with the faster scrambling pace. No move is genuinely ruleset-unavailable for the top passer (all leg locks live on the opposite/bottom role), so there are no forced zeros — only the calibrated counter-ashi divergence.

containers.frame_rationale: Guillotine Control/Bottom is an attacking bottom position where the player has already secured the neck wrap. In BOTH frames the finish is the head of the distribution, but the calibrated anchor's direction (gi 27 > nogi 23) is backwards and the panel flips it: the guillotine is fundamentally a no-gi weapon — friction, sweat, and the high-elbow meta let you commit to the squeeze harder without a collar to fight, so raw finish attempts run higher no-gi (~28-30) than gi (~25-26). Conversely the GI diverts attempts into conversions: the top man's collar/lapel grip stalls the squeeze, so the bottom player more often bails to Guard Recovery, Hip Bump Sweep, Closed Guard to Triangle, and especially Closed Guard to Omoplata (sleeve/collar control feeds it — the single most gi-skewed move, gi ~6-9 vs nogi ~4). NO-GI in turn skews toward High Elbow Guillotine Variation and Butterfly Sweep with Guillotine (the modern double-attack), both climbing ~3-4 points over their gi values. containers.frame_rationale: Bottom half guard is a two-pole fight in both rulesets — win the underhook (underhook sweep / old school / back take) or hold the knee shield to survive — and those poles dominate attempts regardless of frame. The gi/no-gi divergence is meta-driven, not legality-driven: no move here is ruleset-unavailable. In the gi, sleeve/collar friction slows scrambles, so retention (knee shield, recovery) and deep half hold a larger share and the underhook trio stays king. In no-gi the whole exchange accelerates and grips vanish: attempt mass migrates out of deep half (which becomes guillotine/darce/leglock bait) and retention into dogfight wrestle-ups, K-guard/kimura leg-and-arm entries, the buggy choke, and slightly hotter back-takes — the modern scrambly no-gi bottom game. Divergences are small (2-4 points per move) because the core underhook-vs-knee-shield battle is frame-invariant.

(3) The Underhook Pass edges up slightly in no-gi (sweaty/gripless scrambles favor the underhook control over collar-based passing), while gi friction marginally lifts pressure passes (smash, crossface) for the gi-native voices. containers.frame_rationale: The core engine is ruleset-agnostic: fight the underhook, elevate on the butterfly hook, then either sweep or climb to the back, with a heavy undercurrent of simply reguarding to full butterfly. No-gi tilts toward the Back Take (the underhook climb is unobstructed with no lapel to trap the arm, so it becomes the position's thesis) and lifts the Kimura Sweep (2-on-1/wrist control replaces the sleeve grip) and the 10th-Planet detours (Electric Chair, Lockdown are natively no-gi). Every move is a passing/control action with no gi-only grip dependency and no heel-hook, so all are available in both rulesets — no availability zeros.

containers.frame_rationale: Deep half is a gi-rooted sweeping station whose no-gi identity shifts toward the leg game. In the gi the pant grip powers the Waiter and the come-up cluster (Deep Half Sweep, Homer Simpson) dominates, so those three plus the back-door back take carry the position. No move is ruleset-illegal in either frame - the electric chair, SLX, X-guard and every sweep exist in both - so there are no per-frame zeros; the Electric Chair submission stays a rare 2-3 attempt in both, never removed.

containers.frame_rationale: Deep Half Guard top is a hip-and-leg position, not a grip position: the opponent controls one of your legs from underneath your hip line, so the gi's lapel/collar/sleeve grips change almost nothing about which counter you reach for. Consequently gi and no-gi are near-mirrored. The only systematic divergences are mechanism-driven, not availability-driven: Backstep from Deep Half runs ~1-3 points higher in no-gi because it feeds directly into leg entanglements (deep-half top and the leglock game are the same conversation there), and Back Step Pass ticks up slightly in no-gi's faster pace; the frontal passing block drifts ~1 point lower in no-gi because there is no lapel to stall a patient frontal pass. No move here is ruleset-unavailable — every entry is a legal hip/leg/arm mechanic in both frames — so there are no per-frame zeros and no availability rulings.

Deep Half TOP is the man whose leg is trapped under the bottom player's hip; his real decision tree is backstep off the trapped leg, whizzer/underhook the far side, or knee-slice out. The sealed site prior treated him as a generic frontal passer (Crossface 36, Smash 16, Half Guard 13) and buried the identity counters at 3/1/1 — that prior is backwards; the panel's inversion is right and should overwrite it. (4) Rank order: Backstep from Deep Half (23) as #1, Whizzer (16) and Knee Slice out (15) as #2/#3 is exactly what a deep-half-top coach teaches — backstep is universally THE answer to deep half. containers.frame_rationale: The Electric Chair from the bottom is a sweep-first station in BOTH frames: the reversal to mount (Sweep from Electric Chair) and the underlying half-guard Old School Sweep are near-tied co-leaders, with Deep Half Entry as a common transition and the Hip Rotation Escape as a situational turtle-recovery tail. Grip differences do not meaningfully change the lockdown/leg mechanics of the sweeps, escape, or deep-half entry, so those four moves are essentially frame-invariant (only a sub-point gi friction bump on the sweeps). The single genuine gi/no-gi divergence is the namesake submission (Electric Chair from Electric Chair): the hip/banana-split stretch is IBJJF-illegal in the gi and is reffed out, so it drops to a legality-discounted low (~11-14 gi) while remaining a real hunt no-gi (~18-20), where it is legal and 10th-Planet rooms emphasize the finish. No move is a per-frame 0 — every technique is a body/leg mechanic that functions in both rulesets.

It is NOT set to 0 because it is still attempted in sub-only gi and 10th-Planet gi rooms; it carries a legality discount (gi ~11-14 vs no-gi ~18-20), not unavailability.

containers.frame_rationale: Flattened half guard bottom is a survival state in both rulesets, so there is no availability divergence and no per-frame zero - every move is legal and mechanically available in gi and no-gi. All gi/no-gi differences here are magnitude, driven by grip friction rather than legality. In the gi, the crossface and collar grips make the top pin stickier and heavier, which pushes the bottom player even harder into the pure recovery cluster (frame, elbow escape, underhook recovery, knee shield) and slightly suppresses scramble-based options; pant/lapel grips also make Deep Half Entry marginally more attractive in the gi (gi >= nogi by ~1). In no-gi, sweat and the absence of anchoring grips let the crossface slip, so Underhook Recovery ticks up (+1) as the bottom player re-pummels, and the faster scramble pace nudges Lockdown (+1 to +2, the 10th Planet un-flattening tool), Underhook Sweep (+1), and Granby (+1) upward. The distribution is intentionally head-heavy: five co-equal recovery heads (Frame, Underhook Recovery, Elbow Escape to Guard, Recover Knee Shield, Elbow Escape from Flattened) carry roughly two thirds of the mass, with a situational mid-tier (Lockdown, Deep Half x2, Underhook Sweep) and an honest low tail (Old School Sweep, Granby, Reversal) that reflects the reality that you do not sweep, granby, or reverse from a genuinely pinned flat state - you recover first.

removal_candidates.reason: A granby roll requires spinal rotation and space; from a genuinely flattened, crossfaced state it is mechanically near-impossible and risks a neck crank. Panel consensus is that real granbys happen only after space is created (recovered half), not from flat. Kept in the low tail (2-4) because people occasionally attempt it in scrambles, but a strong removal candidate.

A direct reversal (bottom to side-control/top) from a pinned flat position is aspirational - you must first recover to a hip before any reversal is viable. Panel rates it bottom-tail (2-4); it lands at side-control/top which is a state-mismatch for a flattened attempt.

The old-school sweep is a recovered-half-guard sweep (get the underhook + trap the leg) mis-attributed to the flattened state; you cannot establish the entry while shoulders are pinned. Kept low-tail (3-4) as a post-recovery attempt but essentially never fires from true flat.

flags: Three near-duplicate frame/elbow-escape entries (Frame and Shrimp to Guard, Elbow Escape to Guard, Elbow Escape from Flattened Half) plus Recover Knee Shield share the same shrimp/frame motor action; the panel deliberately damped Elbow Escape from Flattened Half (~9-12 rather than co-leader) to avoid double-counting the same movement across entries.

State-mismatch: Underhook Sweep from Half (lands side-control/top), Old School Sweep (lands mount/top), and Reversal from Flattened Half Guard (lands side-control/top) are all offensive attempts that are barely viable from a flattened, crossfaced state - they are attempted only after recovery to a hip, so their occurrence is tail-weighted despite attractive landing spots.

Two deep-half entries in one pack (Deep Half Entry and Deep Half Entry from Flattened) partially overlap; the panel treated the general Deep Half Entry as a slightly-more-attempted (gi-favored) recovery-to-attack and the -from-Flattened variant as the harder, state-correct but rarer option, both situational (5-6).

SANITY-DIFF: old site values were grossly uncalibrated - Frame and Shrimp hoarded 68% while five central recovery moves (Underhook Recovery, Recover Knee Shield, Elbow Escape from Flattened, Deep Half from Flattened, Granby) sat at 0. These were 'never authored' zeros, NOT availability zeros; the panel overruled them by distributing mass across the five real recovery heads and did not conform to the old numbers.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Roger Gracie, The Statistician) converged on accept over 3 rounds. Sum coherence exact in both frames (gi=100, nogi=100). The why_selected concern (top-40 L1 shift of 118 from old site) is justified, not an error: the old site hoarded 68% on Frame and Shrimp while five real recovery moves (Underhook Recovery, Recover Knee Shield, Elbow Escape from Flattened, Deep Half from Flattened, Granby) sat at 0 as never-authored zeros, NOT availability zeros. The panel correctly overruled and redistributed across the true recovery decision tree. Zero-legitimacy: no zeros in the proposal and none warranted (pure survival state, every move legal and mechanically available in both rulesets, so no per-frame availability zero). All gi/no-gi divergences are magnitude-only, <=2, and each carries a stated mechanism (gi crossface/collar grips make the pin stickier and push toward pure recovery + favor Deep Half via pant/lapel grips; no-gi sweat + scramble pace lift Lockdown, Underhook Sweep, Granby, Underhook Recovery). Rank order is a clean monotone recovery->situational->offense descent that a flat-half coach would recognize, with Underhook Recovery (16) and Frame (15) as co-leaders exactly matching the 'get the underhook, get to your side' fundamental priority. Head-mass of 68% in the top-5 is appropriate for a pinned survival state where recovery must dominate; the pure-offense tail (~12% across Underhook Sweep, Old School, Reversal) is honestly tail-weighted since you attack only after recovering a hip. Only residual quibble: Roger and Giles argued general Deep Half Entry sits ~1 high (you rarely enter deep half from a truly flat pin), and the panel_means even ranked the general variant above the state-correct -from-Flattened variant, which is backwards. But the rounding already equalized them (6/6 vs 6/5), the residual is sub-1-point, every value is individually defensible within +/-1, and moving a single point would break the exact sum. Not worth adjusting.

containers.frame_rationale: This is a near-won pinning-and-passing position, so the shape is identical in gi and no-gi: overwhelmingly pass-completion (knee slice + complete-pass + crossface synonyms), one real submission (the head-and-arm/arm triangle fed directly by the crossface frame), and a thin tail (kimura, back take). Every gi/nogi difference is small (<=2 points) and mechanically justified: pass-completion mass shades marginally LOWER in the gi because sleeve/lapel grips let the flattened bottom player stall the finish; the arm triangle shades slightly HIGHER in no-gi (sweat plus the head-and-arm being a no-gi staple, whereas in the gi the top hands are occupied with grips); and kimura and back take tick up ~1 point in no-gi from sweatier scrambles and marginal back exposure. No move is ruleset-unavailable — there are no collar/lapel-only or leg-lock moves in this pack, so there are zero availability rulings and no per-frame zeros.

In the gi, pant/sleeve grips let top control the far leg and shield, so grip-driven passes hold share: the leg weave stays a real gi tool and the knee slice / long step / smash carry the game. In no-gi the absence of grips removes the frames the bottom player builds off, so the body lock becomes the systematic knee-shield killer and roughly doubles (gi ~8 → nogi ~14) — the single largest fork in the pack — pulling share from the leg weave (which shrinks without grips) and slightly boosting long step and back step, which rely on pressure and hip position rather than fabric.

containers.frame_rationale: Lockdown bottom runs essentially the same 10th-Planet script in both rulesets - stretch, whip-up to the underhook/dogfight, then old school or electric chair, with re-establishing the lockdown itself as a high-frequency hidden action - so the head of the distribution (whip-up, old school, lockdown recovery, electric chair) is frame-stable. The divergences are all mechanism-driven and small: no-gi leans slightly higher on the leg-lace and back-exposure branches (Electric Chair, Roll to Truck, Half Guard to Back Take, Vaporizer, Crotch Ripper) because there is no jacket grip friction to stall the leg entanglement and the underhook is slicker; the gi leans marginally higher on grip-dependent branches (Old School, Underhook Sweep, Deep Half Entry) where lapel/sleeve grips give the bottom player extra control anchors. No move is ruleset-illegal here - every technique (Kimura, sweeps, and the leg-entanglement transitions) is legal in both gi and no-gi - so there are no genuine availability zeros; the two availability_rulings are affirmative notes that the exotic branches stay at the floor rather than dropping to 0.

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in both frames - listed only to confirm no zero. The Kimura is a no-jacket-dependent joint attack; if anything the gi sleeve grip aids control, so it stays a live low-frequency option, not a ruleset-unavailable move.

containers.frame_rationale: Lockdown/Top is fundamentally a trapped, not a passing, position: the entangled leg must be freed before any legal pass path exists, so in BOTH frames the break/escape/extract family (Lockdown Break and Pass ~16, Leg Extraction to Combat Base ~13, Lockdown Escape to Half Guard Pass ~11) carries ~40% of attempts and the generic half-guard passes stay capped as things attempted mostly by tops who misread the entanglement. The single genuine gi/no-gi divergence is the Darce from Lockdown Counter: no-gi it roughly doubles because the bottom player's whip-up to hunt old-school exposes the head/neck for a front-headlock finish with no collar to frame it off, whereas in the gi the lapel/collar controls that whip-up and the neck is shielded, dropping the darce to a genuine rarity (never zero — it still happens). Secondary, smaller tilts: gi runs about a point higher on grip-assisted pressure passes (Crossface, Half Guard Pass, Smash) because collar/lapel grips aid the pin while stripping the leg, and no-gi is marginally more break/extract-dominant because the sweat-only environment makes the lockdown stickier and the cosmetic passes even less viable.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in both frames but NOT zeroed. The panel forks it roughly 2:1 no-gi:gi. In the gi the bottom player's whip-up to hunt old-school is controlled with collar/lapel frames and the neck is far less exposed, so the darce counter is genuinely rare (~4-6) but real — never 0.

The signature fork of this position. No-gi, when the bottom player whips up chasing old-school there is no collar frame and the head/neck is exposed for a front-headlock darce, making it a real mid-tier counter (~8-11).

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the panel's rarest move (landing ~3 both frames, tiers rare across every legend). A specialist 10th-Planet re-entanglement counter that most tops never attempt from here. Not removed now, only logged: it stays in the tail as an honest low-frequency option.

Structural cap: Knee Slice from Half cannot be executed on a fully locked leg (no free knee line), so it is intrinsically situational/low from THIS position regardless of frame — do not read its low number as an error.

Darce from Lockdown Counter is a top-player counter that fires only on the bottom player's whip-up, not a proactive pass; as opponent behavior it should read as a conditional spice (mid no-gi, low gi), not a primary attack.

containers.frame_rationale: All eight moves are available in BOTH frames — none is a collar/lapel-exclusive or a gi-illegal leglock — so there are no per-frame zeros; every gi/no-gi divergence here is META-driven, not legality-driven. The two real forks both trace to the 10th-Planet lockdown being a predominantly no-gi construct: (1) 'Darce from Lockdown Counter' is a genuine no-gi money counter off the sweaty lockdown/whizzer (~11-12 nogi) but nearly dead in the gi where friction and the bottom man's collar grip to come up suppress it (~5 gi); (2) 'Lockdown Break and Pass' as a NAMED action skews no-gi (~14) over gi (~11) because gi old-school players less often run a true lockdown to break. Conversely the crossface family tilts very slightly gi>nogi (collar-assisted flattening). Knee slice, half-guard pass, and defend-the-sweep are frame-neutral staples. The head of the distribution is REACTIVE — 'Defend Old School Sweep' is the modal ATTEMPT because the bottom man initiates the come-up and the top must respond before choosing a pass — co-leading with the knee slice (~18), which is the reflexive passing workhorse in both frames.
