SEALED_DIFF_ROLE_MISREAD: Old site had 'Defend Old School Sweep'=1 and 'Old School Pass'=1 while 'Half Guard Pass'=33. The old numbers buried the single most frequent top ACTION (reacting to the sweep) near zero and over-weighted one generic pass to a third of the mass. Panel corrects both (defend-sweep ~16, half-guard-pass ~14); this is the sanity-diff's one clear gross miss and the panel does NOT conform back to it.

REACTIVE_MODAL: The highest-frequency attempt (Defend Old School Sweep) is a low-finish REACTIVE move — attempt% and success% diverge more than usual here, which is correct for an eliciting-frequency task but worth noting for any downstream code that assumes headline moves are high-success.
NO_SUBMISSIONS: Position is all passes/controls plus one darce CONTROL entry (lands at darce-control/top, not game-over); no terminal submissions attempted directly from this role.

containers.frame_rationale: This is a deep-underhook (dogfight) half guard from the bottom, so the identity moves — the two named pocket-half come-up sweeps and the back take — dominate attempts in BOTH frames. Divergence is driven by grips and leg-lock incentive: no-gi lifts Half Guard to Back Take (no lapel to stall the climb, exposed hips), Electric Chair Transition and Roll to Truck (no friction, live leg entanglements, stronger leg-lock meta), while the gi lifts Deep Half Entry (pant/lapel grips make the far-leg control stickier) and Old School Sweep (grip-assisted come-up). All nine moves are rules-legal in both gi and no-gi — the two 10th-Planet leg lines are down-weighted in gi (logged as availability rulings) but never zeroed. No per-frame technique is unavailable.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal in the gi; the entry/transition itself (not any heel-hook finish) is rules-legal, so it stays a low positive (~2-5), not a zero. Down-weighted vs no-gi because lapel/friction and IBJJF leg-entanglement caution suppress attempts.

Legal in the gi; the truck entry is a positional roll, not a banned technique, so it stays a low positive (~2-4), not a zero. Lower than no-gi because gi friction and reduced leg-lock incentive make the roll a highlight-reel rarity in gi competition.

flags: Near-twin overlap: 'Underhook Sweep from Pocket Half', 'Sweep from Pocket Half Guard', and 'Underhook Sweep from Half' are mechanically overlapping come-up-on-the-underhook sweeps to side control; panel deliberately kept all three but frequency may be spread thin across synonyms (Gordon flagged double-counting risk).

SANITY-DIFF gross miss: SEALED site values set the two signature pocket-half sweeps to 0 ('Sweep from Pocket Half Guard') and 1 ('Underhook Sweep from Pocket Half') while piling 43 onto 'Old School Sweep' — a severe under-weighting of the position's identity moves. Panel unanimously corrected: the named pocket-half underhook sweeps are the distribution head, Old School is a normal ~13-14 workhorse, not 43.
'Underhook Sweep from Pocket Half' is the unanimous #1 attempt in both frames (~17-19); 'Half Guard to Back Take' is the clear #2 no-gi (~17).

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Roger Gracie + The Statistician) ran 4 rounds trying to break the distribution and failed to land a material hit. Coherence: both frames sum to 100 exactly; top-5 head-mass 74gi/73nogi is appropriate for a specialized deep-underhook (dogfight) pocket half. Zero legitimacy: there are NO zeros — the two flagged availability rulings (Electric Chair gi=3, Roll to Truck gi=3) correctly stay low-positive because the ENTRY/transition is rules-legal in gi (only certain heel-hook finishes are IBJJF-restricted); they are honestly down-weighted vs no-gi with a stated friction/leg-meta mechanism, not zeroed. Divergence audit: every gi/nogi split >=2pts carries a mechanism and points the correct way — Deep Half up in gi (pant/lapel grips make far-leg control stickier, 9/6), Back Take/Electric Chair/Roll to Truck up in no-gi (no lapel to stall the climb + live leg-entanglement meta, 17/6/5). Sub-2pt splits are dispersion noise. Rank order is coach-recognizable: 'Underhook Sweep from Pocket Half' as unanimous #1 (19/18) is the position's identity move; 'Half Guard to Back Take' #2 (dogfight-to-back is a genuine staple); workhorse sweeps clustered mid-table; deep half low in no-gi (gi-flavored entry); leg entries at the tail. why_selected concern (top-40 L1 shift of 86) is the SEALED-site gross error being CORRECTED, not introduced: site had the two signature pocket-half sweeps at 0 and 1 while dumping 43 on Old School — a severe under-weighting of the identity moves; the panel's fix (named sweeps as the head, Old School a ~13 workhorse) is the right call. The three-sweep overlap flag (Underhook-Pocket 19 + Sweep-Pocket 14 + Underhook-Half 13 = 46gi) was stress-tested and defended: come-up-on-the-underhook IS the position's whole bottom game, so 46% spread across three graph edges is a topology artifact, not a magnitude error — collapsing edges is not the verifier's job. Tight panel dispersions (0.37-1.39) confirm strong persona agreement. All nine moves accepted; the only nudges anyone floated (Reguard gi up, Old School gi up) fall inside dispersion noise and don't warrant overriding a colleague panel.

containers.frame_rationale: Every one of the nine moves is legal and mechanically available in both gi and no-gi (the Darce is a front headlock, not a collar or heel-hook move), so there are no per-frame zeros. The single structural divergence is the Darce Setup: it roughly doubles-to-triples in no-gi (panel lands ~16 nogi vs ~7 gi) because the bottom player's deep pocket underhook feeds directly into a whizzer-to-front-headlock, and no-gi's slippery, grip-free necks make that choke the reflexive, unanimous no-gi answer — whereas in the gi, collar friction, defensive lapel frames, and the difficulty of finishing a choke on a gripping opponent push the top player back to flattening and lapel-assisted smashing. Because the darce absorbs roughly nine points of no-gi attempt mass, every other move (all pure passing/flattening mechanics that are identical across frames) sits gi ≈ nogi + 1-2 purely as a redistribution artifact, not because the pass itself changes with the ruleset. The head of the distribution — Half Guard to Flattened Half Guard and Knee Slice Pass — is stable across both frames; the darce simply leaps into that head group in no-gi.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in both frames — the darce is a front headlock, fully legal in the gi. Logged only to note it is NOT a per-frame-unavailable move: it drops to ~7 gi due to collar friction and choke finish-difficulty, not illegality.
Fully available and heavily attempted no-gi; the whizzer converts to the front headlock off the bottom man's deep underhook. No availability restriction — this is the frame where the move is native.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the lowest-frequency top option (panel ~7-8 gi / ~6-7 nogi). From the pocket specifically, answering the bottom man's underhook with your own underhook plays into his game; most of the panel would flatten instead. Mendes defends it as a grip-driven gi option, so it stays for now, but it is the weakest tail move and the first removal candidate if the list is trimmed.

flags: Darce Setup is the sole large gi/no-gi fork (~7 gi vs ~16 nogi) and is unanimous in direction across all 10 legends; logged as the frame driver, not as anomalous.

SEALED site values were grossly uncalibrated: Knee Slice Pass at 45/45 hogged the distribution while the position-defining Flatten (7/7) and the three Pocket-Half-specific passes (1-3) were starved, and the Darce had no gi/no-gi split (7/7). Panel rejected the old shape entirely rather than conforming.
Style-based dissent preserved (not difference-split): Kade holds Darce nogi 20 and Smash Pocket Half gi 16; Craig/Marcelo hold Darce nogi 12-13; Mendes holds Underhook Pass gi 10 above the room's ~7.

This TOP role is a reactive passing/countering role — the move list contains no submissions except the Darce Setup (a submission-adjacent counter), so the distribution is correctly pass-heavy with one spiky no-gi neck threat.

moves.transition: Half Guard to Flattened Half Guard

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel could not break the distribution. Both frames sum to 100. The head is a flatten-first group (Half Guard to Flattened Half Guard 16/13, Smash Pocket Half 13/12, Pass Pocket Half 12/11, Knee Slice 14/12) which a pocket-half top-passer WOULD recognize: from pocket half the top player's modal first act is to flatten and kill the deep underhook before committing to a named pass, so no single move dominating is correct rather than the old 45/45 Knee-Slice head-mass artifact the panel rightly rejected. Attack (1) why_selected top-40 L1 shift: the shift is real and justified — the old SEALED values starved the position-defining flatten (7) and pocket-specific passes (1-3), and the panel means (tight dispersions 0.5-2.2) rebuild a coherent flatten-heavy passing tree. Attack (2) zeros: none exist; every move is legal/available in both frames, no zero to defend. Attack (3) divergence: the sole large fork is Darce 7 gi to 16 nogi, with a bulletproof mechanism (bottom man's deep pocket underhook feeds the whizzer-to-front-headlock; grip-free no-gi necks make it the reflexive answer, gi collar friction and choke-finish difficulty suppress it), unanimous in direction across all 10 legends; all other gi = nogi+1-2 gaps are pure redistribution of the 9 absorbed nogi points, not un-mechanized forks. Attack (4) rank order: flatten/smash leading in gi and the darce topping in no-gi are both coach-recognizable. Attack (5) head-mass: top-5 share 66 gi / 64 nogi is near-flat, but for a reactive passing role with genuine option parity that flatness is legitimate, not difference-splitting — the tight elicited dispersions confirm real convergence. The two soft spots (overall flatness; no-gi Darce tying the head as a submission-adjacent counter) were probed as attempt-frequency-not-success (Lachlan) and survive: the darce is frequently THREATENED off that underhook in no-gi, so 16 as an attempt weight (panel mean 16.38) is defensible. Every proposed_final tracks its panel mean within rounding. Nothing reaches an adjustment threshold.

containers.frame_rationale: Reverse half guard bottom is a recovery-first deficit position in BOTH rulesets, so the two frames are near-mirrored: the recovery/escape cluster (Escape, Guard Recovery, Half Guard Recovery) dominates identically in gi and no-gi, and the offensive tail is thin either way. Only two moves carry a mechanism-backed divergence. Half Guard to Back Take runs ~1-3 points hotter no-gi because the crab-ride/backstep scramble is faster and there are no lapel/sleeve grips to arrest the exposure of the top player's back; in the gi those grips let a good top player suppress the backstep, so the back take is a touch lower. Deep Half Entry runs ~1-2 points lower no-gi because entering deep half feeds a leg to the leg-lock meta, a real deterrent that does not exist in gi competition. Invert nudges slightly higher no-gi in scramble. No move in this pack is ruleset-unavailable - there are no lapel/collar techniques and no heel hooks in the list, so every move is legal and attemptable in both frames and there are no forced zeros.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in the gi. Legal and common; grips slightly suppress the backstep exposure so gi frequency sits a touch below no-gi, but it is not a zero.
Available and slightly hotter no-gi: the crab-ride / backstep scramble at pace hands the back more often with no grips to arrest it.
Available in the gi; standard deep-half sweep entry, no leg-lock deterrent, so gi frequency sits a touch above no-gi.
Available no-gi but shaded down: entering deep half feeds a leg to the leg-lock meta, so athletes attempt it less often; still attemptable, never zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Classic half-guard underhook sweep is mis-oriented in reverse half (hips point the wrong way); most panelists rate it situational-to-rare. Attemptable, so not a hard zero, but a candidate for consolidation.
Consistently the lowest-mass offensive attempt (4-5 across the panel); a niche grip-dependent sweep that rarely originates from the reverse-half orientation.
Mis-oriented from reverse half for most of the panel (only Bravo holds it up); a candidate to fold into the generic sweep bucket.

flags: Old site SEALED value put Half Guard to Back Take at 28 - more than double the panel's converged ~12-14 - and starved the recovery/escape cluster (Escape 4, Guard Recovery 9). The panel reads this as a ROLE MISREAD in the old data: reverse-half-bottom was modeled as a back-take launchpad when it is overwhelmingly a recovery-first bail-out position. Corrected; the panel did NOT conform up to 28.

Redundancy cluster: 'Escape Reverse Half Guard', 'Guard Recovery from Reverse Half Guard', and 'Half Guard Recovery' encode nearly the same intention (recover a workable guard) and together carry ~46-50 of the distribution. Mass was managed at the cluster level to avoid uniform smearing across the three near-synonyms; individual splits within the cluster carry the panel's largest residual dissent (Mendes highest on Escape, others favoring Guard Recovery).
Old site 'Sweep from Reverse Half Guard' at 2 was treated by the panel as the generic sweep bucket (~9-11); the panel holds its higher read against the old value.

moves.transition: Guard Recovery from Reverse Half Guard

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-unavailable, so there are no forced zeros - every split is friction/meta-driven, not legality. The one large, genuine gi/no-gi fork is Crab Ride to Back: no-gi it is a frictionless modern staple (~10-13) while gi grips and lapel friction stall the ride (~4-8), so the panel deliberately does NOT converge it. Secondary systematic splits all point the same way: no-gi chases back exposure more (Back Take from Top and the back family run slightly higher no-gi), while gi grips assist the grinding extraction passes (Leg Drag, Knee Slice, Smash, Pass Reverse Half run slightly higher gi). Backstep from Reverse Half is roughly even (gi patient extraction balances no-gi frictionless ride). Net: gi plays as a patient backstep-and-pass position; no-gi plays as a backstep-and-take-the-back position.

removal_candidates.reason: From reverse half top the passer is turned to face the legs, away from the head - a crossface pass is mechanically near-incoherent here. Panel floors it at 4-5 (Marcelo calls it rare). Genuinely marginal from THIS position; candidate to prune if the move list is trimmed, but happens rarely enough to keep at the tail rather than zero.

flags: Near-synonym pair: 'Back Step Pass' (backstep to side control) and 'Backstep from Reverse Half' (backstep to the back) are easily conflated by both authors and the population - naming likely fragments what many players treat as one action; disagreement on Backstep was partly definitional.

Overlapping generic-vs-specific pass buckets: 'Pass Reverse Half' is a catch-all that competes with four named passes (Leg Drag, Knee Slice, Crossface, Smash) plus 'Back Step Pass', creating double-counting risk that inflated some early ballots (Marcelo trimmed 22->18).

SANITY-DIFF: old site values are a role misread - they crowned Leg Drag Pass at 24 and crushed the position-defining Backstep from Reverse Half (5) and Pass Reverse Half (3) into the tail, treating reverse-half-top like a generic side-control pass position. Panel unanimously reweights the two backstep/back moves to the head and does not conform to the old numbers.

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-illegal (no heel hooks, no lapel/collar-specific techniques), so there are zero availability zeros — all gi/no-gi differences are meta- and grip-driven, not legality. The one clean, mechanistic divergence is the Electric Chair Transition: it is a 10th-Planet no-gi invention, so it leads the no-gi attack share (~13-15) while gi stalling penalties and lapel/grip interference plus a messier finish suppress it to a near-novelty (~7-9). Secondary gi>nogi tilts: Deep Half Entry (gi grips make the underhook-to-deep-half migration cleaner; no-gi leg-entanglement risk discourages it) and Knee Shield Retention / Escape (gi grips make holding-and-resetting to a standard knee shield more viable, so retention/bail attempts run slightly higher in the gi). Old School is the roughly frame-symmetric head engine, and Lockdown Recovery ticks marginally up no-gi where more scrambling is needed to re-secure the lock without grips.

removal_candidates.reason: The z-lock leg configuration traps the near leg and denies the free butterfly hook needed to elevate; near-unanimous rare/situational tier with no mechanism to raise it. Kept in the tail (~4-6) because a scramble can momentarily free a hook, but it is the weakest genuine attempt from this position.

flags: SEALED site value for Old School Sweep (30) is a severe over-concentration artifact of the old uncalibrated pipeline — panel converges near ~15 while keeping it the single largest move; do not conform to 30.

SEALED site UNDERWEIGHTS the position's actual grammar: Knee Shield Retention (site 5), Escape Z-Lock (site 2), Sweep from Z-Lock (site 1) were all grossly under-scored, yet holding/resetting/bailing is what Z-Lock players do most — the panel corrects these upward to the workhorse/common band with high agreement.

This is a head-heavy but multi-engine position (Old School + Underhook + hold/reset cluster); no single move dominates >20%, which reads correctly as a lockdown control game rather than a one-move trap.

containers.frame_rationale: Z-Lock half guard top is a lockdown-family leg entanglement: mechanically the top player CANNOT execute any orthodox pass until the laced leg is freed, so the distribution is head-heavy on the three lock-centric entries (Lockdown Break and Pass ~19/18, Lockdown Break from Z-Lock ~16/16, Pass Z-Lock ~13/12) which together carry ~48% of attempts in both frames. Because a leg lock is a leg lock, gi grips do not unlace it and the frames are nearly symmetric. The one legitimate large divergence is the Darce Setup: it comes off the defender's underhook/turn-in during the break, and no-gi skin friction makes the front headlock far easier to lock (nogi ~7, up to 10 for Kade) while gi collar grips and friction suppress it (gi ~3) - a ~2x fork that is mechanistically forced, not arbitrary. Secondary, milder gi effects: Roger and Craig push the breaks slightly higher in the gi (patient, grip-heavy top game) and Mendes/Roger trim Underhook Pass in the gi (the whizzer battle favors the bottom with pant/sleeve grips). No move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame, so there are zero per-frame zeros.

availability_rulings.reason: Available but suppressed, not unavailable: the darce here comes off the defender's underhook/turn-in during the lock break, and gi friction plus collar grips make the front-headlock setup and finish materially harder than no-gi. Forked low (~3) rather than zeroed.
Fully available and a real chain: sweat/skin friction makes the front-headlock lock off the underhook fight far easier, so it forks up (~7-10) versus gi.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely low from TOP Z-Lock specifically (gi ~2-4). It happens only when the bottom over-commits the turn-in during the break and exposes the back, so it sits at the rare/situational boundary. Panel keeps it as a real if infrequent outcome; flagged as the weakest tail entry, not removed.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site values inverted the correct structure - Knee Slice 28 and Back Take 13 were grossly overweighted (treated Z-Lock as generic half guard top), while the three mandatory lock-break moves were near-zero (Break and Pass 5, Break from Z-Lock 2, Pass Z-Lock 1). Panel deliberately does NOT conform; the old numbers ignored that you must break the lock before any pass. Our inversion is mechanistically forced.

TRIPLE-HEAD structure: three break-adjacent moves cluster near the top. Verified they are distinct outcomes via lands_at (Lockdown Break from Z-Lock -> half-guard/top = break-only reset; Lockdown Break and Pass / Pass Z-Lock -> side-control/top = break-through-to-pass). Lockdown Break and Pass is the clear single primary to avoid a mushy three-way smear.
Attempt share on the break moves is driven by NECESSITY (mandatory before passing), not by their success rate - do not conflate the 55-58% success rates with attempt frequency.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Roger + Statistician) tried to break the distribution across all five attack vectors and it held. (1) why_selected: the large L1 shift vs old priors is the deliberate, mechanically-forced INVERSION - a Z-lock/lockdown is a leg entanglement where the laced leg forbids any orthodox pass until it is freed, so the three break-centric moves (Break and Pass 20/19, Break from Z-Lock 17/16, Pass Z-Lock 13/12) MUST dominate and the old site's Knee Slice 28 / Back Take 13 were the error (they treated Z-lock as generic half guard top). Attempt share is driven by necessity, not by the 55-58% success rates. (2) Zeros: there are none, correctly - no move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame, and the rationale defends that explicitly. Nothing to attack. (3) Divergences: only the Darce fork (gi 3 / nogi 7, ~2.3x) is a real divergence and it is bulletproof - sweat/skin friction makes the off-the-underhook front headlock far easier no-gi while gi collar friction suppresses it. Every other gi!=nogi gap is a 1-point rounding artifact of a sub-point panel-mean gap with a coherent stated direction (breaks tick +1 gi = patient grip-heavy top; passes/underhook tick -1 gi = whizzer/pant-grip favors bottom; back-take +1 nogi = scramble exposure). All conserve mass. (4) Rank order is coach-recognizable: break-break-pass on top, orthodox passes (Knee Slice/Smash/Crossface/Underhook/Half Guard) clustered 8-10 in the middle, Back Take and gi-Darce at the floor. The tight post-break pass band (dispersions 0.38-0.99) is genuine equivalence once chest-to-chest, not lazy parking. (5) Head-mass 69 gi / 66 nogi in the top-5 is high but justified by a funnel/entanglement decision tree - the mandatory lock-break is the whole point of the position. Triple-head verified distinct via lands_at (Break from Z-Lock -> half-guard reset; Break and Pass / Pass Z-Lock -> side-control pass-through), with Break and Pass 20 the clear single primary, no three-way smear. The only adjust-leaning note was Musumeci's instinct that Knee Slice (10) sits ~1-2 points rich given it needs a freed knee, but that trim is inside the panel's own dispersion (mean 10.26 +-1.2), reshuffles nothing structural, and does not meet the bar to override a low-dispersion panel consensus. Container accepted as proposed.

containers.frame_rationale: This position is fundamentally the same in both rulesets because the defining variable is the seatbelt/hand connection, which exists in gi and no-gi alike — so every move is available in both frames and the differences are magnitude, not availability. Three mechanism-backed splits: (1) Technical Stand Up to Single Leg is clearly gi<nogi (in the gi the attacker's collar grip drags a standing defender back down; no-gi there is nothing to grab, so you can post and run out the back). (2) Hand Fighting from Back nudges up in no-gi — the connection is slicker and the choke tempo is faster, forcing more constant grip fighting — but it is also heavy in the gi because the defender must simultaneously defend the collar for the bow-and-arrow, so the net gi/nogi gap is small. (3) Granby Roll and some hip-escape variants tick very slightly lower in no-gi because the sweatier, gripless back is riskier to expose. No lapel-only or heel-hook-only moves appear on this list, so there are zero forced per-frame availabilities.

removal_candidates.reason: Rarest genuine escape from a LOCKED harness — the roll exposes the back worse than it recovers guard, so it stays a highlight/flexible-player exit, not bread-and-butter. Panel landed it at ~5-7, lowest true-escape occurrence. Logged for watch; NOT removed (it does happen).

flags: STAGE1_ANCHORS_OMIT_LEADER: The calibrated_occurrence_anchor set entirely omits Hand Fighting from Back, yet all 10 legends independently rate it the single most-attempted action from a locked seatbelt. The anchors also crown Shrimp (16) as leader. Panel treats the anchor set as underweighting invisible grip-fight work and does NOT defer to it.

SEALED_SITE_ROLE_MISREAD: Old site values put Hand Fighting at 7 (near-bottom) and Elbow Escape at 21 (top) — inverted from panel consensus. Confirmed as a role misread of the position; panel corrected and did not conform.

SUCCESS_NEQ_OCCURRENCE: Harness Escape to Half Guard has the highest listed success rate (55%) but modest occurrence (~8-9) because its success is conditional on already having broken the seatbelt; occurrence was kept honest and not inflated by efficacy.

HEAD_HEAVY_CONFIRMED: Distribution is head-heavy (hand fighting ~18-22 leads, hip-mechanic cluster mid, granby/tech-standup tail) rather than uniform smear — satisfies the statistician's anti-smear and the game designer's real-opponent tests.

moves.transition: Technical Stand Up to Single Leg

containers.frame_rationale: The single decisive gi/no-gi divergence is the collar. In the gi the harness opens a second finishing lane — the Bow and Arrow Choke — which is a genuine gi workhorse (~15-18% of attempts) and a hard 0 in no-gi because it is collar-dependent (logged as an availability ruling). That freed no-gi share does not smear across the tail; it flows straight back into the Rear Naked Choke (gi ~25-27 rises to no-gi ~31-34) plus small bumps to the collar-free variants — Short Choke, Rear Triangle, Crucifix, and the body-triangle upgrade (Harness to Body Lock) — which replace collar work as the secondary no-gi threats. Everything else (Back Control Maintenance ~18-21, Armbar, Kimura, Gift Wrap, Rolling Back Take) is frame-symmetric because it is grip-independent hand-fighting and control. The distribution is head-heavy in both frames: RNC + Maintenance are ~45% of all attempts, matching the control-first reality of the seatbelt.

availability_rulings.move: Bow and Arrow Choke from Harness
availability_rulings.reason: The bow-and-arrow requires a lapel/collar grip to generate the choking tension and the leg-driven angle. With no gi there is no collar to feed, so it is genuinely unavailable in no-gi competition (hard 0, not merely rare). The panel unanimously overrode the calibrated anchor of 2.

removal_candidates.reason: From an already-secured harness/seatbelt, a rolling back take is a re-take used only when the opponent is escaping and you scramble to re-establish the back — it is essentially never a first-choice attempt FROM the harness itself. Consistently the lowest-tier move (1-3) across all 10 legends in both frames. Not removed now, logged for review as a possible structural mismatch (it may belong on the escape/scramble side rather than as a harness-top attempt).

flags: Back Control Maintenance is the site's grossest miss: the SEALED old value was 2, but it is the position's second-most-common action (~18-21% of attempts). The calibrated distribution correctly lifts it ~10x — page rank and opponent AI change materially here.

SEALED old RNC value of 42 was inflated (double-counts finishing into attempting) and flat across frames, missing the collar fork; the panel lands RNC at ~26 gi / ~32 no-gi with an explicit gi/no-gi split.
SEALED old Bow and Arrow was 11 flat across both frames — misses the availability fork entirely (should be ~16 gi / 0 no-gi).
Bow and Arrow no-gi anchor was 2 in the pack; panel unanimously overrode to a hard 0 (collar unavailability, logged in availability_rulings).

moves.transition: Bow and Arrow Choke from Harness

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger, Marcelo, Danaher, Statistician) could not break the proposed distribution across 4 rounds. Sum coherence is exact (100 gi / 100 no-gi). Head mass is appropriate for a dominant control position: top-5 = 75% in both frames, RNC + Maintenance = 46 gi / 52 no-gi, matching the seatbelt's control-first-then-strangle reality. The one zero (Bow and Arrow Choke no-gi) has a bulletproof availability argument — the technique is defined by the lapel/collar feed plus leg-driven angle; no-gi has no collar, so it is genuinely unavailable, not merely rare (the no-gi analog is a different named strangle). The sole gi/no-gi divergences all trace to a single mechanism, the collar: Bow and Arrow (15 gi / 0 no-gi) frees mass that routes honestly into RNC (27 gi / 32 no-gi, bare neck climbs) plus small collar-free bumps (Short Choke, Triangle, Body Lock); every grip-independent move stays frame-symmetric. Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames (gi: RNC > Maintain > Bow&Arrow > Short Choke; no-gi: RNC > Maintain > Short Choke, Bow&Arrow drops out). The why_selected concern (zeroed Bow and Arrow no-gi) is validated, not a defect. The three flags describe corrections the panel already made correctly — the 10x Maintenance lift (old sealed value 2 was the gross error; ~19-20% for maintaining seatbelt/hooks while hand-fighting is if anything conservative), the RNC de-inflation + collar fork, and the Bow and Arrow availability fork. Softest number is Harness to Body Lock (highest dispersion 1.26/1.48) but its central value is mechanism-justified. Every proposed value sits within ~1-2 points of its panel mean.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split at Headquarters bottom is small and structurally motivated, not a smear. Re-guard is the workhorse in both frames but leans marginally no-gi (no grips to stall recovery, faster scramble re-entry). The two secondary recoveries mirror each other: Inversion leans gi (collar/sleeve grips anchor the spin-under and enable DLR/berimbolo re-entry, ~22 gi vs ~19 no-gi), while Shin-to-Shin leans no-gi (it is the gateway into ashi/leg-lock exchanges, ~23-24 no-gi vs ~22 gi). Sweep is frame-neutral and lowest. All four moves are legal and available in both rulesets, so no per-frame zeros are warranted.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency move here (~17-18) and lands top from a losing pinned position — panel keeps it as a real opportunistic reversal, not a removal, but it is the weakest attempt in this role and worth watching.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed old site values (Re-Guard 30, Sweep 25, Inversion 25, Shin-to-Shin 20) underweighted the central re-guard and overweighted sweep; calibrated panel shape (re-guard ~36-37, sweep ~17-18) is the correction and matches the occurrence anchors — panel did NOT conform.

containers.frame_rationale: The one structural gi/no-gi divergence in Headquarters/Top is Saddle Entry from Top, driven by heel-hook legality: in no-gi (ADCC/sub-only) HQ is a genuine fork where back-stepping into the saddle is a co-equal branch to the forward pass (~12-15 attempt share), whereas in IBJJF gi the heel hook is illegal, so the saddle collapses to a rare legal-ankle-lock/sweep option (~5-8) — non-zero, but a footnote. Every other move differs by only 1-2 points with a stated mechanism: gi grips (collar/sleeve/pant-cuff) make the knee cut and toreando complete at a slightly higher attempt share in the gi, while in no-gi skin friction and cleaner back-flow nudge the leg drag and body lock up and, critically, the extra saddle slice compresses all forward passes slightly (knee cut ~26 gi → ~22 nogi). Knee cut remains the workhorse king in both frames; the tail (Back Step, Body Lock, HQ Pass) is honest and head-heavy with no availability zeros, because every listed move is a legal, real passing option in both rulesets.

availability_rulings.reason: NON-ZERO but heavily reduced. The heel hook is illegal in IBJJF gi competition, so the saddle from HQ is not a finishing launchpad in the gi. It remains legally available for a straight ankle lock or as a sweep/off-balance entry, so it stays a rare, opportunistic option (~5-8) rather than a zero. The gi/no-gi divergence for this move is driven entirely by heel-hook legality.
Fully available and a genuine mainline. In ADCC/sub-only no-gi the saddle is a heel-hook launchpad off HQ, making it a co-equal branch to the forward pass (~12-15). No restriction applies.

containers.frame_rationale: Hindulotine/Bottom is a front-headlock pin whose engine is binary: finish the guillotine or sweep off the choke threat, with darce/anaconda/back-take as opportunistic neck-family conversions and guard recovery / sweep-to-mount as bail-outs. The frames are mirrored, not forked — R1 mean CV was only 0.098 — and the divergence is entirely mechanism-driven and modest. In the gi, collar friction and grip interference fight the finishing wrist, so every neck attack (Guillotine Choke, High Elbow Variation, High Elbow finish, Darce, Anaconda) is a few points LOWER, and that displaced volume flows into the sweeps and especially Guard Recovery (gi players bail to guard sooner when the finish stalls) and Sweep to Mount (completing the sweep pays better than a stalled gi choke). No-gi the slick, collar-free neck makes the finish cluster a few points HIGHER. There are no availability zeros — every move is legal and mechanically possible in both frames; nothing here is lapel/collar-dependent and there are no heel hooks.

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in both frames. Logged only to note the mechanism-driven frame gap: gi collar friction and grip interference fight the finishing wrist, so the pure-choke attempt share is lower in gi (~21) than no-gi (~25). No zeros anywhere in this position.

containers.frame_rationale: The single mechanical axis is the collar. In no-gi the front-headlock/guillotine game runs hottest — a slick, sweaty neck and no collar to frame the defense push the straight Guillotine Choke to the head of the distribution (~25) and make it the position's dominant attack. In the gi the collar gives the defender a real strangle-defense frame, so the top player attempts the straight guillotine less (~16-17) and instead (a) leans on the namesake Hindulotine squeeze as the primary gi finish (~20, higher than no-gi) and (b) bails to the back more readily via the two distinct back-routes (Back Take from Top + Front Headlock to Back). Every gi/no-gi divergence is collar-driven and directionally justified: Guillotine up no-gi, Hindulotine-from-Hindulotine and the back-take exits up (or flat-to-up) gi. No move is ruleset-illegal in either frame (no lapel/collar-only technique, no heel hooks), so there are zero availability zeros anywhere on this position.

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in the gi — this is a hand-to-hand strangle (no collar/lapel dependency). It is attempted LESS in the gi (collar gives the defender a framing/defense) but is never unavailable, so it carries a positive value in both frames, not a zero.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split here is behavioral, not legality-based — every one of the seven escapes is legal in both rulesets, so there are no availability zeros. In the gi the inside-sankaku finish is slower and grips let the trapped player post and cross-frame safely, so gi defense stays fundamental: frame-and-extract, hip escape, and (safely) technical stand-up dominate, while counter-attacking the opponent's legs is largely absent because the heel-race payoff is small and the instinct is not part of gi competition. In no-gi the saddle is more immediately dangerous and both heels are live, so the pragmatic top-level answer shifts toward counter leg attacks and counter-entangling into a 50-50 heel-hook race; standing up is trimmed no-gi because posting feeds the heel. Net divergence: Counter Leg Attack ~+6 no-gi (the single most-motivated fork), Technical Stand-up and the two guard-recovery frames a few points higher in the gi.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi divergence here is the sharpest legality split in the leg-lock corpus and is confined entirely to the two heel-hook nodes. Inside sankaku (honey hole) top exists in no-gi FOR the inside heel hook: the primary heel-hook node lands ~30-35% of all attempts and, combined with the secondary re-entry heel hook (~12), pushes over 40% of the no-gi distribution onto 'break the leg' — a mechanistically real, head-heavy peak. In the gi, IBJJF reap rules make the heel hook effectively illegal, so its mass does NOT vanish into a zero (sub-only/ADCC-gi rulesets keep it at a genuine 1-3, never 0) but instead redistributes onto the four LEGAL outlets: kneebar (~18-20, the gi lead), saddle transfer (~16-17), toe hold (~16), and back take (~12), with outside-ashi re-entry and honey-hole re-consolidation filling the tail. Grips/lapels are irrelevant here — this is leg-on-leg entanglement — so the ONLY driver of the gi/no-gi split is finish legality, which inverts the position's purpose from a finishing hub (no-gi) to a control-and-legal-finish hub (gi).

containers.frame_rationale: Inverted guard is a transitional funnel, and the gi/no-gi split here is mechanical, not stylistic. In the gi, the far-hip pant grip enables the rotation-to-the-back, so the Berimbolo Entry dominates gi attempts (~18-19) and its cloth-dependent sibling the Bolo Sweep holds up (~8); Reverse De La Riva Recovery is also grip-driven and slightly favored in the gi. Strip the cloth in no-gi and both the berimbolo (~10) and bolo sweep (~4) collapse hard, while the volume redistributes to cloth-independent leg entries and scrambles: Single Leg X Entry becomes the no-gi #1 (~15), Granby Roll to Guard and Rolling Back Take rise into the top cluster (~13/~12), and Reverse X-Guard Entry and Roll to Truck are modestly no-gi-favored (leg-meta + 10P scramble outlets). No move is genuinely unavailable in either ruleset — every divergence has a stated grip/meta/legality mechanism (IBJJF heel-hook rules further suppress the gi reverse-X payoff) — so there are no per-frame zeros and no availability rulings. The result is correctly head-heavy in the gi (single dominant berimbolo) and flatter but still ordered in no-gi (a leg-hunting scramble funnel with no spam move).

containers.frame_rationale: This is a pure passing role with no lapel/collar moves and no submissions, so every technique is legal in both frames and there are no availability zeros. The gi/no-gi split is meta-driven, not legality-driven. In the gi, grips reward weight and stalling, so the classical pressure family (Stack Pass, Pressure Pass, Smash) holds slightly more attempt-share and Roger legitimately keeps Stack at the top of his gi ballot. In no-gi, the absence of grips and the constant threat of the inverted player's leg entries push movement passing up: Leg Drag and Toreando gain a point or two, and Back Step rises meaningfully (7 gi -> 9 nogi consensus) as passers deny the bolo and stay clear of leg-lock entries. Leg Drag Pass leads both frames as the canonical anti-inversion pass — its no-gi edge (~18 vs ~16 gi) reflects unimpeded lateral hip travel.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is legal and mechanically available in both rulesets, so there are no per-frame zeros and no availability rulings. Lockdown Recovery and Electric Chair Transition lean no-gi because they are 10th-Planet friction constructs (double-paw lockdown, whizzer game) that the gi's slower, grip-heavy exchanges reward less — in the gi people default to plain guard recovery instead. Jailbreak to Turtle and Jailbreak to Back Take tick slightly up no-gi because the absence of a lapel makes scrambles faster and exposes the back more readily. Old School Sweep leans slightly gi because the lapel/underhook grip aids the elevation. Guard Recovery (the clear workhorse), Deep Half Entry, and the core escapes stay near-mirror across frames.

containers.frame_rationale: This is a passing/re-pinning position, so most moves mirror closely across gi and no-gi. The one mechanism-justified divergence is the front-headlock family: Darce Setup and Front Headlock to Back rise materially in no-gi (Darce roughly 6-8 gi to 10-13 no-gi) because when the bottom man turns into the escape he exposes a slick, ungripped neck - with no collar to fight and sweat aiding the closure, the darce and front-headlock-to-back become live weapons rather than footnotes. In the gi, collar/lapel grips give the turning defender a frame and dry friction resists the neck closure, so those attempts stay suppressed but nonzero. Passing mechanics (smash, leg weave, underhook, knee slice) run 1-2 points higher in the gi where grips aid the pass, while re-pinning gets a slight gi bump from friction; none of this crosses into a per-frame zero.

Near-duplicate of Knee Slice from Half in mechanism and same landing (side-control/top); the panel spreads attempts across both, which may be double-counting one passing action. Candidate for merge, not removal now.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site value for Smash Pass was 33 (roughly double the panel's ~15) - an uncalibrated spike that smeared all pressure-passing into one bucket; panel does not conform.

SANITY-DIFF: sealed values starved Knee Slide (3), North-South Recovery (1), and Reestablish Side Control (1); the panel's calibrated view treats Reestablish as a genuine common-tier re-pin (~10-12) - a deliberate correction, not a miss chased from the old numbers.

containers.frame_rationale: K-guard/bottom is a leg-entry vehicle whose distribution forks on ruleset in one dominant way: in no-gi it is a legs-first funnel where the 50-50 Entry (gi ~7 → no-gi ~16) and K-Guard to Single Leg X (gi ~11 → no-gi ~16) entries eat a large share, driven by the leg-lock meta and no-gi points/entanglement structure; in the gi it reverts to a sweep-and-back-take guard where grips make X-Guard Sweep and the eponymous K-Guard Sweep more attractive coming-up options, and players avoid settling in a neutral 50-50 (Roger holds gi 50-50 lowest at 5). Deep Half Entry sits slightly higher in gi (you can settle) than no-gi (you keep moving to the legs). No move is legality-locked to zero — every technique is a legal sweep/entry in both rulesets — so the only availability ruling is the meta-driven gi suppression of 50-50 Entry, which stays a genuine 1-8 rather than 0.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in gi but rarely chosen from K-guard (1-8 range, never 0): sitting into 50-50 is a no-gi points/leg-entry habit; gi players prefer to come up into X-guard or hit the K-guard sweep off grips rather than settle in a neutral 50-50.

removal_candidates.reason: Rarest exit from K-guard in both frames (gi ~5, nogi ~3). Panel views it as an inherited deep-half/lockdown sweep that is mechanically off-pattern for K-guard's inverted-hook posture — genuinely happens occasionally, so kept, but a candidate for future pruning.

Situational-to-rare (gi ~6, nogi ~4). A classic half-guard sweep bolted onto this pack; K-guard's real coming-up mechanic is X-guard/SLX, not the old-school underhook-and-come-up. Low value but non-zero.
Situational (gi ~6, nogi ~5). K-guard is not a hooks-in butterfly posture; this reads as a generic sweep imported from butterfly guard rather than a native K-guard attempt.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: SEALED site value for Deep Half Entry was 29 (gi/nogi) — a gross overweight. All 10 legends and the calibrated anchor (11) place it ~7-9; the 29 is legacy conflation of K-guard with deep-half guard and was NOT adopted.

SANITY-DIFF: SEALED site had K-Guard Sweep=2 and K-Guard to Single Leg X=1 — gross underweights of the position's own namesake exits. Panel correctly raises both into double digits (K-Guard Sweep gi ~13/nogi ~10; K-Guard to SLX gi ~11/nogi ~16), confirming the calibration direction.
Largest R1 disagreement was no-gi 50-50 Entry (spread 12-24) driven by Lachlan's 24 outlier; he genuinely updated down to 18, converging the panel to a ~14-18 no-gi band.

Deep Half Entry and Butterfly Hook Recovery lack calibrated_occurrence_anchor in the pack (Waiter Sweep, 50-50 Entry, Butterfly Hook Recovery, K-Guard Sweep, K-Guard to Single Leg X all missing anchors) — panel values are expert-derived for those.

All 11 moves are non-submission sweeps/entries, so no submission-floor or terminal-state concerns apply; distribution is head-heavy (top ~5 moves carry ~65%) with an honest low tail (Waiter/Old School/Butterfly Sweep).

containers.frame_rationale: K-Guard/Top diverges gi vs no-gi almost entirely on one axis: disengagement urgency. In no-gi the bottom K-guard player is a backside-50-50 / inside-heel-hook factory, so the Backstep (disengage before the leg is trapped) becomes the single most-attempted move (~19-21 no-gi vs ~14-16 gi) and the Guillotine Setup rises (~6-8 no-gi vs ~3-4 gi) off level-change neck exposure. In the gi, grips let the passer stay heavy and grind, so the conventional pressure passes (Knee Slice ~16, Smash ~13, Leg Drag ~14, Half Guard ~11, Underhook ~10) each hold 1-2 points more than no-gi and the distribution reads broader. No move is ruleset-unavailable here (the top player is passing, not attacking heels), so there are no legitimate zeros — only the two guillotine mechanism-divergences are logged.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in gi but rarer (gi ~3-4): no-gi off the K-guard level-change scramble the front-headlock/guillotine is more live due to sweaty neck exposure and no lapel needed. Kept at 3-4, not zeroed — 'rarely attempted' is 1-3+, never 0.
More available no-gi (~6-8): front-headlock chains off the K-guard scramble are a genuine no-gi option. Divergence from gi is a mechanism (neck access), not an availability zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Generic catch-all 'pass' that semantically overlaps the named passes (Knee Slice / Smash / Leg Drag / Half Guard / Underhook). Panel keeps it at ~10-11 for now but it is a redundant bucket with no distinct mechanism — candidate for folding into the specific passes.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site had Backstep from K-Guard at 3/3 — a gross underweight of what the entire panel unanimously calls THE answer to K-guard; calibration corrects to ~15 gi / ~20 nogi. Do not conform to the old value.
SANITY-DIFF: old site Knee Slice 28/28 and Half Guard Pass 18/18 were inflated (single-move hogging); panel lands head-heavy but healthier (~16/~11).
Pass K-Guard is a generic redundant bucket overlapping the named passes — logged as removal candidate, kept for now.
Backstep from K-Guard has no calibrated_occurrence_anchor yet it is the flagship move here — its landing zone is panel-driven, not anchor-driven; recommend adding an anchor.

containers.frame_rationale: The Kimura Trap bottom is really a dominant control seat whose premium output is the back — Kimura to Back Take leads in both frames, followed by a balanced sweep cluster (Old School, Kimura Sweep, Underhook from Half, Half Guard to Back Take). The gi/nogi fork is driven by tempo and grips, not legality: in the gi the sleeve/pant grips keep the deliberate Old School Sweep higher and create more stall-and-recover situations (Kimura Defense, Counter via Roll tilt slightly up, notably on Roger's fundamentalist read), while no-gi's sweaty, scramble-heavy pace pushes the Rolling Kimura, Half Guard to Back Take, and the 10th-Planet Lockdown/Electric Chair entries up. Lockdown and Electric Chair are the sharpest divergence — live no-gi staples but near-dead gi rarities (kept nonzero as availability rulings, since they are legal, just mechanically discouraged by the gi).

availability_rulings.reason: Legal in the gi but a genuine tempo/mechanics rarity — pant grips let top pass out of the lockdown and the deliberate gi pace works against the double-paw hook. Held at ~3-5 (rare, nonzero), not zeroed.
Legal in the gi (not a lapel/legality issue) but a 10th-Planet no-gi phenomenon; the gi tempo and grip framing make it near-dead, so ~2-4 rather than 0.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency tail in both frames (~3/3). It overlaps heavily with Kimura Counter via Roll as a failed-offense residual escape and is the least distinct attempt from this seat; flagged for possible fold, not removed now.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site value for Old School Sweep was 31/31 — a gross over-weight; panel unanimously lands it at ~15 gi / ~11-12 nogi, correcting the mistaken assumption that Old School (rather than Kimura to Back Take) is this seat's identity move.
SANITY-DIFF: sealed site under-weighted Kimura Sweep (10 vs panel ~14) and Underhook Sweep from Half (7 vs panel ~12); the sweep cluster was too flat in the old uncalibrated numbers.
SANITY-DIFF: sealed site used flat 6/6 for Electric Chair, missing the gi/nogi fork; panel forks it to ~3 gi / ~5-6 nogi.

Kimura Defense carried the widest cross-panel R1 spread (Lachlan 3-4 as failed-offense residual vs Roger/Craig/Gordon 7-8 as a recurring gi stall action); dissent is principled and retained rather than smeared to consensus.

High-success defensive moves (Kimura Defense 60%, Counter via Roll 55%, Rolling Kimura Escape 55%) are intentionally low-frequency: success rate is decoupled from attempt frequency per Lachlan's frequency-vs-prevalence point.

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-unavailable, so availability_rulings is empty and no per-frame zeros are warranted — every option (finish, back-take, mount pass, north-south, knee-on-belly, Americana, arm-triangle, reverse scarf, arm extraction) exists in both gi and no-gi. The gi/no-gi differences are magnitude, not availability, and all mechanism-justified: Kimura to Back Take is the single clean divergence, materially higher no-gi (~18-20 vs ~15 gi) because the sweaty, ungripped arm slides through the figure-four into the seatbelt/back rather than staying trapped for the finish; conversely Side Control to Mount and Knee on Belly run a hair higher in the gi where lapel/pant grips stabilize the pin and pin-pass, and the direct Kimura finish is marginally higher gi where the grip holds the shoulder lock longer to crank. North-South, Arm Triangle Setup and the tail moves are effectively frame-neutral.

removal_candidates.reason: A concession/re-consolidation bail (give up the trap, re-pass to half) rather than an offensive plan; lives at the bottom of every ballot (5-8). Real but the lowest-value line here — flagged for possible future pruning, not removed now.

containers.frame_rationale: Bottom knee-on-belly is the most ruleset-agnostic position on the board: the escape is one biomechanical motion (frame the knee, off-load it, hip escape, reguard) taught under several names, and it dominates in both gi and no-gi. The only material fork is Technical Stand-up — meaningfully higher in no-gi (~7-10) than gi (~4-6) because there is no collar/lapel to pin the bottom player down, so posting and wrestling up out of KOB is a live modern answer; in the gi grips hold you flat and standing is a lower-percentage choice. Secondary, minor divergences: Deep Half Entry leans marginally gi (grip-driven under-hooking of the leg), while Elbow/Hip Escape and Frame-and-Shrimp shave 1-2 points in no-gi as the escaping frames climb and stand-up absorbs share. No move is ruleset-illegal, so there are no per-frame zeros. Push-Knee-and-Reguard is the one genuine intra-panel disagreement — elevated on raw attempt frequency (the universal reflex) but downgraded by high-level players because it feeds the far-side armbar; it lands mid-tier (~9-13) with Mendes high and Gordon/Kade low.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal and available in the gi, only rarer — the top player's collar/lapel grips pin the bottom down, making standing a low-percentage attempt choice. Floored at ~4-5, never zero; not a ruleset unavailability.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely rare from KOB bottom (~5-6) — a diehard's / specialist's entry that most players never attempt from under the knee. Happens, so not zero, but a candidate for future pruning if the tail needs trimming.

removal_candidates.move: Turn to Turtle from Knee on Belly
removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically near-duplicate of 'Hip Escape to Turtle' — both surrender guard to reach turtle. Combined turtle-tail is small; this specific entry is a merge/removal candidate.

flags: Near-duplicate move names split the dominant escape family across synonyms: 'Frame and Shrimp to Guard', 'Frame and Shrimp from Knee on Belly', 'Elbow Escape to Guard', and 'Hip Escape to Guard' are the same one-motion escape wearing different labels — each looks modest individually while the family is dominant (~55-65% combined).
'Hip Escape to Turtle' and 'Turn to Turtle from Knee on Belly' are mechanically the same guard-surrendering move to turtle; their attempt-share is split across two names.

SANITY-DIFF: old sealed site values put Elbow Escape to Guard at 42 gi/nogi — a pre-calibration artifact where a single 'escape to guard' edge ate the entire escape share before the frame-shrimp family was split out. The panel deliberately redistributes across the family and does NOT conform to the 42.
Push Knee and Reguard is the only move with genuine (non-noise) intra-panel dissent driven by reference class (all-levels reflex frequency vs high-level armbar-aware avoidance).

containers.frame_rationale: Knee on Belly / Top is fundamentally a gi scoring-and-finishing position but only a transitional waypoint in no-gi, and that split is driven almost entirely by the two collar chokes. In the gi, Baseball Bat Choke and Cross Collar Choke together carry ~18-20 points of attempt share because the collar is exposed right under the driving knee and the position exists to make the opponent frame and defend, opening the collar and the far-side arm. In no-gi both chokes are collar-dependent: Cross Collar Choke is mechanically impossible (hard 0, availability ruling) and Baseball Bat Choke collapses to a fringe 1-2 (kept as 'rarely attempted' rather than logged unavailable, since a no-collar neck/shoulder grip attempt is physically possible even if it almost never lands). Those ~18 gi points drain in no-gi onto the moves that stay live: KOB to Mount rises to the clear modal action (~21-22) because you can't stall on a collar and migrate straight to mount, Far Side Armbar and KOB to Side Control each pick up a few points, and Kimura roughly doubles (6-7 gi to 11-12 no-gi) because it is the one grip-agnostic submission that attacks the opponent's framing arm without needing a collar. Back Take and the direct/belly-down armbars shift only slightly. The net effect: a choke-heavy, more terminal gi distribution versus a mount-and-arm-attack, transit-heavy no-gi distribution.

availability_rulings.move: Cross Collar Choke from Knee on Belly
availability_rulings.reason: Mechanically requires the opponent's collar/lapel to cross-grip and choke. No gi = no collar = the technique cannot be attempted. Genuine ruleset unavailability, scored 0 unanimously; the calibration anchor's 3% is treated as noise.

removal_candidates.move: Belly Down Armbar from Knee on Belly
removal_candidates.reason: Consistent tail move (3-6 both frames) across all 10 legends. It is a real but rare finishing variant that is more naturally reached from mount/S-mount than directly from KOB; it never approaches workhorse volume from this position. Log only — do not remove.

flags: Baseball Bat Choke from Knee on Belly no-gi micro-split (1 vs 2): panel treated it as 'rarely attempted' (fringe no-collar variant) rather than availability-0. A defensible case exists to score it 0 as a fundamentally two-lapel choke; kept at 1-2 to honor the 'rarely != never' rule. Watch for a future availability ruling if usage data shows a true zero.

SANITY-DIFF vs SEALED old site values: old values had both collar chokes ALIVE in no-gi (11-12) and gi==nogi flat everywhere — this is the exact calibration error being corrected; panel holds its no-gi zeros. Old values also badly underweighted KOB to Side Control (8) which the panel unanimously reads as a workhorse (14-17); the raise is strongly justified, not conformed away.

Roger holds cross collar (11 gi) and mount (21 gi) above the field per his gi-fundamentalist read; Mendes holds direct armbar (10/11) high on a grip-driven near-arm read; Kade/Lachlan hold back take slightly high no-gi. These are authentic held dissents, not un-updated anchoring.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger/Danaher/Gordon + Statistician) failed to break the proposed distribution. Sums are clean (gi 100, nogi 100). The two why_selected zeros survive hostile review: Cross Collar Choke nogi=0 is a bulletproof ruleset-availability zero (no lapel, cross-collar is mechanically impossible; anchor's 3% correctly dismissed as noise), and Baseball Bat Choke nogi=0 is a defensible round-to-zero of panel_mean 1.1 (dispersion 0.27, anchor 2) with the 'rarely!=never' concern properly flagged for future usage data. Every gi/nogi divergence carries an explicit mechanism: the ~18 collar-dependent gi points drain in no-gi onto grip-agnostic actions — KOB-to-Mount rises to the clear modal (18->22, you can't stall on a collar), Kimura roughly doubles (7->12, the one grip-agnostic framing-arm attack), Side Control and Far Side Armbar each pick up a few. Head-mass is coherent: gi top-5=65 with both collar chokes alive matches a choke-heavy gi position; nogi top-5=77 is higher only because two moves are mathematically forced to zero, not a modeling artifact. Transit/submit split (gi 48/52, nogi 57/43) correctly encodes KOB as a scoring-and-finishing position in the gi versus a transitional waypoint in no-gi. Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames (Mount > Side Control > Far Side Armbar leading; far-side armbar correctly above direct armbar). The KOB-to-Side-Control raise (prior 8 -> 15/17) is a justified correction of a genuine old-value underweight, not anchoring — the panel unanimously reads it as a workhorse re-consolidation and the raise is confirmed, not conformed away. Roger's authentic gi dissent (cross collar 11, mount 21) is within noise of the panel means (9.02, 18.63) and does not clear the bar for override. No move has misallocated mass; all 10 accepted.

containers.frame_rationale: This is an attacker-dominant leg-entanglement page: the person 'bottom' in Kneebar Control is the one who has isolated the leg and is finishing, so attempt mass concentrates on the Kneebar Finish in both frames (~18-24 gi, ~15-20 no-gi). The single decisive gi/no-gi divergence is the secondary weapon when the kneebar stalls or the leg straightens. No-gi: the rotation goes to the HEEL HOOK (14-18), the whole strategic point of the position. Gi: the heel hook is illegal and functionally dead (0-2), so that rotational share is absorbed by the TOE HOLD (elevated to ~10-12 as the legal rotational substitute) and the ANKLE LOCK (elevated to ~12-14 as the safe gi finish). Toe hold is thus gi >= no-gi and ankle lock is clearly gi > no-gi - both are reasoned legality-driven substitutions, not smear. The escapes (Straighten Leg Defense, Turn and Extract, Reversal, Ashi Garami Escape) and re-entries (Inside Ashi, Backside 50-50, SLX, X-Guard) form an honest non-zero minority tail; no-gi shifts entry mass slightly up (better leg entries) while gi shifts escape mass slightly up.

availability_rulings.reason: Heel hooks are IBJJF-illegal at all belts and banned in the overwhelming majority of gi competition, so the kneebar-to-heel-hook rotation is essentially never a real gi attempt. Roger and Danaher hold a hard 0; others log 1-2 to account for heel-hook-legal gi sub-only/ADCC-gi rulesets. Not a hard universal 0 because such rulesets exist - it is floored at 0-2, with those attempts flowing to the toe hold and ankle lock in gi.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely rare from a committed kneebar-control breaking position - the panel floors it at 2-5. A leg-entanglement finish position does not naturally revert to an X-guard sweep; it reads as a tail artifact of the shared leg-family transition list rather than a real attempt from here. Log only, do not remove.

Also a tail entry (2-6 across the panel). Re-entering single-leg-X from an established kneebar control is uncommon; more a leg-family default than a position-specific attempt. Log only, do not remove.

flags: MIXED-ROLE PAGE: kneebar-control__bottom carries both attacker finishes (Kneebar Finish, Heel Hook, Ankle Lock, Toe Hold, ashi re-entries) AND defender escapes (Ashi Garami Escape, Straighten Leg Kneebar Defense, Turn and Extract, Reversal) on the same ballot. The panel treated the role as attacker-dominant (the bottom player has secured kneebar control and is finishing), which matches the leg-entanglement convention where 'bottom' is the underneath leg-attacker. If the site intends 'bottom' here to mean the person whose leg is being attacked (pure defender), the finish-heavy weighting is inverted - worth a role-definition check.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Danaher + The Statistician) pressure-tested the container over 5 rounds and found it fundamentally sound: both frames sum to exactly 100, and every gi/no-gi divergence carries a stated, non-arbitrary mechanism (heel-hook fork = pure IBJJF legality; ankle-lock/toe-hold gi>=nogi = legal-substitute absorption of the dead heel-hook rotation; entries nogi>=gi = faster no-gi leg entries; escapes gi>nogi = more gi grips to frame/hold with). The why_selected concern (heel-hook gi zero) survives: with heel hooks illegal at all belts in the dominant gi rulesets, a floored 0 is defensible; Danaher pushed for a floored 1 (panel mean 1.13) but conceded it is a 1-point cosmetic difference the frame rationale already owns as 'functionally dead (0-2)'. Musumeci's ankle-vs-toe reorder was withdrawn: the panel means (ankle 12.54, toe 11.31) genuinely rank ankle above toe and the gap is inside dispersion noise. Trim it to 8 and restore those 2 points to the Kneebar Finish (19->21), which returns the headline to its own panel mean of 21.02 -- strictly MORE faithful to the panel than the proposed value -- and reinstates a clear #1. No-gi left untouched (less defensive grip-mass, headline already tied with the heel-hook fork; both frames stay at 100). Not re_elicit: <2% of mass moved and the correction is grounded in the panel's own means.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is legal in both gi and no-gi at the levels this position models, so all divergences are distributional, not availability. The gi differs in two mechanically real ways: (1) gi grips and pant/sleeve friction let the top player stall the defender's rotation and hold the kneebar bite longer, so maintenance and the ankle-lock catch tilt gi-heavy while the raw kneebar finish attempt and the toe-hold switch tilt no-gi-heavy (slick hips make the finish freer and the leg-triangle defense more exploitable via toe hold); (2) the gi carries a points incentive, so bailing a stalled kneebar to knee on belly for a scoring top position is a genuinely more attractive gi behavior — the only move where gi > no-gi for a non-friction reason. The 50-50 and ashi re-entry resets edge slightly no-gi because leg-entanglement chaining is a no-gi staple.

removal_candidates.reason: From a locked kneebar control almost nobody abandons the leg to chase a scoring top position; it survives only on the gi points incentive and beginner behavior. Genuinely rare (panel landed ~5-7 gi / ~4-6 nogi) but not zero — do not remove, log.

flags: Ankle Lock Finish is labeled is_submission:false in the pack yet is mechanically a terminal-ish finishing attack (falls out of kneebar over-rotation); treated as a finishing switch, not a positional transition.

Kneebar to 50-50 Transition and Kneebar to Ashi Garami overlap heavily — both are 'reset the entanglement' moves; panel kept them near-equal with Ashi a hair higher no-gi. Redundancy flagged, not removal-worthy.

Position has three finishing lines (Kneebar, Toe Hold, Ankle Lock) plus maintenance; this is correct for a leg-entanglement finish position and plays as a relentless leg-hunter, but worth noting the head-heavy submission concentration.

Old sealed site values smeared the three secondary attacks flat (Ankle 14 / Toe Hold 14 / KOB 13) and were gi==nogi; panel differentiated them by mechanism and did not conform. KOB was the largest sealed overweight (13 -> ~6); 50-50/Ashi were the sealed underweight (5 -> ~8-9).

containers.frame_rationale: This position is categorically gi-only (pack family: guard_gi). Every one of the 11 moves is a named lapel mechanic — the guard is built by feeding a cloth lapel through/around the opponent, and even the 'universal' technique names (Lapel Triangle, Lapel Omoplata, Lapel Elevator) are explicitly the lapel-fed versions, not generic no-gi analogs. Therefore the gi frame is fully live and head-heavy — Worm Guard Entry (~18-20) is the workhorse funnel, followed by a Sweep-to-Back / Elevator / De La Riva cluster (~10-13) and a Squid/Lasso/Spider/Omoplata/Triangle mid-tier (~5-9), tailing to Ringworm (~5) and Piranha (~3). The no-gi frame is UNAVAILABLE for the entire node: without a lapel the position does not exist, so all 11 moves are zero and logged as ruleset-unavailability rulings. The R1 fork (a partial-survivor camp had put DLR 30-40, triangle/omoplata/elevator 15-20 no-gi, with Danaher at DLR=100) collapsed cleanly downward once the panel accepted that the move STRINGS are all lapel-specific — the partial-survivors were really describing a different position (standalone DLR/triangle in no-gi), not an attempt from lapel guard bottom. This is the cleanest possible gi/no-gi divergence: not a probability shift but a categorical availability boundary.

availability_rulings.reason: Worm guard is entered by feeding the opponent's lapel through the legs — categorically impossible without a gi lapel. Unavailable in no-gi.
Squid guard is a lapel-wrap variant; no lapel exists in no-gi, so the entry cannot occur.
Ringworm is a worm-guard lapel derivative; cloth-dependent, unavailable no-gi.
The sweep is driven by the lapel grip/wrap to unbalance and take the back; without cloth the named mechanic does not exist.
Lapel-fed omoplata setup; the shoulder-lock entry as authored requires the lapel. A generic omoplata is a different node (closed/rubber guard).
Lapel-fed triangle; the strangle setup as named uses the lapel to trap/angle. Generic no-gi triangles belong to other positions.

containers.frame_rationale: Lapel Guard/Top is fundamentally a gi position (the position is defined by the opponent weaving a jacket lapel into worm/squid/ringworm control), so the gi frame is the native one and all nine moves are live there, led by the Lapel-Clear-to-Toreando workhorse plus the boring-but-common Distance-Creation reset. verify.rationale: Lapel Guard/Top is a gi-native passing position; gi is the observed frame and no-gi is a defensible conditional projection of which passing mechanics survive when the lapel structure vanishes. ADVERSARIAL FINDINGS: (1) The two hard no-gi zeros the why_selected flags — Lapel Clear to Toreando and Backstep Around Worm Guard — are bulletproof availability calls, not probability calls: the entire defining action is manipulating a lapel/worm structure that does not exist without a jacket, so the move literally cannot instantiate. Accepted. (2) The contested Leg Drag (kept nogi 10) vs Leg Extraction (dropped to nogi 2) asymmetry survived attack: a leg drag is generic-core-plus-cloth-addon (survives strongly no-gi), while a leg-extraction 'from lapel wrap' is cloth-core (only residual footwork survives). The 10/2 split has a real mechanism; the large dispersions (6.02, 7.86) confirm the panel disagreed but the majority resolution is defensible, so both are accepted. (3) The gi column is fully coach-recognizable: Lapel Clear to Toreando as #1 is exactly the canonical answer to lapel guard, Backstep correctly demoted from the old overweight 16 to 10, Distance Reset correctly promoted to a genuine workhorse 12; top-5 gi share (63) is appropriately head-heavy. Accepted wholesale. (4) THE ONE DEFECT: the no-gi top two INVERT the panel's own elicited means. Raw means had Knee Slice 24.15 > Distance 21.77, but proposed_final flipped them to Distance 24 > Knee Slice 21 — an unjustified inversion. On a lapel-DEPENDENT guard, removing the lapel collapses the bottom player's retention, so the top player should ATTACK (knee cut) more than RESET, not less. The elicited means already said this. Bounded fix: Knee Slice nogi 21->23, Distance nogi 24->22, restoring Knee Slice > Distance while keeping both near their means and preserving the head-heavy no-gi shape and the sum at 100. Both frames sum to 100 after correction. Nowhere near re_elicit; a single ±2 swap on two cells is the whole correction.

containers.frame_rationale: Lasso guard is a sleeve-cuff wrap structure: the bottom player threads the shin behind the opponent's arm and pins the sleeve cuff. In the gi this is a coherent, head-heavy guard whose two workhorses are the Lasso Sweep (~14) and the Omoplata from Lasso (~13), backed by a middle band of Triangle, Sickle, Omoplata Sweep and De La Riva. In no-gi the defining cuff grip does not exist, so the position degenerates into a grip-agnostic overhook / trapped-arm guard: every lasso-GRIP-dependent move (Lasso Sweep, Russian Leg Lasso, Inverted Lasso) drops to the rare floor, while the freed attempt-mass concentrates on the mechanics that survive without a sleeve — the Triangle becomes the clear no-gi #1 (~16-17), and Sickle, Hook Sweep, De La Riva and X-Guard conversions rise. Critically, the panel distinguished grip-availability from technique-availability: the Omoplata FINISH mechanic survives no-gi even though its lasso ENTRY does not, so Omoplata from Lasso is reduced (~7-9) rather than zeroed. No move earned a hard availability-0 because each retains at least a degraded grip-agnostic analog; the purists' zeros were logged as no-gi removal_candidates instead.

containers.frame_rationale: Lasso Guard/Top is fundamentally a gi position, so gi is the reference frame and no-gi is a degraded projection of it. In the gi the lasso is a real, sticky arm-prison built on a sleeve grip and a foot threaded through the passer's bent arm; the top game therefore leads with arm-liberation (generic Lasso Guard Pass), backed by a pressure shoulder (knee slice, smash, stack, leg weave) that only lands cleanly after the wrap is compromised, plus sleeve-dependent specialties (leg weave, spider handling, the lasso backstep) that all lean on the jacket. No-gi the guard loses its teeth because there is no sleeve to anchor the lasso - the arm simply slides out - so two things happen together: the sleeve-dependent lasso variants (Leg Weave, Spider Guard Pass, Lasso Backstep, Lasso Stack) compress, and the untethered speed/pressure passes (Toreando, Body Lock) rise sharply because nothing binds the passer's arm to the bottom leg. No move is illegal in either ruleset, so there are no per-frame zeros; every divergence is availability-of-effectiveness (grip suppression), not legality.

Take the sleeve away and roughly 37% of attempts (the two lasso-named moves) become structurally impossible — logged as availability zeros, not smeared. The two why_selected concerns are cleared: (1) the top-40 L1 shift from the SEALED site values is CORRECT, not a defect — the site had the two namesake lasso moves grotesquely underweighted (2/2 and 1/1) and Berimbolo Entry overweighted (44/44); the panel rightly refused to conform to the site, putting the sleeve-mechanic moves at the gi head (22, 18) and burying berimbolo to 7/5. (2) The Σ|Δ|=86 divergence is fully mechanism-justified: 40 gi points sit on two sleeve-only moves (Inverted Lasso Sweep, Inverted-to-standard-Lasso) that structurally cannot exist without a sleeve, so no-gi redistributes that counterfactual mass onto the leg/DLR/triangle conversion tree (Single Leg X 27, Triangle 18, DLR 15, Sickle 12). Both nogi zeros carry bulletproof move-specific sleeve-dependency rulings (not lazy blanket zeros — the panel explicitly corrected Craig's blanket-nogi-zero error so only the lasso moves vanish, the position survives). Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames: gi = lasso sweep > revert-lasso > omoplata > triangle > tail; nogi = SLX > triangle > omoplata > DLR > sickle. Head-mass gi 72% / nogi 89% top-5 is appropriate — nogi is compressed because two moves are zeroed. Omoplata surviving gi 15 → nogi 17 correctly reflects a sleeve-independent shoulder lock. containers.frame_rationale: Inverted lasso guard is a gi-native, sleeve-defined position: the lasso wraps and inverts on the sleeve, so the passer's whole game is built around that cloth grip. In the gi the head of the distribution is Arm Extraction and Pass (~16-18) — strip the sleeve first — followed by a mid-band of stacking, pressure, knee-slice (kept modest gi because slicing a live lasso donates the omoplata) and smash passes, with lasso-specific responses (Lasso Guard Pass, Pass Inverted Lasso Guard, Stack from Inverted Lasso) and the cartwheel filling the tail. No-gi the position barely occurs because there is no sleeve to hold the inversion, but nothing here is illegal, so no availability zeros: attempt% is conditional on already being in the position, so the no-gi rarity redistributes shares rather than zeroing them. Given that conditioning, no-gi shifts to be MORE head-heavy on Arm Extraction (~22-27, share concentration when there is no cloth for fancier answers), Knee Slice rises (no sleeve-omoplata punishment), Pressure/Smash rise slightly (grip-free, sweat aids the passer), and the sleeve-dependent lasso-specific moves collapse to the floor (2-6).

containers.frame_rationale: The Russian Leg Lasso is a sleeve-anchored deep-lasso guard, so the gi and no-gi attempt distributions genuinely fork. In the gi the position is a sweep-omoplata dilemma: its namesake Russian Lasso Sweep is the workhorse (~20) and the lasso omoplata (sweep + finish) plus the DLR exit carry real mass, because all three depend on the sleeve/lapel anchor that lets the outside leg thread and hold the lassoed arm. Remove the cloth and that anchor evaporates — the three lasso-named lines (Russian Lasso Sweep, Russian Lasso to De La Riva, and the sleeve-dependent portion of the lasso omoplata) collapse to low-single-digit shadows that survive only as overhook/wrist-ring analogs (the panel rejected hard zeros because the overhook mechanic genuinely persists, so these are 'rare' 2-8, not 'unavailable' 0). The mass they lose no-gi transfers to the frame-independent overhook chain: Overhook Sweep becomes the clear no-gi crown (~24), with Triangle Setup, Omoplata Sweep and Back Take all rising as the sweaty overhook game opens angles. Net: gi is namesake-sweep-led and head-heavy on lasso lines; no-gi is overhook-sweep-led with the lasso lines demoted to the tail.

containers.frame_rationale: The decisive framing point is mechanism: the 'Russian' leg lasso is an ARM-WRAP variant (the attacker's leg wraps the far arm), not the classical sleeve-driven lasso. That means the position and every lasso-named move survives no-gi, correcting the R1 zeros from Craig (whole no-gi column) and Marcelo (the two lasso-named moves), which assumed a sleeve grip. Because the wrap is reinforced by sleeve control in the gi, the strip is a heavier grip fight and is attempted slightly MORE in gi; no-gi the wrap is slipperier so stripping is nearly automatic and resolves fast (fewer discrete attempts, hence lower attempt-frequency, not higher). After the strip clears, no-gi favors movement/pace passing — Toreando, Leg Drag, Pressure and Knee Slice all tick up a point or two because there are no grips to respect. The generic Lasso Guard Pass is the one move meaningfully gi-weighted (it targets the sleeve-lasso configuration). Net: Strip is the workhorse in both frames (~17 gi / ~14 nogi), Knee Slice the top actual pass, deltas modest throughout because an arm wrap keeps the two rulesets close.

The strip resolves faster no-gi (slipperier wrap), so attempt-frequency is modestly lower than gi but firmly non-zero — it remains the workhorse.

containers.frame_rationale: Leg Drag Control/Bottom is a losing, being-passed position: the outside leg is already dragged across the body and the clock is the back-take, so the distribution is head-heavy on damage-control reguarding (Half Guard Recovery and Frame and Shrimp are the two workhorses at ~15-18 in both frames, with the gi framing recoveries marginally higher as gi frames hold better). The gi differs from no-gi in two mechanically-justified places: (1) Leg Recovery to De La Riva leans gi (~10 gi vs ~6 nogi) because the collar-sleeve/lapel grips let a disciplined bottom slow the pass and re-establish the DLR outside hook as a trained counter, whereas no-gi that grip disappears; (2) Inside Position Recovery leans no-gi (~14-15 nogi vs ~11 gi) because without lapels to stall, the athletic answer is to spin into inside position/butterfly to deny the back. Minor no-gi > gi leans on Roll to Turtle and Granby (less grip friction on the rolls) are the only other divergences. No move is ruleset-illegal here, so there are no availability zeros — every recovery is available in both frames; the only availability ruling is the no-gi down-weighting (not zeroing) of DLR recovery.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is legal in both rulesets — the leg drag is a positional pass with no collar-only or heel-hook-only branches — so there are no availability zeros; all gi/no-gi divergence is meta-driven, not rules-driven. The spine (pass-to-side + back-take, ~42 combined) is stable across frames, but its balance tilts: in the gi the pass-to-side is the single most concentrated move because collar/sleeve grips let you nail the side-control pin (Roger/Bravo push it to 25), while in no-gi the exposed hip and frictionless seatbelt tilt volume toward the back-take (Danaher/Gordon/Marcelo/Mendes at 22-23). The cleanest fork is Leg Drag to Inside Ashi: a genuine no-gi-only bump (nogi 7-9) because the leg-lock backstep re-entry is a no-gi cultural staple, collapsing to 3-5 in the gi where the pants hide the leg and the passing culture favors consolidation. The darce family (Setup + Choke) also skews slightly no-gi off the live front-headlock, and North-South / Technical Mount edge up no-gi where there are no grips to stall the run-around.

removal_candidates.reason: A direct submission finish from the leg-drag control point itself is a low-frequency terminal branch — the darce almost always routes through the Darce Setup control node first rather than finishing straight from the drag. Kept in the tail (3 gi / 4-5 nogi) but flagged as the closest thing to a never-happens direct-finish here.
