containers.frame_rationale: Leg Entanglement / Bottom is a defender-first role, so both frames are dominated by leg extraction (~23-24 gi, ~20 nogi) and guard recovery (~20 gi, ~16 nogi) — together roughly 44% gi and 37% nogi of all attempts. The gi/nogi split is driven by two mechanisms. First, ruleset legality: reaping and heel hooks are banned in mainstream gi competition, so the Inside Heel Hook from Ushiro counter collapses from ~8 in no-gi to ~1 in the gi, and the whole counter-leg-attack line (Counter Leg Attack 8 gi vs 13 nogi) is a no-gi reflex; conversely the legal straight-ankle counter (Ankle Lock Finish) rises in the gi (~9) versus no-gi (~7) because it is the one permitted counter-finish. Second, cloth friction: gi grips slow the attacker's re-entries and help the defender clear the leg, so the gi tilts even harder toward extraction/recovery and away from slippery inversions and counter-entries, which run slightly hotter in no-gi (Inversion 10 gi / 11 nogi). No move earns a hard 0 in either frame — every option stays at least 1, with the gi heel-hook suppression logged as a legality ruling rather than an availability zero.

availability_rulings.reason: Heel hooks (and the reaping required to enter this counter) are banned under IBJJF and most mainstream gi rulesets, so this line is near-absent in gi competition. Not scored 0 because sub-only/ADCC-style gi formats do permit it and it is attempted in gi training; held at 1 (rarely attempted, not unavailable).

containers.frame_rationale: The rulesets fork almost entirely at the finishing mechanism, not the control. The head of the no-gi distribution is the Outside Heel Hook (~19-20, the single dominant attractor because its ~41% success pays and it is fully legal), with the Saddle Entry (~13) as its gateway to the inside heel hook. In the gi both of those collapse: the outside heel hook is IBJJF-illegal (floored to 1-2) and the saddle loses its payoff (~3-5), so their combined ~30 no-gi points redistribute into the legal gi finishing/control set - the straight Ankle Lock becomes the gi workhorse (~16-18), the inside-Ashi and Outside-Ashi re-entries run higher (people cycle entries more when finishes are lower-percentage), and bailing out via Leg Extraction Pass / Guard Pass is a more frequent, legitimate gi choice. Net: no-gi is a head-heavy heel-hook-hunting distribution; gi is a flatter ankle-lock-and-pass distribution with no illegal-but-dominant single move.

containers.frame_rationale: Leg Hook / bottom is a compromised, transitional half guard, so both frames are recovery-dominant (Half Guard Recovery is the unanimous modal move at ~16/17, and the three reguard actions clear 40% of attempts). The gi/no-gi divergences are all grip-mechanism driven: gi grips make the Hip Escape to a full grip-based guard slightly more attractive (gi ~13-15 vs nogi ~12-13) and support framing (Frame and Shrimp gi>=nogi), while the absence of pant grips in no-gi pushes attempts toward the physical Underhook Sweep (nogi 11-12 vs gi 10), the Shin/knee shield frame (nogi 13-14 vs gi 12), Old School, and Butterfly Hook Recovery (butterfly being the no-gi open-guard currency, nogi 9 vs gi 7). No move is ruleset-unavailable here — no lapel/collar or gi-illegal leglock actions on this list — so there are zero availability zeros; the tail (Counter/Sweep from Leg Hook) is rare but real at the 4-5 floor.

containers.frame_rationale: This is a passing hub, not a distinct pin: the top player's mandate from a leg-hook entanglement is to clear the leg and consolidate a pass, so seven of eight moves land at side-control/top or half-guard/top and the distribution is head-heavy on the knee slice in both frames. Gi and no-gi differ only at the margins and always with a mechanism: (1) Back Step Pass rises in no-gi because back-stepping a leg entanglement is the leg-lock-entry door — attempted more often no-gi even though it is the riskier choice — and falls in gi (Roger especially) where pant grips make the direct pass faster; (2) Smash and Pressure Pass tick up slightly in gi where pant/hip grips let the top player stay heavy and pin while clearing the leg (Roger's stylistic bias, held against a modern-gi minority led by Mendes); (3) Leg Weave nudges up fractionally no-gi where skin/friction threading pins the near leg. Every move is legal and available in both rulesets, so there are no availability zeros. The only live dissent is the two unanchored named advances (Leg Hook to Half Guard / to Side Control), which Danaher and Gordon rate as genuine safe consolidations (~9-10) and Marcelo/Mendes/Craig rate as semi-redundant repositions (~6-8).

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a grip/position transition with no ruleset-illegal component, so all six are available in both gi and no-gi and there are no per-frame zeros. In no-gi, Leg Knot bottom is a heel-hook race: a leg-lock-literate population counter-entangles to win inside position rather than concede, so 'Counter-entangle to 50-50 Guard' (the biggest fork, ~14 gi to ~19 nogi) and 'Reverse the entanglement to Outside Ashi' (~11 gi to ~15 nogi) both rise. containers.frame_rationale: This position diverges more sharply by ruleset than almost anything in the corpus, and the divergence is entirely rules-driven. In no-gi the Leg Knot/saddle exists to deliver the inside heel hook, so the frame is head-heavy on Heel Hook from Saddle (~30, Kade 32) with passing/bailing options forming a modest, honestly-ordered tail (backstep ~19-20 > pressure ~18 > extraction ~17, because no-gi you would rather keep the heel threat than give the leg back for free). In the gi the heel hook is banned by the dominant IBJJF ruleset, so the whole position converts into a passing/points game: Pressure Pass and Leg Extraction become the two near-equal workhorses (~28-30 each), Backstep is a controlled third exit (~24), and the Toe Hold INVERTS to sit slightly ABOVE its no-gi value (~15-16 gi vs ~14 no-gi) because it is the legal finish substituting for the forbidden heel. Gi-heel survives only as a floored, ruleset-suppressed 2 (fringe sub-only gi keeps it off a true zero). Net: no-gi = heel-hook shark with a pass-bail tail; gi = relentless passer with an occasional toe hold.

availability_rulings.reason: Heel hooks are banned in the dominant gi ruleset (IBJJF, illegal at every belt), but remain LEGAL in fringe sub-only gi events (EBI-style gi brackets, some ADCC-adjacent gi). Therefore this is NOT a true availability-0: the panel floors it at 2 as a ruleset-SUPPRESSED 'rarely attempted' move. Downstream should not 'correct' this 2 upward as an underestimate — it is intentionally low because the mainstream gi ruleset forbids it.

Toe Hold INVERTS by frame (gi ~15-16 > no-gi ~14): the legal gi finish is relatively more attempted than in no-gi where the heel dominates finishes. Intentional, mechanism-backed.

containers.frame_rationale: Leg Weave/Top is a low-divergence position: every move on the list is a pressure/pass mechanic available in BOTH gi and no-gi, so there are no ruleset-forced zeros. The gi/no-gi differences are small and mechanism-driven — gi friction and pant/collar grips make the bottom player's frame-recovery slower, which slightly raises commitment to the canonical weave finish in the gi; no-gi's faster shrimping and slicker mobility nudge the mobile re-passes (long step, backstep, leg drag, over-under) up 1-2 points because a stalled weave means the opponent recovers, prompting a spin-off rather than a grind. The dominant structural fact, not a ruleset fact, is that this list carries the same weave-completion action under three labels (Leg Weave Pass / Complete Leg Weave Pass / Leg Weave Pass Completion) plus two backstep labels — the panel consolidated the completion mass onto the canonical 'Leg Weave Pass' rather than smearing it, matching the calibrated anchor of ~26 and correcting the old site's role-misread (it had Knee Slice at 32 and the weave finish at only 15).

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in both rulesets — a friction/pressure pass mechanic with no grip dependency; no zero warranted.

That freed berimbolo share does not vanish: it migrates into the grip-independent guard-recovery bucket (Granby Roll, Rolling to Guard, Turtle to Guard) which each tick up 1-2 points in no-gi, and the primary Matrix Back Take also cools slightly no-gi (~16 vs ~19 gi) because the gi's grips make the finish more attemptable. Everything else — arm drag, escape-to-turtle, counter roll, sweep — is essentially frame-neutral because it relies on body positioning rather than cloth.

The one decisive divergence, Berimbolo Entry gi 9 vs nogi 3, has a bulletproof cloth-lever mechanism (pack success 40.1% gi vs 18.6% nogi) and its shed ~6 no-gi points are conserved into the grip-independent guard-recovery bucket (Granby +4, Turtle +2, ArmDrag +2, Rolling +1, Counter +1) while Matrix Back Take sheds 4 no-gi (gi grips aid the finish) — the mass bookkeeping balances. containers.frame_rationale: This is the TOP player imposing on a turtling/inverting (Matrix/berimbolo) opponent, so the ruleset split is driven by grips and friction. In the GI, pant and collar grips make positional passing stick: knee slice (pant-grip king, ~15-16) and crossface (~13-14) lead, back-take and turtle-flatten fill the head, and the arm-in front-headlock trilogy (darce/guillotine/anaconda) is suppressed because friction and collar snags make the neck harder to isolate cleanly. In NO-GI, remove the gi and the front-headlock family roughly doubles (darce/guillotine ~7-9, anaconda ~4-5) as sweat and the absence of collars reward the neck dive, the back-take ticks up (~14-15, since grips can't shuck you off and the meta funnels to the back), and knee slice/crossface each shed a couple points into that shift. No move is ruleset-illegal here — there are no lapel/collar-only techniques and no heel hooks — so there are zero availability-forced zeros in either frame.

The two double-label flags (S-Mount Transition / High Mount to S Mount both -> s-mount/top; Mounted Triangle / Triangle from Mount both -> mounted-triangle/top) are content-graph edge redundancies, NOT distribution errors -- the split volumes are two doors to the same room and each remains a real graph edge the game rolls against, so the combined s-mount migration (~19-21%) and mounted-triangle (~11-13%) are defensible. The panel's corrections to the legacy sealed values (old Mount to Armbar=30 catch-all, under-weighted s-mount/gift-wrap/armbar-from-HM) are more truthful than the priors. Divergences are all grip/lapel/elevation mechanisms: Lockdown Recovery leans no-gi (no lapel to kill the elevation the lockdown needs; 10th-planet-native) and is the single largest gi/nogi gap. Deep Half Entry leans faintly gi (grips help burrow under the posted leg). Arm Extraction to Turtle leans faintly no-gi (less grip friction on the turn). The classic Upa and Bridge-and-Roll are DEGRADED in both frames by the modified base, sitting below the shrimp-family escapes.

containers.frame_rationale: The single structural gi/no-gi difference here is the Cross Collar Choke: it is a lapel-and-collar submission that is a central, workhorse-adjacent gi threat from modified mount (the chest angle sets it up cleanly, ~13-16 gi) but has no true no-gi equivalent, so it collapses to a rare facsimile (0-2) no-gi and is logged as an availability ruling. That freed no-gi weight does not smear uniformly — it flows to the position's mechanically-native lines: the gift-wrap-to-back and the direct back take (both climb notably no-gi, matching the modern no-gi mount meta), plus modest bumps to the arm attacks (kimura, armbar). Everything else moves in the same direction in both frames — Consolidate Mount leads the count as the re-tightening workhorse (slightly higher no-gi where the opponent is harder to pin without grips), the armbar is the top pure submission, and the tail (Americana, Mounted Triangle, S-Mount) stays low and stable across rulesets.

Weight redistributes to gift wrap, back take, kimura, and armbar in the no-gi frame.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger/Danaher/Gordon + Statistician) tried to break the distribution across 4 rounds and failed to land a correction. (1) The why_selected zero — Cross Collar Choke nogi=0 — has a bulletproof availability ruling: it is a gi collar-feed mechanic with no true no-gi equivalent, the panel split is documented (Danaher/Gordon/Marcelo score genuine 0, rest a rare facsimile), and the facsimile lives under a different node. Legitimacy zero, not a data gap. (2) Every gi/no-gi divergence carries a stated mechanism: Consolidate 18->20 (harder to pin no-gi without grips), Back Take 12->15 and Gift Wrap 11->14 (absorb freed cross-collar mass into the native no-gi back-take engine), and the uniform +1 elsewhere is just proportional redistribution of the ~13 freed points. (3) Rank order is coach-recognizable for a MODIFIED (destabilized) mount: re-consolidate leads, armbar is top pure submission, Americana/Mounted Triangle correctly sit in the tail — the panel rightly refused the old site's inflated Americana(13) and Mount-to-Armbar(19) and under-weighted Consolidate(12). (4) Head-mass: GI top-5=67%, NOGI top-5=74% — appropriately head-heavy for a control pin with a dominant re-secure action plus a back-take line, not degenerate. Both frames sum to exactly 100. Proposed integers are faithful roundings of the panel means. No move survives a hostile challenge as mis-allocated.

containers.frame_rationale: The mounted crucifix pins BOTH of the bottom player's arms (one trapped between the top player's legs, the other pinned by their arm/head), so the escaping player has no free hands to establish grips or frames. Every listed move is grip-agnostic bridging or shrimping mechanics, which is why gi and no-gi attempt distributions are essentially identical and no move is ruleset-unavailable (no zeros, no availability rulings). The only defensible divergence is a marginal +1 attempt-frequency for Explosive Bridge to Turtle (and lightly the other scramble/turtle-giveback lines) in no-gi, because sweat degrades the top player's crucifix retention and makes bailing to a back-exposed turtle scramble slightly more common; the gi's stickier crucifix control (collar/sleeve reinforcement) is a near-offsetting nudge the other way, so net divergence stays within noise. Attempt frequency, not success rate, drives these numbers: bridging variants are attempted constantly and succeed rarely, but the reflex mass belongs to whatever recovers the trapped arm back to ordinary mount-bottom, which is why the plain Hip Escape from Mounted Crucifix leads.

removal_candidates.reason: Unanimous panel judgment: with both arms compromised under the mounted crucifix an arm-drag to back control is mechanically near-impossible. Its 65% pack success rate is a data artifact, not a real attempted line. Kept at floor (~3) as a rarity, flagged for possible future removal — not removed now.

flags: Arm Drag Sweep carries a 65% pack success_rate that is inconsistent with its near-zero real attempt frequency from this position (both arms compromised) — success-rate data artifact flagged for review; kept at floor (~3), not zeroed.

SANITY-DIFF: site value for Bridge Escape from Mounted Crucifix was 1 (spurious near-zero for a legitimate distinct half-guard-recovery bridge); panel restores it to ~11-12.

containers.frame_rationale: This position barely forks between gi and no-gi because its mechanics are grip-agnostic: control comes from the legs trapping both of the opponent's arms, and the strangles here are naked-style (arm-around-the-neck), not collar-driven, so the gi confers no special choking option. The two real divergences are (1) the Neck Crank, which is IBJJF-illegal and therefore suppressed to a near-floor 1-2 in the gi versus a small ~3 in no-gi, logged as an availability ruling; and (2) the Rear Naked Choke / naked strangle, which entries slightly faster in no-gi (~10) than in the gi (~7) because gi friction and grip-fighting slow the choking-arm insertion, while the trapped-arm armbar remains the dominant attack in both frames. Roger's gi ballot additionally leans a touch more on the free-arm armbar (a gi-fundamentalist read), but the overall shape — armbar family #1, S-mount / gift-wrap consolidation #2 tier, back-takes and strangle in the middle, crank and the circular Back-Control-to-Crucifix at the floor — is essentially mirrored across rulesets.

availability_rulings.reason: Spinal locks and neck cranks are prohibited under IBJJF gi rules, so gi attempts are suppressed to a near-floor 1-2 (borderline can-opener pressure only). Not zeroed because a crank can incidentally arise from the crucifix strangle attempt, but it is effectively off the table as a deliberate attack in the gi.

Legal in most no-gi/ADCC rulesets, so it holds a small positive weight (~3). Still rare because most practitioners attack the exposed arm or convert to the back rather than commit to a crank from here.

removal_candidates.reason: Near-circular: from the mounted crucifix you are already ON the trapped-arm attack, so 'going to crucifix/top' is essentially staying put / re-entering the same control. Panel consensus 2-3, and the old site value of 10 is a gross over-weight. Genuine attempts from THIS position are marginal.

Net divergence is within noise; frames are effectively mirrored.

containers.frame_rationale: Mounted triangle is a purely mechanical bodylock/leg-triangle position with no collar, lapel, or heel-hook dependency, so gi and no-gi are near-identical (r1_mean_cv 0.089) and every panelist balloted them within 1-2 points. The only defensible divergences, each with a stated mechanism, are tiny: a slight gi edge on the two armbar entries ('Armbar on Free Arm', 'Triangle to Armbar') because sleeve grips isolate the free arm before extension (Mendes, Marcelo, Gordon, Mikey), a slight gi edge on 'Mounted Triangle Squeeze' because gi posture/hand-fighting slows the finish and buys more squeezing time (Roger), and a slight no-gi edge on 'Belly Down Armbar' and back-take traffic because sweat and faster scrambles favor rotational finishes and reactive back exposure (Gordon, Marcelo, Kade). No move is ruleset-unavailable, so there are zero availability-zeros.

The systematic nudge: gi friction makes the controlled armbar finish and shoulder-line submissions (kimura/americana) slightly more holdable, so the armbar family and those submissions tick up ~1 point in the gi; no-gi sweat aids the swim to the back, so the scramble exits (Gift Wrap to Back, Back Take, and to a lesser degree Mounted Crucifix Entry / Mounted Triangle) tick up ~1-2 points in no-gi. All per-move gi/no-gi differences are within 2 points and each has a stated friction-vs-sweat mechanism.

containers.frame_rationale: Technical mount bottom is a grip-agnostic escape position: the top has stepped a leg over the head and threatens the back, so the entire bottom game is a race to recover the hip and elbow to the mat before the back is taken. None of the eight moves is a lapel/collar or leg-lock technique, so no move is ruleset-unavailable and there are no forced zeros. Gi and no-gi are therefore mirrored to within ~1 point: the only honest divergences are second-order — no-gi's lower cloth friction lets the top slide to the back marginally faster, so no-gi shifts a hair away from full-guard recovery (hip escape -1) and toward the back-turn scramble (+1); gi affords slightly more hip-escape control (Roger's +1 gi). The head stays balanced (elbow ~18 ≥ hip ~17, not a single-move spike), with a middle band (half-guard recovery, shrimp, upa) and an honest tail (bridges ~10, back-turn ~7 as the recognized error line).

availability_rulings.reason: Grip-agnostic hip/elbow recovery; fully available in both frames.
Grip-agnostic hip/elbow recovery; fully available in both frames.
Legal and mechanically available; kept nonzero (situational scramble/error line), not unavailable — no forced zero warranted.

flags: Site's SEALED Elbow Escape=40 is a gross over-weight (single-move spam spike) that starved Hip Escape (13) and the bridge/back-turn tail; panel corrected to a balanced head (~18) and did not conform.

Upa Escape and Bridge and Roll both target closed-guard/top and are both compromised by the stepped leg; kept distinct but low-common, not workhorse.

containers.frame_rationale: Technical mount is a body-position pin whose control is grip-agnostic, so gi and no-gi land nearly mirrored. The intent in both frames is identical: the opponent turned to their side to escape mount and this is the back-harvesting station, so Back Take plus Technical Mount to Back Control dominate the distribution regardless of ruleset. The only meaningful divergences are minor: Gift Wrap Control ticks up 1-2 points in no-gi (a clean wrist-and-neck trap that doesn't need a sleeve/collar to secure, and in the gi you'd sometimes prefer a collar route instead), and the two arm-attacks (Armbar, Americana) get a marginal gi lean from sleeve/collar grips aiding isolation — none large enough to fork the distribution. No move is unavailable in either frame, so there are no per-frame zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely low-frequency from technical mount — the arm is often already framing away and the angle is awkward — but it is a real occasional attempt (5-8%), not a candidate for actual removal; logged only as the tail scrap the panel flagged as near-vestigial.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: the sealed current-site values are a gross intent/role misread — they set Armbar at 48% (making technical mount an armbar-machine) while collapsing Technical Mount to Back Control to 5% and every other transition to 4-7%. This contradicts the unanimous panel mechanism that technical mount exists to harvest the back. The panel did NOT conform; it re-weights the position head-heavy on the two back-take routes (~36 combined). Old file needs replacement, not blending.

Back Take and Technical Mount to Back Control overlap heavily in intent (both are back-harvest paths); the panel deliberately split the ~36% back-harvest pie between them rather than double-counting, which is why neither individually exceeds ~20 despite being the clear purpose of the position.

High success rate (Armbar 55%, Consolidate 58%) does not translate to highest attempt frequency here — occurrence is driven by positional intent (the back), so the finishes sit mid-pack in attempts despite strong finish odds.

containers.frame_rationale: North-South bottom is a pin-escape state whose behavior is grip-agnostic: the top player controls your head and shoulders, and the sound answers (the dedicated North-South Escape and the belly-down turn to turtle) are the same motor patterns in gi and no-gi. Divergences are therefore small and directional rather than categorical. Turn-to-turtle and Technical Stand-up tick up 1-3 points no-gi because wrestling-up culture is stronger and there are no pants to anchor you flat; Granby Roll rises ~2 points no-gi because there is no lapel to trap the inverted roll and mat friction aids the spin; the frame/hip-escape family gets at most a negligible gi edge (grips can aid frame retention). No move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame, so there are no per-frame zeros and no availability rulings.

removal_candidates.reason: Panel near-unanimous that a straight bridge-and-roll is mechanically almost absent from flat under a stacked head/shoulder control — you cannot bridge into someone posted over your head. Held low (~6-7) rather than removed; it survives only against a loose top player.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site under-weighted North-South Escape (site 13 vs panel ~18, the position's signature answer) and Explosive Bridge to Guard Recovery (site 3 vs panel ~9-10), and over-weighted Bridge and Roll (site 12 vs panel ~6-7, a near-dead move here). Panel did not conform.

Correlated cluster: Elbow Escape / Hip Escape / Frame and Shrimp / Explosive Bridge to Guard Recovery are near-synonymous frame-to-guard recoveries; held level to avoid uniform smearing, but they collectively risk double-counting one behavior.
North-South Escape and Bridge and Turn to Turtle share an overlapping spin-out motor pattern; panel kept both high but resisted maxing both to avoid double-counting the single dominant behavior.

containers.frame_rationale: The single true frame divergence here is the North-South Choke: gi lands ~10-11 while no-gi lands ~17-18, an honest near-doubling. Mechanism — in the gi, collar friction resists the sliding chin-choke and the collar simultaneously offers competing chokes that steal attempts, whereas no-gi the neck is slippery, the arm slides skin-on-skin into the pocket, and the Marcelo-lineage choke is the headline finish. Secondary, smaller divergences all favor the gi and are point/grip-driven: Side Control to Mount, Knee on Belly, and Side Control to North-South tick up in the gi because gi scoring rewards the mount/KOB spins and the collar aids the pin-cycle, so gi north-south plays more positional. Everything grip-agnostic — the kimura (far-arm gauntlet), armbar, arm triangle, reverse mount, and back-take — stays roughly frame-flat, with a marginal no-gi edge on the kimura and back-take (no sleeve/collar to hide the arm or jam the seatbelt). No move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame, so there are no zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Vaguely-defined niche re-orientation; the panel's smallest, softest number (gi ~4 / nogi ~5). It happens rarely as a spin off north-south but is not a distinct high-frequency attempt — flag for possible consolidation, not removed now.

Gordon: 'a white-belt fantasy.' A genuine tail move (gi ~4-5 / nogi ~4) that does occur at lower levels but is almost never a serious expert attempt from north-south, where the far-arm capture becomes a kimura, not an americana. Logged, not removed.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site value for 'Armbar from North-South' (11/11) is a gross overweight — no legend placed it above 9 and consensus is ~6; the calibrated panel corrects it down.

SANITY-DIFF: sealed site value for 'North-South Choke' (21/21) was frame-flat and uncalibrated — it ignored the well-established gi-suppression/no-gi-doubling of the choke; panel splits it ~11 gi / ~18 nogi.

SANITY-DIFF: sealed site values underweighted two genuinely central pin-cycle turns — 'Back Take from Top' (5/5, panel ~9-10) and 'Side Control to North-South' (6/6, panel ~11-12); kept honest at panel levels, not conformed down.

Head-heavy distribution confirmed by Statistician: top-2 (Kimura + NS Choke) carry ~37-38% no-gi; gi head is flatter (Kimura leads, choke drops, transitions rise), reflecting a more positional gi game — no uniform smear.
'North-South Choke' and 'Americana from North-South' have lands_at:null in the pack (submissions terminating at game-over) — expected for finish moves, not a data error.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split here is driven by grip friction and dwell time. In the gi, lapel and sleeve grips let the controller fold the opponent and hold the shoulder lock, so the offensive lines land better and stick longer: the Omoplata Sweep peaks highest, and the sticky lines (Rolling Omoplata finish, Closed Guard to Omoplata re-entry, Triangle Setup) sit at or above their no-gi values. In no-gi there is no lapel to pin the fold, so the arm slips and the opponent spins, rolls, or cartwheels out — pushing the escape tail (Roll Forward, Cartwheel, and slightly Stack) higher no-gi and trimming the sweep a touch. The Omoplata to Back is roughly even with a faint no-gi lean because scrambles favor the back-take. Gordon is the lone principled dissenter on the sweep, reading it as a no-gi sweep/back-take vehicle (nogi >= gi) rather than a gi product; the panel nets to a small gi edge because more voices plus the grip mechanism favor gi. No move is ruleset-illegal, so there are no per-frame zeros.

availability_rulings.reason: Available both frames; gi lapel/sleeve grips mechanically aid the fold-and-come-up so it is faintly higher in gi. No zero.
Fully available no-gi as a sweep-vehicle; slightly lower than gi for most panelists because there is no grip to hold the fold. No zero.
The finish is available both frames; gi it is hunted slightly more because the control sticks longer. No zero.
Available no-gi but attempted a hair less as people prioritize the sweep/back-take. No zero.

containers.frame_rationale: Open guard bottom is the single sharpest gi/no-gi fork in the batch, and the fork is structural, not stylistic. In the gi, open guard is a grip economy: roughly a third of all attempts are grip-driven entries - collar-sleeve, De La Riva, double-sleeve, and the collar drag - because acquiring cloth grips IS the game before any sweep or submission is threatened. Those four grip-dependent moves collapse the instant the gi comes off: collar-sleeve, double-sleeve, and collar drag go to a hard, availability-logged zero (no collar, no sleeves), and the De La Riva entry survives only as a reduced leg-hook game (5-ish, not zero, because the DLR hook itself needs no cloth). The mass those cloth moves shed does not smear - it concentrates head-heavily into the three no-gi workhorses: Butterfly Sweep roughly doubles (7 -> 14), Arm Drag to Back roughly doubles (6 -> 12), and Technical Stand Up nearly triples (4 -> 12) because modern no-gi open guard is a wrestle-up game, not a footsie game. Success rates barely differ across frames, but attempt frequency forks hard: the gi rewards patient grip entries, no-gi rewards elevation and standing back up.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci gi-precision, Giles frequency-vs-success rigor, Roger gi-fundamentalist, plus The Statistician) attacked all five vectors and the distribution held. Sums are exactly 100/100. The three nogi zeros (Collar Sleeve, Double Sleeve, Collar Drag) are bulletproof availability zeros, not rare-move zeros: each is definitionally a hand-on-cloth grip that cannot exist without a gi, and the panel correctly kept 'Open Guard to De La Riva' at 5 nogi because the DLR hook is cloth-free — a mechanistically consistent razor. The gi/no-gi fork is accounted for, not smeared: ~30 points of nogi mass freed by the dying cloth moves lands head-heavily on Butterfly (7->16), Arm Drag (6->13), TSU (4->14) and Feet-on-Hips (6->10), and the ledger balances. Head-mass is appropriate: gi top-5 45% (light, but open guard is the sport's most diffuse position), nogi top-5 60% (properly head-heavy). Rank order reads correctly to a coach in both frames. The single value the panel poked — TSU nogi 14 — carries the container's highest dispersion (1.82), but it sits exactly on its panel_mean (13.64), and the only motivation to trim it to 12 was to reverse a cosmetic Arm-Drag-vs-TSU rank gap of 1 point that is deep inside both moves' overlapping dispersion bands. The Statistician showed that adjusting a mean-anchored high-dispersion cell forces off-mean re-homing of the 2 freed points elsewhere, INCREASING total deviation-from-panel-mean to fix within-noise cosmetics; Giles and Musumeci withdrew the adjustment on that basis. No move survives challenge as needing correction.

containers.frame_rationale: Divergences here are meta-driven, not legality-driven: every listed move is a passing mechanic legal in both gi and no-gi, so there are no true zeros. The gi concentrates attempts on the Toreando (~19) because pant grips make it a cheap, high-volume initiation even at its low 27% gi success, and it chains directly into the Leg Drag; the gi also slightly lifts stacking/pressure passes (Double Under, Stack) since grips let you hold and grind. No-gi, the vanishing grips transfer that share outward: Float Passing roughly doubles (~5 gi to ~9 no-gi, Danaher highest) because you ride hips over sweaty legs instead of gripping them, Long Step and X Pass rise as movement answers, and Knee Slice edges up to become the highest-frequency no-gi pass. Double Unders falls no-gi for lack of a stack. The shape is deliberately head-heavy — Toreando + Knee Slice own ~34 combined — correcting the old flat, uncalibrated site distribution (many 8s, Toreando underweighted at 12).

containers.frame_rationale: Overhook Control from the bottom is a sweep-and-back engine in both rulesets, so the two twin overhook sweeps (Overhook Sweep, Overhook Control Sweep) lead every ballot regardless of frame. The gi/no-gi split is narrow and mechanism-driven: Arm Drag to Back rises in no-gi (+2-3) because the exposed far arm and underhook take you straight to the back where the underhook is king, while grips slow the drag in the gi; Closed Guard to Omoplata rises in the gi (+2-4) because sleeve/collar friction traps the shoulder that a sweaty no-gi shoulder slips out of; Triangle Setup and Old School Sweep lean marginally gi for the same grip-friction reason. No move is ruleset-illegal here (no lapel/collar-only or leg-lock-only techniques), so there are no availability zeros.

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-unavailable — every technique (kimura, darce, anaconda, snap-down, two-on-one, crab ride, crucifix, pass, side-mount) is legal and executable in both gi and no-gi, so there are no zeros and no availability rulings. All gi/no-gi divergence is a finish-ability shift, not a legality one. In no-gi the arm-in front-headlock strangles are live and slippery (no collar/lapel to post on, sweat aids the slide), so the darce (~12 gi → ~15 nogi), anaconda (~8 → ~11), snap-down chain, and wrestling-paced crab-ride all lift no-gi. In the gi those same strangles are easier to stall, so attempts migrate to the kimura (stickier figure-four grip, ~16-17 gi vs ~14-15 nogi) and to the coming-around pass / side-control grind (the 'no finish available' outlet, gi-leaning). The kimura leads both frames; the darce is the clear #2 and co-leads no-gi.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Roger Gracie, The Statistician) attacked the L1-shift that inverted the sealed legacy distribution (old Smash 27 / Break 7 / Side-to-Mount 14). The ONE mechanism error is rank-order within the pass bucket: Over-Under Pass — the textbook on-theme answer to a captured arm (you go WITH the underhook and pass to that side) — was ranked dead last among the five passes, below Smash Pass (which smashes toward the framing arm and is mechanically harder here). Correction: rebalance Over-Under up and Smash down by 2 points, moving Over-Under at/above Smash. This stays inside panel dispersion, preserves the 69-point aggregate pass mass, fabricates no divergence (Over-Under keeps its native +1 no-gi tilt), and touches only 2 of 7 moves. containers.frame_rationale: Piranha guard is a gi-only lapel construct: the position's identity is the practitioner feeding their own lapel under the opponent's leg to build a leash, so in the gi the attempt mass concentrates on the three cloth-dependent moves - the signature Piranha Guard Sweep (head, ~20-24), the Piranha to Worm Guard feed (~14-18) and the Collar Drag (~11) - with the Berimbolo, Triangle, Omoplata and De La Riva forming a mid cluster and the minor sweeps a tail. Strip the gi and those three lapel/collar moves become hard zeros (logged as availability rulings), freeing roughly 40-45 points that redistribute onto gripless seated-open-guard offense: Arm Drag to Back becomes the clear no-gi head (~24-30), Triangle the strong #2 (~20-22), then a differentiated Omoplata/De La Riva/Pendulum secondary, with the Berimbolo shrinking gripless (loses its DLR/lapel grip). So gi and no-gi are two genuinely different opponents - a lapel-sweep specialist versus an arm-drag/triangle seated scrambler - rather than a rescaled copy of one distribution.

availability_rulings.reason: The signature sweep's control mechanism is the practitioner's own lapel fed under and around the opponent's leg (the leash). With no lapel there is no piranha leash, so the named move cannot exist no-gi; its sweeping motion, if attempted gripless, degenerates into an arm-drag/butterfly sweep counted elsewhere.
Worm guard is itself a lapel guard; the transfer feeds the opponent's leg into your lapel wrap. No gi means no worm guard to transfer into, so this is a hard zero no-gi.
A collar drag grips the opponent's collar (gi-only). No-gi the analogous action is the arm drag, which is scored separately, so the collar drag itself is unavailable no-gi.

SEALED site values were grossly mis-ranked: the namesake Piranha Guard Sweep was at 5 and Piranha to Worm Guard at 3 (near-bottom) while Pendulum Sweep sat at 21 as the top move - a role misread the panel corrected by promoting the signature sweep to the head and dropping Pendulum to the tail. Old values were also uniform gi==nogi, ignoring the three gi-only moves.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Giles, Roger + Statistician) failed to break the distribution across 6 rounds. Both frames sum to 100. The two why_selected concerns survive hostile review: (1) the zeroed Collar Drag no-gi is a legitimate grip-dependency zero (collar literally needs cloth) with the arm-drag analog scored separately as 'Arm Drag to Back' - no lost mass, no double-count; all three no-gi zeros (Piranha Sweep, Worm feed, Collar Drag) rest on own-lapel/worm-lapel/opponent-collar dependencies, the right kind of zero. (2) The Sigma|Delta|=104 divergence is fully mechanism-justified: it is not a rescaled copy but two genuinely different opponents - a gi lapel-sweep specialist (Piranha Sweep 22 > Worm feed 16 > Collar drag 11) versus a no-gi arm-drag/triangle seated scrambler (Arm Drag 29 > Triangle 23). The Arm Drag 7->29 (+22) and Triangle 9->23 (+14) swings are the largest but the cleanest: arm drag explicitly absorbs the zeroed collar drag's role, and no-gi's share inflation is the arithmetic consequence of 3 zeroed moves concentrating the remaining 7. GI top-5 share 66 is a healthy specialist decision tree (clear signature + real 8-9pt mid cluster), not a degenerate spike; no-gi top-5 share 88 is forced by having only 7 live moves. Rank orders match a coach's mental model in both frames, correctly reversing the documented old-site role misread (Piranha Sweep was mis-ranked 5, Pendulum wrongly the head at 21). Every proposed_final equals its panel mean rounded to nearest int with no renormalization thumb on the scale. Softest numbers (GI Piranha Sweep 22 slightly hot, no-gi Triangle 23 rides small-menu inflation) are both panel-mean-backed and within tolerance - correcting them would mean redoing the panel, not correcting a colleague. Missing no-gi leglock offense is a fixed-candidate-set limitation, not a panel error.

containers.frame_rationale: Piranha guard is a fundamentally gi-only position: the bottom player creates the guard by feeding their own lapel around the passer's leg/back, so the whole position cannot form in no-gi. This drives the single largest gi/no-gi divergence. In the GI, the load-bearing lapel connection re-steers the passer's hips and compromises every pass, so the professional sequence is strip-the-lapel-first — 'Strip Lapel from Piranha' is the single most-attempted action (~26-30) even though its success rate is only middling (a prerequisite, not a finisher). Cloth grips also slow speed passes, so the Toreando is comparatively low in the gi. In NO-GI the position is a phantom that degrades to a generic seated/open-guard passing spread: 'Strip Lapel' is a hard 0 (availability), and its ~28 points redistribute across the real named passes, which also run faster without cloth to grip — so Toreando, Knee Slice and Leg Drag all rise and become the head of the no-gi distribution, and the no-gi numbers should be read as nominal rather than empirical.

availability_rulings.reason: Genuine ruleset unavailability. Piranha guard is built on the bottom player feeding their own lapel; no lapel exists in no-gi, so the lapel-strip cannot be performed. Hard 0, unanimous across all 10 legends in R1 and final.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a sweep, recovery, or scramble that is fully legal in both rulesets, so there are no hard per-frame zeros - all divergences are meta/mechanism-driven, not availability. Gi grips (pants, belt, sleeve) make the commitment moves cleaner and stickier: Deep Half Entry and, to a lesser degree, Old School Sweep and Underhook Sweep rate slightly higher in the gi because grips let you hold the dive-under and finish the elevation before the top man slides free. No-gi is frictionless and pace-heavy, so the underhook scramble dominates: Half Guard to Back Take rises no-gi (the frontheadlock/underhook race off an overcommitted pass), Deep Half drops no-gi (a sweaty opponent slides out of the deep-half hold), and Lockdown Recovery ticks up no-gi as its native 10th-Planet home. Across both frames the position is head-heavy and identical in shape - the two literal recovery moves, Recover Full Guard and Knee Shield from Quarter Guard, are the workhorses (~18-20 and ~17-18) because quarter guard bottom is a survival way-station where upgrading the entanglement precedes any offense.

verify.rationale: Unanimous accept after 4 adversarial rounds. Both frames sum to 100; every proposed_final tracks its panel_mean within honest rounding; top-5 share (gi 69, no-gi 68) is appropriate head-mass for a recovery-dominated survival way-station. The why_selected concern (large L1 shift from sealed old values: gi 86 / nogi 82) is fully justified by the disclosed SANITY-DIFF: the old site was role-inverted, starving the two namesake recovery workhorses (Recover Full Guard, Knee Shield from Quarter Guard) and inflating rare sweeps (Old School, Underhook, Electric Chair). The panel's rebuild puts the recovery pair (19/19 and 18/17) correctly on top, which any half-guard coach recognizes as the real decision tree from quarter guard bottom. No zeros exist, so no availability burden is triggered; all divergences are small (max 3 pts) and each has a stated mechanism (gi grips stick Deep Half; no-gi frictionless pace lifts Half Guard to Back Take and Lockdown Recovery). Adversarial probes that failed to break anything: (a) the knee-shield establish(18)/retain(11) split survived as two genuinely distinct skills with a believable establish>retain ratio; (b) the generic 'Sweep from Quarter Guard' catch-all is a disclosed, conservative absorber that keeps the named sweeps from being over-credited; (c) the only genuine inconsistency found is narrative-only — the frame_rationale calls Underhook Sweep slightly gi-favored while the panel mean is marginally no-gi-favored, but the proposed_final flattens it to 8/8, so no integer is wrong. Correcting a colleague panel, not redoing it: nothing meets the bar for adjustment.

containers.frame_rationale: Quarter guard top is a pass caught at ~80% completion, so both frames are head-heavy on completing actions (knee slice, generic complete-pass, knee-through) which together carry ~50%. No move here is ruleset-unavailable, so there are no availability zeros — every gi/nogi gap is an effectiveness/frequency shift, not legality. The single largest divergence is Darce Setup (gi ~4, nogi ~9-10, Kade riding to 15 no-gi): no-gi the bottom man's desperation underhook dig exposes the neck with no grip friction, making the front-headlock/darce a live main line; in the gi that same dig is slower and the passer just knee-cuts through, so the darce nearly vanishes. Secondary gi lean: knee slice and complete-pass edge slightly higher in the gi because collar/pant grips help pin the far hip during the cut and let the passer 'walk through' on fundamentals (Roger/Mendes push this hardest). Underhook Pass and Kimura tick up marginally no-gi (live underhook battle, no sleeve hiding the posted arm). Knee-through vs complete-pass is the main non-frame disagreement (Kade/Gordon ~14-15 vs Marcelo/Mikey ~10-12) resolved on double-count grounds toward the low-teens.

containers.frame_rationale: Reverse mount is a transitional, unstable pin where the top player faces the bottom player's legs, so the bottom has no collar, lapel, or sleeve to grip from underneath — every escape is a grip-agnostic hip/frame mechanic. That collapses the usual gi/nogi divergence: the whole panel runs the two frames essentially mirrored, with only a one-point nogi lift on scramble-dependent moves (Sit Through to Guard, occasionally Hip Escape / Bridge and Roll) where sweat and pace let the bottom spin out slightly more readily. No move is legality-gated in either ruleset, so there are no availability zeros. The distribution is genuinely head-heavy on the two shrimp workhorses (Hip Escape, Elbow Escape), with the four commons (Frame and Shrimp, Escape Reverse Mount, Sit Through, Bridge and Roll) splitting the middle and Bridge from Reverse Mount the lone situational tail.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-attempted move; bridging under a leg-facing top to turtle is near-desperation. Panel keeps it as a genuine situational fallback (~9-11), not a removal, but it is the weakest candidate here.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site values badly overweighted 'Bridge and Roll' (22 vs panel ~10) and underweighted the generic 'Escape Reverse Mount' (3 vs panel ~14), and over-concentrated 'Elbow Escape' (28) at the expense of the co-dominant 'Hip Escape' (17); panel did not conform — the calibrated two-workhorse head-heavy shape is better justified.

'Escape Reverse Mount' carries the highest success_rate (50%) in the pack but is a generic catch-all label; its attempt share is a common (~14), not a workhorse — success rate must not be read as attempt frequency here.

containers.frame_rationale: Reverse Mount/Top is a transient waypoint whose mechanics do not hinge on grips, so gi and no-gi are nearly identical (r1 mean CV 0.04, the tightest kind of position in the corpus). All three moves — forward conversion to true mount, the side-control retreat, and the leg-trapped belly-down armbar — are fully legal and available in both rulesets, so there are no availability zeros. The only mechanism-justified divergence is the belly-down armbar: no-gi the sweaty arm slides through more easily and the 10th Planet school hunts it (Bravo forks 28 gi / 30 nogi), while in the gi the sleeve offers a mild countervailing trap for the arm (Mikey) plus more bottom-bridge friction that occasionally routes attempts into the side-control settle instead of a completed spin (Mendes shades one point gi→side-control). These small opposite-sign effects roughly cancel, so the panel runs gi≈nogi with only single-point forks on the tail.
flags: only-3-moves: the distribution is tightly constrained — any shift on one move forces the other two, and all ballots are near-degenerate on the same 40/32-33/27 shape (r1 mean CV 0.04).

containers.frame_rationale: Ringworm Guard is a lapel guard: the bottom player has wrapped the opponent's leg with a passed lapel, and the position exists to take the back via the lapel-sweep network. This makes the gi/no-gi split structural rather than stylistic. In the gi the position is a coherent, head-heavy back-take machine — the namesake Ringworm Sweep to Back Control leads (~30), with the Lapel Sweep to Back (~16-18) and Worm Guard recycling (~15-18) as the second engine and reset valve, and triangle/omoplata/bolo/spider filling a modest tail. No-gi the guard literally cannot be assembled: all three lapel/cloth-dependent moves (Ringworm Sweep, Lapel Sweep, Worm Guard recycle) are hard availability zeros, so the entire distribution collapses onto the three fabric-independent mechanics — Berimbolo Entry and Triangle Setup co-lead (~30-40 each, bolo edging ahead for the panelists who weight it as the surviving back-take), Omoplata Sweep as an honest third (~27-30), and a 2-point residual for a spider-style knee-push scramble (rarely attempted, not unavailable).

availability_rulings.reason: Requires the passed-lapel leg wrap that defines Ringworm Guard; no lapel exists no-gi so this back-take sweep cannot be assembled. Structural zero.
Lapel-dependent by name and mechanism; the sweep is powered by the wrapped lapel. Cannot exist no-gi. Structural zero.
Worm Guard is itself a lapel guard requiring the opponent's passed lapel; the recycle target does not exist no-gi. Structural zero.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Roger/Mendes + Statistician) failed to break the proposed distribution across 4 rounds. Both frames sum to 100 (gi 30+7+8+17+11+16+11; nogi 0+34+28+0+36+0+2). The three nogi zeros (Ringworm Sweep to Back Control, Lapel Sweep to Back, Ringworm Guard to Worm Guard) are existence-zeros, not stylistic ones: Ringworm Guard is a passed-lapel guard, and all three moves are lapel/cloth-dependent by mechanism (the third recycles to Worm Guard, itself a lapel guard) — so no lapel means the moves and even the recycle target cannot be assembled. The flagged Sigma|Delta|=144 divergence fully decomposes into the lapel collapse: gi lapel mass (Ringworm Sweep 30 + Lapel Sweep 17 + Worm Guard 16 = 63) evaporates nogi and redistributes onto the three fabric-independent mechanics (Triangle +27, Berimbolo +25, Omoplata +20, Spider -9), so the largest-divergence flag is mechanism-justified rather than a defect. Rank orders are coach-recognizable in both frames: gi is a head-heavy back-take machine (namesake sweep leads at 30, lapel network second, top-5 share 85 fitting a specialist position); nogi collapses to bolo/triangle/omoplata co-leads with Berimbolo and Triangle within noise of each other (36 vs 34). Every proposed value sits within ~1 point of its panel mean (rounding only). The only elevated dispersion (Berimbolo nogi 3.01) does not warrant correction because the proposal sits at the mean and its lead over Triangle is inside that noise. No zero lacks a bulletproof availability argument, no divergence lacks a mechanism, and head-mass matches the real decision tree. All 7 moves accepted.

containers.frame_rationale: Ringworm Guard is a gi-only lapel guard, so the top (passing) player's attempt distribution forks sharply by ruleset. In the gi the fight is against a live lapel wrapping the leg: neutralizing that wrap comes first, so Lapel Grip Break/Posture Recovery (~27) and Leg Extraction from Lapel Wrap (~21) together form a legitimate ~48% two-move head, with the three actual passes (stack, standing-distance, smash) and the reset splitting the remainder. In no-gi the position barely exists: all three lapel-dependent actions (grip break, leg extraction, and the lapel-negation stack) go to zero as availability rulings, and the surviving mass collapses onto generic passing with Standing Guard Pass with Distance Creation as the clear ~40 head, followed by Smash Pass Counter and Standing Reset to Open Guard (~25-30 each). The only live intra-frame dissent is a token 2 on the stack pass no-gi from the two legends who argue a generic stack is universal.

verify.rationale: Ringworm Guard/top is a gi-only lapel-guard passing distribution; the adversarial panel (Musumeci, Roger, Mendes + Statistician) attacked every value and all six survived. The two definitional no-gi zeros (Lapel Grip Break, Leg Extraction from Lapel Wrap) are unbreakable availability rulings — no lapel means no referent, unanimous 0, dispersion 0.0. The third no-gi zero (Stack Pass with Lapel Control Negation) is a correct anti-double-count fold: its identity is lapel-negation, and any generic no-gi stack is already captured by Smash Pass Counter, so the two-legend token-2 dissent would double-book mass. The gi head is a mechanism-correct 49% (grip break 28 + leg extraction 21) — you cannot pass until the leg-trapping lapel wrap is neutralized, and grip break correctly precedes extraction. The no-gi head (Standing Distance Pass 41) is the correct modern default once the leg is freed. The only concern raised — Standing Reset (31) ranking above Smash Pass (28) in no-gi — was resolved as noise: the panel-mean gap is 2.5 with ~2.2 dispersion on both, a statistical tie, and in a seated/open-guard scramble reset legitimately competes with smashing, so no forced reorder. Σ|Δ|=124 divergence is fully traced to the lapel vanishing (gi head zeros out, surviving generic passes absorb the freed mass). Gi sum=100, no-gi sum=100; gi dispersions tight, no-gi wide but coherent.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a body-mechanics escape — no collar/lapel, no leglock, no ruleset-illegal technique — so there are no availability zeros and no legality-driven divergence; the gi/no-gi split is entirely grip-mechanism. In the gi, the top player's back-of-collar and pant/sleeve grips pin the bottom man down, so the population settles into grip-assisted guard recovery: Turtle to Guard is the clear gi head (Roger and the gi voices lift it to 13-16), and shaking the hook clean before recovering (Shake Off) is a natural gi first step. In no-gi the ride is slippery — sweat and the absence of anchoring grips mean the top man can't re-pin — so wrestling-up actions climb across the board: Technical Stand-up (Kade's no-gi 14), Standing up in Base, Sit Through Escape, and Granby Roll all gain 2-4 points no-gi at the direct expense of grip-dependent guard-pulling. Net: gi is guard-recovery-heavy, no-gi is scramble/stand-up-heavy, with Turtle to Guard and Shake Off co-anchoring the head in both frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Lands at half-guard/bottom — a low-value lateral roll that overlaps heavily in intent with Rolling to Guard and Granby Roll to Guard, both of which recover a better guard. Uniformly rated situational (7-8) by every legend and the thinnest attempt in the pack; a genuine but rare option, not a distinct escape the population reaches for. Flagged for possible fold, not removed now.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site values put Turtle to Guard at 50/50 and dumped the entire ride-kill family (Escape from Rodeo Ride 1, Roll from Rodeo Ride 1, Shake Off 2, Standing up in Base 2, Sit Through Escape 3) into near-zero — a single-spike uncalibrated distribution. Panel deliberately does NOT conform: the correct shape is head-heavy but plural (Turtle to Guard ~13, Shake Off ~11-13, plus a respected wrestling-up family), because a 50% single move plays as a spam-bot opponent and buries the moves that actually happen under a rodeo ride.

Ten near-peer escapes with no submissions and no dominant single move — inherently flatter than an attacking role. Panel resisted the uniform smear by anchoring a Turtle-to-Guard + Shake Off head, but the distribution legitimately has a long shallow tail here.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger Gracie, Marcelo Garcia, John Danaher + Statistician) accepts all 10 moves. Sum coherence holds exactly (gi 100, nogi 100). The why_selected top-40 L1 shift is legitimate: the panel correctly rejected the broken single-spike prior (Turtle to Guard 50/50, ride-kill family dumped near-zero) and replaced it with a plural head-heavy shape appropriate to a 10-move no-dominant escape role. Head-mass threads the needle: top-5 share is 57% in both frames — not a spike (70%+) and not a uniform smear (~50%). No zeros exist to defend, correct since every move is a body-mechanics escape with no availability or legality constraint (frame_rationale confirmed). Every gi/no-gi divergence carries a directional mechanism: gi lifts grip-assisted guard recovery (Turtle 14, Shake Off 13), no-gi lifts slippery wrestle-up actions (Technical Stand-up 11, Sit Through 12, Granby 12, Standing Base 11). Rank order is recognized by Marcelo (the position's coach): Turtle+Shake Off co-anchor the gi, no-gi flattens into a Granby/Sit-Through/Stand-up wrestling cluster, honest long tail. The single contested divergence — Shake Off gi 13 vs nogi 10 — drew adjust-pull from Marcelo and Danaher (shaking is arguably a no-gi-friendly slippery action, not gi-favored), but it carries the container's highest dispersion (nogi 1.74) and rides panel-mean support (12.74/10.25); correcting it would substitute our noise for theirs, so both conceded. The flagged overlap cluster (Turtle/Granby/Rolling/Elbow all terminating in bottom guard, ~41% mass) is a content-graph consolidation issue, correctly left as a flag rather than forced into the numbers. No corrections warranted.

containers.frame_rationale: Rodeo Ride/Top is a leg-ride harness whose entire purpose is to convert to back control, so in BOTH frames roughly half the attempt volume lives in the back-conversion cluster (Rodeo Ride to Back Control, Turtle to Back Take, Crab Ride to Back, Rolling Back Take). The gi/no-gi split is driven by two mechanisms. First, availability: the collar chokes — Clock Choke and Bow and Arrow — are pure gi moves and go to a hard 0 in no-gi (logged as availability rulings); their volume redistributes in no-gi into the Rear Naked Choke (nogi ~8-10 vs gi ~5), the strangle that replaces the collar finish. Second, preference under grips: no-gi favors entanglement-as-control, so Crab Ride to Back (nogi ~16 vs gi ~11-13), Turtle to Truck (nogi ~7 vs gi ~3-4), Darce (nogi ~5 vs gi ~2-3) and Calf Slicer (nogi ~4 vs gi ~2) all lean no-gi, because in the gi those points are absorbed by the collar-choke options and gi grips give alternative control routes. A few moves lean slightly gi (Crucifix, Rolling Back Take) because grips aid trapping and steering. The generic conversion 'Rodeo Ride to Back Control' and 'Turtle to Back Take' are the two symmetric workhorses in both frames.

availability_rulings.reason: Requires a gi collar/lapel to establish the choking grip across the neck; the technique does not exist without a collar, so it is genuinely unavailable in no-gi (attempt% = 0).

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely rare from this ride in both frames (gi ~2, nogi ~4). It is a real no-gi-native bonus off the leg entanglement so it is NOT zero, but it sits at the floor and is a candidate for later pruning if the position's move list needs trimming. Logged, not removed.

The panel did NOT conform; the shift is mechanism-justified.

(1) The two why_selected zeros — Clock Choke and Bow and Arrow, both no-gi — are bulletproof: both are definitionally collar/lapel strangles with no no-gi expression, backed by explicit availability_rulings, and the old 7/6 SEALED values were a genuine uncalibrated symmetric smear (correctly flagged SEALED_NOGI_SMEAR). (3) Every gi/no-gi divergence carries a stated mechanism: Crab Ride 13->17, Turtle to Truck 4->7, Darce 3->5, Calf Slicer 2->5, RNC 6->9 all track the no-gi entanglement-as-control / collar-substitution logic; gi keeps the collar chokes at #4/#5, which Roger endorses. containers.frame_rationale: No lapel/collar-dependent or leg-lock/heel-hook moves appear in this pack, so every one of the 12 moves is legal and attempted in both gi and no-gi — there are zero availability rulings. The gi/no-gi divergence is entirely a friction-and-grip story: gi lapel/sleeve friction eats the flexibility budget rubber guard depends on, so in the gi the honest 'Rubber Guard to Closed Guard' bail rises (typically 12-15 gi vs 8-12 no-gi) while Mission Control maintenance and the deep 10th Planet controls (Crackhead, Meathook, New York Control, Omoplata Sweep) shrink a point or two, because holding the deep rubber-guard structures is harder against gripping. No-gi lets committed 10P players climb the ladder more freely, so Mission Control entries and New York traffic sit slightly higher there. All divergences are small (<=2-4 points) and mechanism-justified; no move flips tier between frames.

containers.frame_rationale: The dominant and only large gi/no-gi divergence here is the heel hook: in no-gi Carni is fundamentally a heel-hook entanglement (workhorse ~40-45), but IBJJF gi competition bans heel hooks, so the gi attempt collapses to low single digits (~3-5, not zero — legal in some non-IBJJF gi rulesets and self-defense). That freed heel-hook volume does NOT smear evenly: it redistributes primarily to the kneebar (the legal leg attack sharing the same entry, which becomes the clear gi leader ~32-35), then the calf slicer (~30-33 gi), then the gogoplata setup (~24-30 gi). Consequently every non-heel move is meaningfully higher in gi than no-gi. The no-gi tail (kneebar ~20-22, calf slicer ~18-20, gogoplata ~15-18) stays honest and head-heavy behind the heel; the calf slicer's high success rate (50%) is deliberately not translated into high frequency.

availability_rulings.reason: IBJJF gi competition bans heel hooks, so attempts collapse to low single digits rather than zero — heel hooks remain legal in some gi rulesets (ADCC-gi crossovers, submission-only gi events) and in self-defense / non-IBJJF gi training, so the move is rare-but-present (gi ~3-5), not unavailable.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuine honest dissent on frequency: Craig/Mikey view the gogoplata as a flashy low-percentage tail move that rarely happens outside rubber-guard specialists; it survives (Bravo/Marcelo/Kade defend it as canonical from this exact shape) but is the weakest-support move here and the most plausible future removal if attempt data shows near-zero real usage.

verify.rationale: The no-gi frame and the central gi mechanism survive hostile review intact: Carni-bottom is a no-gi heel-hook delivery system (heel 45 workhorse, honest head-heavy tail), and the IBJJF gi heel-hook ban correctly collapses the gi heel to a fringe-legal ~4 (non-zero, not a hard zero) with that volume redistributing to legal leg attacks. The single Σ|Δ|=82 divergence is fully explained by that one ban, not smearing, so the frame is not re-elicited. One bounded correction survives: the gi gogoplata was over-allocated freed heel-hook volume it should not mechanistically receive. Heel volume flows to moves sharing the ashi/Carni leg-entanglement ENTRY (kneebar, calf slicer) — the gogoplata is a distinct rubber-guard neck/upper-body mechanism, so it should rise only modestly in gi (gi does mildly help its setup), not absorb heel volume like a leg-attack substitute. The panel pulled gogoplata gi from 28 down to 22 (top of the conservative Craig/Mikey dissent camp, honoring the spread rather than difference-splitting) and moved those ~6 points onto the kneebar (35->41), the true direct heel-hook substitute and the correct gi leader once heels are banned. Resulting gi deltas vs no-gi (heel -41, kneebar +20, calf +15, gogoplata +6) are MORE mechanistically coherent than the proposal: the primary leg substitute diverges most, the non-leg-entry gogoplata barely diverges. Calf slicer and heel accepted as proposed; no-gi accepted wholesale. Note the panel flag stands that this 10th-Planet-terminology node may see low real-world attempt volume overall.

containers.frame_rationale: Carni/Top is a defensive extraction position — the top player is caught in a leg entanglement while the bottom hunts heel hook, kneebar, calf slicer, and gogoplata, so every move is a pass or a posture reset, not offense. All four moves are passing/posture mechanics that are fully legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi, so there are no availability zeros. The gi/no-gi differences are small and grip-mediated rather than legality-driven: the knee slice gains a slight gi edge because a collar/sleeve grip stabilizes the slice, the leg drag gains a slight no-gi edge because slicker legs make the redirect cleaner, the stack pass has a tiny gi lean from cloth friction (partly offset by no-gi pace), and posture recovery is essentially frame-neutral since it is a head-position/posture reset. Net: knee slice and leg drag are near-tied co-leaders in both frames, posture recovery a clear third as the reset, and the stack pass the honest tail.

containers.frame_rationale: Chill Dog/Bottom is a defensive turtle variant (10th Planet terminology), and every one of its nine moves is legal and mechanically available in BOTH gi and no-gi — there are no collar/lapel-only or gi-illegal techniques here, so no availability-zero rulings apply. The gi/no-gi divergence is therefore purely FRICTION-driven, not legality-driven, and it is small. Two moves lean no-gi: Granby Roll to Guard (no pant/collar grips to follow the inverted roll, so it flows more freely and is attempted a bit more) and Technical Stand-up (no collar drag pinning you down, so wrestling up is easier and more frequent). Everything else is essentially mirrored, with gi occasionally a hair higher on grip-dependent framing (e.g., shrimping/framing recoveries) and no-gi a hair higher on scramble-out recoveries. The distribution is head-heavy on guard re-establishment — Escape Chill Dog (named signature), Turtle to Guard, Granby Roll to Guard, and Rolling to Guard form the head — with an honest tail of Roll and Sweep from Chill Dog as opportunistic attacks. The sanity-diff confirmed the old site values were badly miscalibrated: Technical Stand-up was grossly overweighted at 32 (even the wrestle-up advocates land it ~9-15) and the named Escape Chill Dog was grossly underweighted at 5 (it is a co-head at ~15); the panel corrected both and did not conform to the sealed numbers.

containers.frame_rationale: Chill Dog/Top is a rubber-guard-derived scramble where the bottom player is in a defensive shell exposing the back and a front-headlock line, so in BOTH frames the back-take leads clearly (weighted ~20 gi / ~19 nogi) and no move is ruleset-unavailable — every entry (positional, wrestling, or choke) exists with a no-gi equivalent, so there are zero availability zeros and the whole gi/no-gi story is magnitude, not presence. The divergence is driven by the collar and sweat: in the gi the front-headlock choke family (darce, anaconda, guillotine) is defended by the collar frame and chin tuck, so it compresses while grip-dependent control raises the crucifix (Mendes' thesis) and lets gi players posture-and-pass methodically (pass and posture are the second and third gi heads). In no-gi the same choke family roughly doubles its share (darce ~7→~12, guillotine ~5→~8, anaconda ~5→~7) because there is no lapel to frame and sweat makes the chokes live, the truck ticks up as a native 10th Planet exit, and back-take/posture/pass/stack/crucifix each drift down a few points as the finish threats eat their share — turning the no-gi opponent into a front-headlock hunter (darce+FHL-to-back+guillotine+anaconda ≈ a third of all attempts) while the gi opponent plays like a control-and-pass rider.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely native to Chill Dog (Bravo's signature exit) and mechanically valid in both frames, so NOT recommended for removal — but flagged as the lowest-frequency population move (weighted ~4 gi / 7 nogi). Only Bravo weights it double-digit; the field treats it as a specialist 10th Planet entry whose 48% success rate does not translate into attempt volume for the general grappler.

The old file also over-weighted the front-headlock choke family flatly (Crucifix/FHL 12, Darce/Truck 10) with no no-gi skew. We did NOT conform: back-take held at ~20 (old 31 was too high) and the choke family carries a genuine gi/no-gi split.

containers.frame_rationale: Crackhead Control is a 10th-Planet, no-gi-native rubber-guard position: as a whole it is far more PREVALENT under no-gi, but that is a between-position fact, not a within-position one. Conditional on already being in Crackhead Control, the internal attempt distribution is nearly frame-identical because nothing here is lapel/collar-dependent and no submission is heel-hook/reaping (so there are no ruleset-illegal moves and no per-frame zeros). The only genuine, mechanism-backed gi/no-gi divergence is the Gogoplata (nogi > gi: gi pants friction plus the extreme flexibility demand suppress the shin-across-throat slide, while no-gi sweat aids it), with a slighter same-direction edge on the Triangle (no-gi is its native frame and the fabric-free control cinches cleaner). Everything else holds equal across frames.

containers.frame_rationale: All six moves are grip-agnostic mechanical passes and back-takes, so none are ruleset-locked and there are no per-frame zeros or availability rulings. Stack Pass is the clearest split (no-gi higher: ~18-19 vs gi ~15-16) because sweat lets the top drive through the flared guard while gi cloth gives the bottom framing and shrimping resistance — this tracks the success anchors (gi 41.6 / nogi 51.3). Arm Extraction reads a hair higher in the gi for grip-oriented players (sleeve/wrist control strips the overhook) but stays essentially even. Back Take and Rolling Back Take run marginally higher in the gi for players who climb to the back off collar/posture control, though the rolling anchor actually favors gi success, so they are kept near-even with gi a touch ahead. Posture Recovery ticks slightly higher in the gi where the position feels stickier and tops bail out more.

(1) why_selected concern 'Back Take spread 32': the crosscheck flagged wide panel disagreement, but post-convergence dispersion is low (gi 0.54 / nogi 0.76) and panel_mean (22.09/21.77) sits exactly on the proposed 22/21 — the disagreement was resolved, not papered over, and Back Take's promotion from old prior 18 to a clear #1 is mechanism-backed (crackhead-control exposes the bottom's back when the lockdown fails). (2) Zeros: none, correctly — all six are grip-agnostic mechanical passes/back-takes, so no availability zero is warranted; frame_rationale defends this explicitly. (3) Divergences: the only splits are Stack Pass (gi16/nogi18) and Double Underhook (gi18/nogi19), both no-gi higher on a stated friction mechanism (sweat/no-cloth lets the top drive through the flared guard), and Stack Pass tracks its success anchor (gi41.6/nogi51.3); Back Take and Rolling run gi-a-touch-higher for the collar/posture climb. All divergences are <=2pt with mechanisms. (4) Rank order (nogi): Back Take 21 > Double Under 19 > Stack 18 > Arm Extraction 17 > Posture Recovery 14 > Rolling 11 — a passer's real decision tree, with the deliberate and defensible demotion of Posture Recovery from the old plurality (20) to 14 (panel_mean 14.32/13.44), since posture recovery is a retreat not the dominant intent. (5) Head-mass: top-3 = 57gi/58nogi across 6 moves — head-heavy but non-degenerate, matching a control-escape position where the top hunts the exposed back and drives passes. Sums are exact (gi 100, nogi 100). Every proposed_final rounds within +-0.7 of its panel_mean, with the small up/down rounding choices serving sum-to-100 coherence rather than distorting evidence. Nothing to correct.

containers.frame_rationale: This is a back-control/turtle-adjacent escape position and the 'invisible collar' is a shoulder-line arm concept, not a lapel-dependent grip, so every move survives fully into no-gi and no move earns a per-frame zero. The distribution is near ruleset-stable and head-heavy: hand fighting the choking arm is the single workhorse (~36-38) in both frames, edging slightly higher no-gi because the RNC finishes faster and winning the grip is more urgent. Hip escape is the clear #2 (~21-23) and sits marginally higher gi where you can post on cloth to frame and shrimp. The one genuine mechanism-backed divergence is Standing Escape: it is more available no-gi (~11-14) than gi (~6-9) because in the gi the collar/lapel anchors you down and standing surrenders the back, while no-gi the slide-out standup is cleaner. Elbow escape (~15-16) and the two rare recovery scrambles (rolling ~8, granby ~5-6) are essentially flat across rulesets.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split here is driven entirely by cloth. Invisible Collar is a back-control configuration, and in every ruleset control comes first: Back Control Maintenance is the single most-attempted move (~27-30) in both frames, with the Body Triangle Lock the second workhorse (running slightly higher no-gi, ~18-21, because without collar grips the body triangle does the position-holding job the cloth does in the gi). The submission traffic is where the frames fork. In the gi the collar family carries the attack volume — cross-collar (~15-17), bow-and-arrow (~15-16), and clock choke (~5) — while the RNC drops to a modest ~12-13. In no-gi that entire collar family collapses: the Rear Naked Choke absorbs nearly all finishing traffic (~36-38), the bow-and-arrow and clock choke are hard availability zeros (both require a collar), and the cross-collar keeps only a small 2-5 residual for the gi-less gable-grip neck strangle that people still reach for even though it rarely finishes and is close to a re-labeled RNC. Armbar-from-back-transition (~7-8) and the Aoki-to-crucifix tail (~2-4) are frame-neutral situational/rare moves.

availability_rulings.move: Bow and Arrow Choke from Invisible Collar
availability_rulings.reason: The bow-and-arrow is defined by gripping the opponent's collar and pulling it across the neck with a leg-assisted bow. No collar exists in no-gi, so the strangle is mechanically impossible. Unanimous hard zero.
The clock choke drives the far collar into the neck while circling. It requires cloth on the far side of the neck; without a gi collar the lever does not exist. Unanimous hard zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Every legend independently tiered this 'rare' and landed it at 2-4 in both frames; it is a genuine tail move from Invisible Collar (a crucifix-entry leg entanglement) that almost never happens here. Kept for now, but a candidate for pruning if the position's move list is trimmed.

verify.rationale: Invisible Collar is a back-control configuration and the proposed distribution reads as a legitimate back-control decision tree in both frames. Structural checks pass: gi sums to 100, nogi sums to 100. The two why_selected zeros are bulletproof availability rulings, not disputable content decisions: Bow-and-Arrow and Clock Choke are collar-dependent strangles that are mechanically impossible without cloth, so nogi=0 is correct and the old prior (11/10) leaving them live was the actual bug. Every gi/no-gi divergence is mechanism-backed by the cloth story: the gi collar family (CrossCollar 16, BowArrow 16, Clock 5) collapses in nogi while the RNC absorbs the finishing traffic (12 gi -> 37 nogi) and the Body Triangle rises (12 -> 19) to do the position-holding job the collar does in the gi. The contested CrossCollar nogi is correctly resolved as a small 2-5 residual (proposed 4) for the gable-grip neck strangle rather than a hard zero, since that strangle is mechanically possible without cloth. Rank order is coach-recognizable in both frames (control first, then strangles, with armbar/crucifix tails). Head-mass is concentrated (gi top-5 84%, nogi top-5 97%) but that is expected and correct for a high-conviction back-control position, not a misallocation. Soft spots (BowArrow gi tied with CrossCollar at 16; RNC gi arguably a touch low for a fundamentalist) sit inside the panel's tiny dispersions (0.4-1.4) and do not justify overriding a colleague panel.

containers.frame_rationale: Meathook is a 10th-Planet no-gi-native waypoint, so most volume tilts slightly toward no-gi: the gogoplata line (the whole purpose of the position), the mission-control reset, the triangle, and the carni continuation all run marginally hotter no-gi, where there is no gi friction on the shin and no grip-management tax on the chain. The gi divergence is concentrated in the two shoulder-lock exotics, Baratoplata Setup and Tarikoplata Setup: these are grip-driven, gi-meta shoulder locks, so they sit at ~5-8 in the gi and fall to a 3-4 floor no-gi. No move here is a lapel/collar-only technique and none is banned in either ruleset (baratoplata/tarikoplata remain gripless-executable, just rarer), so there are no forced per-frame zeros and no availability rulings are required.
