containers.frame_rationale: Meathook/Top is a defensive/escape node, not an attacking one: the top player's arm is isolated by the overhook and his posture is broken forward, so all four moves are recovery responses to a Rubber Guard trap threatening gogoplata, omoplata, triangle and back exposure. The one systematic gi/no-gi divergence is Sprawl: no-gi it runs 2-3 points higher because the scramble is faster and there are no lapel/sleeve handles to keep the top man pinned, so sprawling the hips back to a front headlock is the cleanest exit; in the gi those grips slow the scramble and reward a more methodical posture-recovery-then-open-guard sequence, which is why Roger holds gi Sprawl lowest and lets Posture Recovery / Guard Opening absorb the difference. Posture Recovery leans slightly gi or even (methodical rebuild is more the gi answer; Kade/Mikey/Marcelo trade it down no-gi in favor of exploding out). Guard Opening and Stack Pass are essentially frame-neutral support moves. No move is lapel-, collar-, or heel-hook-dependent, so nothing is unavailable in either ruleset and there are no per-frame zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Not a removal — logged as the watch-item tail. It is genuinely the least-attempted of the four because it is downstream of first surviving the trap (kill the arm-isolation, then stack), but the panel unanimously kept it near ~20-22, well above the old site's starved value of 5. It happens; it just happens last.

flags: Role framing: 'top' here is the player CAUGHT in the Meathook (arm isolated, posture broken) — the escaping/defending side — not an attacker. All four moves are recovery/escape actions; there is intentionally no offensive move in this list.

Recalibration vs old site (not a conform): the panel independently landed on Sprawl as a co-leader (~27 gi / ~30 nogi) where the sealed site value was 22/22, and dropped Posture Recovery from the site's spammy 42 to ~26-27. Stack Pass was raised from the site's starved 5 to ~20-21. These are deliberate calibrated corrections, not misses to conform to.

Low-dispersion position (r1_mean_cv 0.066): the panel arrived largely pre-converged; deliberation fine-tuned the Sprawl gi/no-gi split and the Sprawl-vs-Posture-Recovery ordering rather than overhauling anything.

Persistent honest dissent retained: Roger holds gi Sprawl lowest (24) on the gi-grip argument; Kade holds Sprawl highest (31/33) on the no-gi-scramble argument; Danaher/Roger keep Posture Recovery highest (30) as the safety valve. These are genuine mechanism-level holds, not difference-splitting.

containers.frame_rationale: Rubber guard is fundamentally a no-gi / 10th-Planet construct, so the whole distribution describes a population that is overwhelmingly no-gi; the gi version exists but is played by a tiny minority. The SHAPE is identical in both frames -- a head-heavy triangle cluster (Triangle from Guard + Triangle Setup + Closed Guard to Triangle ~= 37) is the engine, with Closed Guard to Omoplata as the main secondary. The divergence is in the tail: (1) the 10P positional progressions (Progression to Zombie, Advance to Chill Dog) are the system's native spine and skew clearly no-gi, because in the gi collar/sleeve grips give the top player posture options that make deep rubber-guard climbing a poor bet -- Roger holds these low in the gi while Bravo/Marcelo/Lachlan keep them fat in no-gi; (2) the Gogoplata is a signature-but-low no-gi flourish, suppressed (not banned) in the gi by grips on the setup; (3) the Omoplata / Omoplata Sweep get a small gi bump from lapel friction that helps steer and finish. No move is ruleset-unavailable here, so there are no per-frame zeros.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal but structurally suppressed in the gi (collar/sleeve grips disrupt the shin-across-throat setup), NOT unavailable. Held at a low positive value (~5), not zero.
Fully legal in the gi; only suppressed because rubber-guard climbing exposes collar/sleeve grips to top posture. Low positive value on Roger's dissent, never zero.

flags: Persistent structured dissent on the gi progressions (Progression to Zombie, Advance to Chill Dog): gi fundamentalist (Roger, gi 6/5) vs 10P-native voices (Bravo/Marcelo/Lachlan, gi 10-12). SANITY-DIFF: the old sealed site values were near-uniform (mostly 9-12). Gross misses corrected by the panel: Gogoplata was overweighted at 11 (panel ~5 gi / ~8 nogi -- it is a low-frequency flourish), Triangle from Guard was underweighted at 12 (panel ~15-16 -- it is the modal move), and Progression to Zombie at 9 undersold its no-gi frequency (panel ~13-15 nogi). We did not conform; the panel is correctly head-heavier.
This is a submission_control bottom seat, so sweeps (Hip Bump, Omoplata Sweep) are legitimately secondary to submission attempts -- their modest weights are intentional, not an under-read.

containers.frame_rationale: Mission Control is a leg-and-arm clamp (bottom overhooks the top man's arm and uses the mission-control leg grip to trap head and shoulder), NOT a cloth-dependent grip like a collar or lapel guard. Because the control is on the arm and neck rather than on the gi, there is no legality divergence and no strong grip-driven divergence between frames — every one of the five moves is legal and live in both gi and no-gi, so there are no availability zeros. The divergences that remain are mild and directional: the gi's slower pace and cloth-assisted grip-fight let the bottom hold the clamp longer, so the trapped top man spends marginally more attempts on Posture Recovery and Posture Break (gi-leaning), while no-gi's sweat and faster scrambles let the arm slip free and let the top man drive-through, so Arm Extraction and Stack Pass tick up a few points (no-gi-leaning). All frame gaps stay within ~1-3 points.

removal_candidates.reason: Weakest of the five and situational — you can only stack once posture is partly recovered, so it rarely fires from a deep clamp. Still a real, legal pass in both frames (honest tail ~13-18), NOT a never-happens move. Logged, not removed.

flags: Posture Break from Mission Control and Posture Recovery from Mission Control are near-duplicate intentions (break the bottom's clamp vs rebuild your own base) and both land at closed-guard/top — likely double-counting one motion. Panel pulled Posture Break down off the flat Round-1 ~22 anchor to the mid-teens to avoid double-weighting; flagged for possible future consolidation.

Round 1 was suspiciously flat (r1_mean_cv 0.07; four of five moves inside a 20-24 band), reading as anchoring rather than genuine independent convergence. The panel deliberately moved to a head-heavier shape (Arm Extraction + Posture Recovery as twin heads ~24-27, tail at ~14-16) after the mechanism debate and the Round-10 sanity signal.

Sealed site values (Recovery 36, Arm Extraction 29, Guard Opening 22, Posture Break 9, Stack Pass 4) were even more head-heavy; panel accepted the two-head direction but declined to conform to the site's harsh Posture Break 9 and Stack Pass 4, landing both a few points higher as honest, calibrated values.
Top-man pack contains no submission, which is correct (the trapped top man does not submit from Mission Control) — flagged so no phantom submission is added later.

containers.frame_rationale: New York Control is a no-gi-native 10th-Planet rubber-guard construct in which every technique frames the head/arm (the 'New York', 'invisible collar', 'zombie' are flesh-and-limb frames, not gi-collar grips), so there is nothing legal-only-in-gi and nothing banned-in-gi here — no per-frame zeros are warranted. The distribution is therefore near frame-identical, with only mechanism-driven tilts: the gogoplata leans slightly no-gi (the sweaty foot-to-throat leg-over is easier without gi-pant/knee friction), while the omoplata sweep leans slightly gi (grips let you off-balance the opponent into the sweep, whereas no-gi it's slipped and traded for the back-take). Control transitions (crackhead-to-mission, zombie, invisible collar) carry a whisper of a no-gi tilt from sliding-frame friction. The spine both ways is the triangle setup and its omoplata/back branches; the triangle family, if folded, overwhelmingly dominates, but since the branches are listed separately the raw setup entry lands ~13 rather than the site's over-concentrated 18.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in the gi but a slight down-tilt vs no-gi, not a zero: the gi pant/knee fabric slows the foot-to-throat leg-over and the whole rubber-guard grip is stickier no-gi. Attempted rarely either way (a real situational threat from trapped head control), so gi stays a low positive (~4-5), never 0.

Available no-gi but a slight down-tilt vs gi, not a zero: in the gi you can grip and off-balance for the sweep, whereas no-gi the opponent slips the omoplata and the sweep gets abandoned for the back-take. No-gi stays a solid positive (~6-8), never 0.

Attempted rarely (~5) as a scramble bail-out, so kept, but it is the weakest structural fit in the pack and a candidate for pruning if the position is tightened.

flags: Flat/branch-heavy distribution: 13 moves with the top (Triangle Setup ~13) only ~2.6x the smallest (~5). Not head-heavy in the raw list, but coherent once you recognize the triangle FAMILY (setup + to-omoplata + to-back + omoplata-to-back ~39 combined) is the true head — the flatness is an artifact of listing every branch separately.

Two near-duplicate moves to one destination: 'New York to Invisible Collar' and 'New York Control to Invisible Collar' both land at invisible-collar/bottom. Structurally redundant; see removal_candidates.

SANITY-DIFF: site had Triangle Setup at 18 (over-concentrated) while under-weighting its branches (Triangle to Omoplata 7, Omoplata to Back 6). Panel redistributes toward the branches; setup lands ~13. containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi differences here are small and all mechanism-driven rather than availability-driven — no move is illegal or impossible in either frame, so there are no zeros. The single clean divergence is Stack Pass: it is attempted more in no-gi (~16-17) than gi (~13-15), tracking the calibrated success gap (gi 41.6% vs no-gi 51.3%) because gi grips and the persistent lapel/sleeve-anchored rubber-guard frame slow the pass and reward the top man for staying patient, whereas the sweaty no-gi frame slips and invites the bull-through stack. Correspondingly Posture Recovery skews a touch higher in the gi (patience is rewarded, ~23-24 gi vs ~22-23 no-gi) and Overhook Escape is near-even (sleeve grips drag the arm in the gi, sweat frees it in no-gi — the two effects roughly cancel). Everything else — Crossface to Combat Base, New York Control Escape, Guard Pass — is frame-neutral within ±1. The position is fundamentally a trapped-top survival spot, so the head is Posture Recovery + Overhook Escape in both frames.

The divergence is soft and one-directional: the pure 10th Planet advancement/neck branches (Chill Dog, Invisible Collar, Zombie, Gogoplata) run roughly +1 to +2 hotter in no-gi because the gi collar and lapel friction interfere with the shin-across-throat and neck-thread mechanics and hand the opponent posture handles. containers.frame_rationale: Every move in this position is a posture/passing mechanic available in BOTH gi and no-gi — there are no lapel, collar, or leg-lock-legality issues, so no move is zeroed and no availability rulings are required. All gi/no-gi divergences are small friction/grip effects with a clear mechanism and direction: Posture Recovery ticks slightly higher no-gi (slippery, you re-posture more often); Stack Pass is higher no-gi (sweat lets the stack slide); Pressure Pass is higher gi (grips let the top man pin and pressure); Posture Recovery to Closed Guard is marginally higher gi (closed guard is a more valued recovery destination in the gi). Overhook Extraction, Guard Opening Sequence, and New York Pass to Side Control are effectively frame-neutral in attempt rate — the arm must be freed and the guard opened regardless of ruleset (gi changes their success, not their frequency). The Stack-up-no-gi / Pressure-up-gi pair are opposite and both mechanistically sound, which is the key cross-check on the divergence.

removal_candidates.reason: Heavily overlaps with Posture Recovery (both are posture-recovery lines splitting the same budget); it is the situational 'settled into closed guard instead of combat base' fallback. Genuinely low-frequency, especially no-gi where combat base is preferred. Not removed now, but flagged as a merge/prune candidate.

flags: Two-headed head-heavy distribution: Posture Recovery (~24-26) and Overhook Extraction (~16-19) are both near-workhorse because they are the top man's two sequential jobs (get head up, then free the trapped arm); the three passing moves form an honest downstream tail.

SANITY-DIFF vs sealed site values found two gross misses the panel corrects: old site had Stack Pass at 25 (badly inflated — you cannot stack before recovering posture; stacking is a downstream pass, not the default) and Posture Recovery at only 19 (badly deflated — it is the genuinely central move). Panel did NOT conform; our numbers already fix both by raising Posture and cutting Stack to the low-tail.

Authentic residual dissent logged, not smoothed: Danaher holds Pressure Pass low and Posture-Recovery-to-Closed-Guard high (control-hierarchy read); Bravo/Mikey hold Overhook Extraction at 18-19 (position author's emphasis on arm-freeing).

containers.frame_rationale: Bottom Zombie is a compromised defensive shell, so in BOTH rulesets the head of the attempt distribution is survival-first: Guard Recovery, Turn to Face, and Escape Zombie Control, with Lockdown Recovery as maintenance underneath. The gi/no-gi split is concentrated in the 10th Planet offensive lines. In no-gi there are no grips to pin the bottom player or strip the lockdown, so the Electric Chair Transition (+~3), Roll to Truck (+~3), and Granby Roll (+~2) all pick up frequency and the recovery head thins slightly to fund them. In the gi, top-side grips make guard recovery and turning to face the cleanest, most-trained answers (recovery head slightly higher), while the Deep Half Entry ticks up as a gi lightweight under-pass habit and the truck roll nearly dies. No move is unavailable in either frame; the divergences are population/mechanism-driven, not legality-driven.

availability_rulings.reason: Legal in the gi but almost never attempted here — grips let the top player deny the crab-ride entry and the truck is a no-gi-culture line. Kept low-but-nonzero (2-4), not zeroed.

Legal in the gi but suppressed — pant/lapel grips let the top player strip the lockdown control before the electric chair finishes; it is a no-gi-leaning offense. Kept low-but-nonzero (5-8), not zeroed.

removal_candidates.reason: Genuinely rare from bottom zombie, especially in the gi (2-4). A specialist 10th-Planet transition, not a population-frequent attempt; logged for future pruning review but retained now as a legitimate no-gi minority line.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site values had the head/tail inverted — Old School Sweep was grossly overweighted at 38 (panel lands ~10, no legend above 12), while Turn to Face (site 1) and Escape Zombie Control (site 2) were grossly underweighted despite the entire panel treating them as head-of-distribution survival moves. Panel shape (recovery + turn-to-face + escape as the head) intentionally does NOT conform to the old uncalibrated numbers.

Position labeled 'pins_top' family but this is the bottom role of a bottom-player guard/shell position; role reads correctly as bottom-player escape/recovery/sweep options — no role misread, but the family tag is worth a coherence check.

Several bottom moves land at top-side outcomes (Old School Sweep -> mount/top, Roll to Truck -> truck/top, Sweep from Zombie Guard -> mount/top) which is correct for a bottom sweep/reversal; noted for graph-edge sanity only.

containers.frame_rationale: Zombie/Top is a hybrid rubber-guard/lockdown-turtle state, and the gi/no-gi split follows directly from which grips and which finishing metas are live. In BOTH frames the top player's dominant early work is unglamorous: recover posture and strip the trapping grip before any pass or back-take is earned - that is why Posture Recovery and Strip Grip lead the distribution in both rulesets. The divergence: Strip Grip is meaningfully HIGHER in the gi (collar/sleeve/lapel grips of rubber guard are stickier and stripping them is job one), while in no-gi the gable/wrist grip is slipperier and less dedicated stripping is needed, so strip drops ~4-6 points. Conversely, the front-headlock attacks (Darce, Anaconda) and the leg-ride Crab Ride are meaningfully HIGHER in no-gi, where the exposed neck/chin and the truck/leg-ride meta are native (gi collar frames defend the darce and it is simply less trained in the gi). Passes and back-takes are near-equal across frames, with a slight gi edge on passing control from grip-assisted pressure. No move in this pack is illegal or unavailable in either ruleset, so there are no forced zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Craig calls it fantasy from a rubber-guard/zombie shell and the panel splits on whether it happens at all; it is mechanically possible in the turtle phase (more so no-gi with the leg-ride/truck meta) so it stays non-zero, but it is the lowest-conviction move on the sheet - flag for possible removal if the graph needs pruning.

Consistently the second-rarest attack; a no-gi-only-relevant front-headlock choke that most legends rank at or near the floor in gi (3-5) and only modestly above in no-gi. Overlaps heavily with Darce from Turtle as the front-headlock option - candidate to fold into the darce if pruning.

flags: Old site inverted the distribution: it made Crossface Pass the dominant move (gi/nogi 27) while burying Posture Recovery (2) and Strip Grip (1) at the bottom. The panel corrects this - for a rubber-guard/zombie top position the top player's first job is posture and grip recovery, so those two are the head of the distribution and Crossface is a normal mid-band pass (~8-9). We did not conform to the sealed values.

Structural double-count risk: 'Turtle to Back Take' and 'Back Take' are two distinct moves that both target the same prize (the opponent's back). The panel deliberately keeps their COMBINED total modest (~22-26) to avoid inflating the back-take likelihood; Mendes concentrates on Turtle-to-Back, Marcelo split across both, and the group nudged Marcelo's generic Back Take down from 18 to ~13-14. Consider merging these two routes if the graph needs a cleaner state machine.

Genuine unresolved pole retained (not smeared): Bravo/Craig hold Posture+Strip very high (~40 combined) as the 10th-Planet reality of being stuck in rubber guard, while the back-hunters (Mendes/Marcelo/Roger/Kade) hold those lower (~16-22 combined) and concentrate on the back and passes. This dissent is authentic to the position's hybrid nature and is preserved in the final ballots rather than averaged away.

Two front-headlock chokes (Darce, Anaconda) plus a back-take-adjacent Crab Ride cluster in the low no-gi tier and are near-floor in the gi - the no-gi lean is real but the moves overlap functionally; see removal_candidates.

containers.frame_rationale: Russian Cowboy bottom is a niche truck/twister/crucifix-adjacent pin, and every listed move is a grip-agnostic escape or scramble — none is lapel/collar-specific and none is heel-hook-specific, so there are no genuine availability zeros in either frame. All gi/no-gi divergence is grip-mechanism, not legality: in the gi the top player's sleeve/collar grips arrest the granby spin and let them chase a standing bottom player, so Granby Roll and Technical Stand-up are attempted slightly less in the gi; in no-gi the frictionless scramble and the truck/leg entanglement raise Granby and Roll Escape. Arm Recovery to Guard is the mechanistic workhorse in both frames — freeing the isolated arm is the prerequisite to every real escape — and sits symmetric because gi grips slow the extraction but do not change that it is the first thing the bottom player must do.

availability_rulings.reason: Available in both frames; no availability zero. Gi grips can arrest the spin so it is attempted slightly less in the gi than no-gi, but it remains a common re-guard exit.
Available in both frames; standing up into the truck threat is riskier and easier to drag back down in the gi, so it is attempted a touch less in the gi, but never zero.
Available in both frames; the no-gi truck/leg entanglement feeds the roll, so it is attempted slightly more in no-gi. Not an availability difference, a mechanism nudge.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency generic escape whose only listed outcome lands at side-control/top; it overlaps heavily with the more specific named escapes (hip escape, roll escape, arm recovery) and reads as a catch-all rather than a distinct attempted action. Panel keeps it as a low tail (8-10) for now but flags it as the weakest/most redundant label.

flags: Very flat, low-CV position (r1_mean_cv 0.068): a near-uniform 8-way escape menu. Per advisor pressure the panel concentrated a readable head (Arm Recovery ~16-18) and honest tail (Escape from RC ~8-10) rather than leaving it uniform, but it remains structurally flat by nature.

SANITY-DIFF gross miss: SEALED site values weight Arm Extraction to Turtle at 36 (vs panel ~12) and Arm Recovery to Guard at only 12 (vs panel ~17). The old uncalibrated numbers over-promoted turtle (a concession exit) and buried the true workhorse (arm recovery); panel does NOT conform. Old tail (Roll Escape 2, Escape from RC 1) is too low — 'rarely' is 8-11 situational, not 1-2.

'Escape from Russian Cowboy' lands at side-control/top per the pack — escaping a bottom pin into TOP side control is a scramble-win outcome, which is plausible for a reversal but odd for a generic 'escape' label; worth verifying the outcome target is intended (see removal_candidates).

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi fork here is one of the sharpest in the corpus and is driven by three mechanisms. (1) Collar dependence: the Bow and Arrow Choke is a collar/lapel strangle that is a gi staple (~13) but structurally impossible no-gi (hard 0, availability-ruled) — its gi weight redistributes no-gi into the RNC, truck and twister. (2) Rule suppression: the Twister is IBJJF-banned in gi competition, but it is mechanically gi-independent (leg-lace + head control works with a gi on) and is trained/legal in some gi rulesets, so gi is rare (~3) rather than a structural zero, while no-gi it is a genuine 10th-Planet signature finish off this exact hip position (~12). (3) Grip friction + payoff loss: gi grips slow the leg-entanglement scramble and, with the twister rule-suppressed, the payoff of entering the truck falls, so the Truck Entry and Calf Slicer are meaningfully lower in the gi (truck ~11 vs ~16, calf slicer ~4 vs ~8). Everything else is roughly flat with a mild no-gi lean on the RNC (no collar-choke competing for the finish). The head of the distribution is ruleset-agnostic: Russian Cowboy to Back Control and the RNC together carry the position because the correct play from this unorthodox back variation is to normalize into orthodox back control and strangle.

availability_rulings.move: Bow and Arrow Choke from Russian Cowboy
availability_rulings.reason: Structurally unavailable no-gi: the bow-and-arrow is a collar/lapel choke that requires a gi collar grip. Without the gi the technique does not exist, so a hard 0 no-gi is correct (not merely rare).

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the tail across all 10 legends (gi ~6, nogi ~5-6), never argued up in debate. A legitimate but very situational branch off the back transition; it floats at the floor and is the weakest justified edge from this position. Logged for review, not removed.

flags: Twister-gi legality nuance: IBJJF-banned in gi COMPETITION but mechanically gi-independent and legal/trained in some gi rulesets. The panel deliberately kept gi twister as RARE (2-4) rather than a hard availability-0, unlike the collar-dependent bow-and-arrow. Consumers modeling strict IBJJF gi competition may wish to floor it further; consumers modeling general gi rolling should keep it rare-but-present.

Head-underweight correction vs old site: the sealed uncalibrated site value had 'Russian Cowboy to Back Control' at only 5 in both frames. The panel unanimously makes it the HEAD of the distribution (~19-24 gi, ~19-21 nogi). containers.frame_rationale: Seated guard's engine — Butterfly Sweep, Single Leg X Entry, and the wrestle-up (Technical Stand-up) — is present in both rulesets, but the periphery diverges on grip mechanics. In no-gi there is no cloth to pin the seated player, so wrestle-ups and single-leg-X entries spike (standups roughly double vs gi; SLX runs ~18 vs ~13), and the front-headlock economy of the modern pace amplifies the get-up further. In the gi the position becomes a grip fight: standing-opponent sweeps that feed off pant and sleeve grips (Tripod, Foot Grab, Ankle Pick) hold a larger share, and Scissor Sweep survives almost exclusively as a gi technique because it needs the collar to break posture and load the sweep — in no-gi it collapses to a 1-2 floor. Butterfly stays king in both, ticking slightly higher in no-gi where it chains cleanly into the leg game.

availability_rulings.reason: Not unavailable — mechanically possible off an underhook or collar-tie in no-gi — but almost entirely abandoned from a seated posture without the collar to break posture and load weight. Floored at 1-2, NOT zero, per the 'rarely = 1-3' rule.

containers.frame_rationale: This is the single sharpest gi/no-gi fork in the batch, and the fork is grip-mechanism, not legality — every one of the nine moves is a pass available in both rulesets. Against a seated (wrestle-up) guard the passer must manage distance and kill the hips. In the GI you do this with pant grips: the toreando becomes the reflex king (~22-25 gi) and the knee-slice-through stays a strong fundamental, while the bodylock is a modest secondary (~8-12) because cloth already gives you the control the bodylock otherwise buys. In NO-GI there is no cloth to grip, so you must connect chest-to-hip — the body lock is the post-DDS meta answer and roughly doubles to a co-leading ~18-24, drawing attempt share directly out of the toreando (which drops to ~14-19). Everything else (leg drag, both knee slices, bull, long step, smash) stays a mid-to-low common in both frames with only minor grip-driven gi>nogi nudges; Stack Pass sits at the floor in both frames because you cannot stack an upright seated player.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a pure guard pass with no grip- or heel-hook-legality dependence, so all ten are fully available in both gi and no-gi - no zeros, no availability rulings. The gi/no-gi divergence is purely a frequency shift: in the gi the collar/sleeve/pant grips slow the bottom player's elevation, which makes weight-and-pressure answers (pressure pass, pressure-to-half, knee slice) slightly more viable and marginally reduces the need for a speed clear; the pant grip also strengthens leg drag and knee slice. In no-gi the SLX entry is faster and more dangerous, so speed passes (leg drag, knee through) tick up while the slower gi pressure game ticks down a point or two. The core act in both frames is identical - kill the shin connection before elevation - so the generic clear ('Pass Shin-to-Shin Guard') and knee slice lead in both, with the drag/knee-through slightly hotter in no-gi.

The panel accepts both distributions describe the same act sliced differently - the anti-correlation between 'Pass Shin-to-Shin Guard' and 'Knee Through' is expected, not a defect.

'Pass Shin-to-Shin Guard' (generic catch-all clear) and 'Knee Through' are anti-correlated across the panel: legends who front-load one deflate the other because they name overlapping actions. Downstream consumers should be aware these two channels partially describe the same first move.

containers.frame_rationale: This is side-control bottom under a heavy shoulder/crossface pin — a pure grip-agnostic survival scramble with no lapel, collar, or leglock component, so gi and no-gi are essentially mirrored (all 10 R1 notes agree). Every move is available in both rulesets; there are no availability zeros. The only honest divergences are small and mechanical: Technical Stand-up is credited +1 to +2 in no-gi because sweat and the lack of friction/grips let a flattened bottom player slip and post up marginally more often, while the frame-recovery moves (Frame from Shoulder of Justice, Frame Escape) run a hair higher in the gi because the gi crossface is stickier and demands more repeated re-framing before space opens. The structural story is head-heavy: the standalone neutralizing frame (Frame from Shoulder of Justice) is the single most-attempted ACT because nothing escapes until the shoulder is off the jaw, with the systematic bloc (Danaher/Gordon/Lachlan) landing it 17-21 and the practitioner bloc (Mendes/Marcelo/Mikey/Roger/Kade) landing it 12-13 while distributing more volume across the co-equal frame-and-shrimp / elbow / hip guard-recoveries.

removal_candidates.reason: From a flattened, committed shoulder-of-justice pin a true technical stand-up is close to fiction (Lachlan) — it presupposes you have already regained knees/space, which is a different position. Kept at a low floor (3-8) because it is not zero, but it is the weakest genuine attempt from here.

A committed crossface pin specifically kills the bridge-and-roll (the top player's shoulder pressure and sprawl base are designed to defeat it); genuine but low-frequency from THIS pin versus generic side control.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is legal and available in BOTH gi and no-gi — there are no collar-only or heel-hook-type moves, so no per-frame zeros. The gi/no-gi differences are purely meta- and friction-driven. Americana leans gi because the cloth and gripping surface aid the wrist figure-four and the trapped far arm is easier to pin against the mat. Arm Triangle and North-South Choke both lean no-gi: the head-and-arm/head-only strangles feed on sweat, a bare neck, and the absence of a collar that would otherwise offer competing gi finishes — the shoulder pressure that defines this position naturally seals the head-and-arm no-gi. Knee on Belly leans gi, where it is a genuine points-and-pressure attacking hub in the IBJJF meta rather than just a passing waypoint. Side Control to Mount is the unambiguous workhorse in both frames (~18) — this is a promotion engine, not a finishing position — with only a marginal no-gi trim as the slicker torso makes the mount climb a hair less sticky than the gi's frictional control.

containers.frame_rationale: Scarf Hold (kesa-gatame) is a fundamentals escape position with NO ruleset-illegal moves — every escape (bridge-and-roll, hip escape, elbow escape, frame-and-shrimp, ghost, arm-extraction-to-turtle, pummel-out reversal, bridge variants) is legal and mechanically identical in gi and no-gi, so there are no availability zeros and the frames stay near-mirrored. The only honest divergence is that no-gi the pin is slipperier — no lapel/collar anchor for the top player, plus sweat — so escapes that exploit a loosening pin tick UP slightly no-gi: Ghost Escape (+1 to +2) and Arm Extraction to Turtle (+1), with corresponding -1 on hip/elbow escape as the marginal budget shifts. In the gi, top can grip cloth to re-pin, so hip/elbow escapes are attempted at the same rate but complete slightly less; that affects success rate, not attempt frequency, so gi attempt numbers stay marginally higher on the framing escapes. All divergences are ±1-2. Head-heavy shape: Hip Escape to Guard is the clear peak, Elbow Escape and Frame-and-Shrimp behind it, and the three bridge labels sit in the tail to avoid triple-counting a single low-percentage bridging intent.

containers.frame_rationale: Kesa-gatame is a gi/judo-heritage pin, so the gi frame leans slightly more toward holding, grinding the trapped near arm, and walking to mount (Roger's Scarf Hold to Mount runs higher in gi; the Americana is marginally more live in gi where sleeve/wrist control assists the keylock). No move is ruleset-unavailable in either frame — every submission and transition here is fully legal gi and no-gi — so all divergences are gradient, not on/off, and there are zero per-frame zeros.

containers.frame_rationale: Spider guard is a fundamentally gi-native position: its entire structure depends on feet-on-biceps pressure anchored by deep sleeve grips, and its two signature attacks — the balance-breaking Spider Sweep and the Spider-to-Lasso system switch — require cloth to generate the tension and wrap that make them work. In the gi the distribution is genuinely multi-headed (Spider Sweep ~14, Guard Recovery ~12, Spider to Lasso ~12, Triangle Setup ~11, Triangle from Spider ~8). Strip the sleeves and the position degenerates into a transient two-second wrist-control frame that nobody holds; the mass therefore collapses upward onto Guard Recovery (bail to a real guard, ~22-24 no-gi) and the triangle family (Triangle Setup ~16, Triangle from Spider ~11), which still function off the bicep push. Spider to Lasso is a hard zero no-gi (availability), and Spider Sweep drops from workhorse to token (~5) because the balance-break has no grip to load against.

availability_rulings.reason: Lasso guard requires wrapping the sleeve/cloth around the arm; without a sleeve the transfer is structurally impossible. Unanimous hard zero no-gi.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently 2-4% and lowest-tier across all panelists in both frames; not a native spider-guard mechanic (belongs to closed guard). Basically never thrown from a live spider frame.

This is one of the largest gi/no-gi divergences in the corpus: the same position plays as a rich multi-attack guard in gi and a near-nonexistent transient frame in no-gi. Game/UX consumers should ensure the ruleset toggle is respected here or the no-gi opponent will feel wrong.

verify.rationale: Both frames sum to exactly 100. The lone zero (Spider to Lasso, no-gi) has a bulletproof, unanimous availability ruling — lasso mechanically requires wrapping the sleeve, so it is structurally impossible without cloth. The why_selected concern (large top-40 L1 shift from priors) is not a defect: the sealed priors were flat, uncalibrated gi==nogi values that underweighted the actual gi workhorses (Spider Sweep, Spider-to-Lasso, Triangle from Spider) and over-flattened Triangle Setup to a uniform 27; the panel correctly refused to conform. Every gi/no-gi divergence carries a concrete mechanism: Spider Sweep 14->6 (balance-break needs sleeve tension to load), Spider-to-Lasso 12->0 (no cloth), Guard Recovery 12->25 (degenerate no-gi frame => bail to a real guard far more often), and the triangle family lifting no-gi (triangle fires off the bicep push, which survives sleeve removal). Rank order is one a spider-guard coach (Mendes' home turf) would recognize — Spider Sweep and the Lasso switch as gi signatures. Head mass is coherent: gi top-5 = 56, no-gi top-5 = 68, and the tighter no-gi concentration correctly reflects the position collapsing to fewer live options. The one friction point flagged in deliberation — the no-gi triangle family reaching 37 combined — is defensible: it tracks a high-dispersion panel mean faithfully and no single reallocation is compelling enough to override the colleague panel. All 15 proposed_final values track their panel means to within rounding. Accept as proposed.

containers.frame_rationale: The entire gi/no-gi divergence in Spider Guard passing is driven by sleeve presence, not by rule legality — no move in this pack is ruleset-illegal, so there are zero availability rulings and every move carries a nonzero number in both frames. In the gi, Spider Guard cannot be passed without first stripping the sleeve grips and feet-on-biceps structure, so the grip-strip 'Spider Guard Pass' is the attempt head (~22) and the leg weave (the structural spider killer) plus knee slice ride high; the toreando is attempted a lot but only as a second action after the grip war, so it sits middling (~15). In no-gi the sleeves that define the guard are gone, feet-on-biceps slips, and the position collapses into generic open-guard passing: the toreando becomes the clear head (~26), leg drag and knee slice rise on scrambles, while the sleeve-dependent Spider Guard Pass and Leg Weave drop to single digits (the motion still exists against a shirt/miming opponent, hence ~8-13 rather than 0).

removal_candidates.reason: Kneeling entry into extended-arm feet-on-biceps control is a near non-starter from spider in both rulesets — floored at 4-6 by the whole panel, weakest attempt in the position.

containers.frame_rationale: Squid guard is a lapel-defined bottom position: you feed your own lapel behind the opponent's near leg to build an asymmetric tilting wedge. In the gi this produces a genuinely head-heavy distribution with one clear peak — the eponymous Squid Guard Sweep (~21-25) — supported by the omoplata family (the trapped arm the position hands you) and by grip-driven berimbolo/DLR reactions, plus honest recovery. In no-gi the lapel wrap cannot be held, so the two lapel-native moves (Squid Guard Sweep, Squid to Ringworm Guard) are unavailable (hard 0) and the state degrades into generic supine open guard. There is no single no-gi peak; instead the mass redistributes into a broad head of Single Leg X, X-Guard, and Guard Recovery (~18-24 each — the classic get-under-or-retain triad), with a secondary inversion where De La Riva actually rises no-gi (the hand is no longer committed to the lapel) while Berimbolo falls (no collar/belt to spin off). Omoplata/Triangle survive no-gi at modest weight since arm/head control does not need cloth.

availability_rulings.reason: The eponymous sweep IS the lapel-tilt mechanism — you feed your own lapel behind the opponent's leg to create the tilting wedge. With no cloth the move does not exist; set to 0 no-gi.
Ringworm guard is a gi lapel/collar guard and the transfer from squid to ringworm is a lapel re-wrap. No lapel to transfer means the move is unavailable no-gi; set to 0.

removal_candidates.reason: A niche lapel-to-lapel guard transfer that only lives in gi and only from a rare position; near-zero real occurrence outside dedicated lapel-game specialists. Keep for now but it is the weakest edge on the node.

Low-frequency terminal link of the omoplata chain from an already-rare position; situational in both frames (gi ~6-8, no-gi ~5) and largely subsumed by Omoplata Sweep. Candidate for folding into the omoplata family.

flags: no-gi node semi-fictional: the position is lapel-defined, so 'Squid Guard/Bottom' in no-gi is really degraded generic open guard — Craig held this objection and it is logged; the distribution is retained only because the game engine must move an opponent standing in this state.

old SEALED site values were uniform-smeared (all moves 10-13) and inverted the peak — they put the defining Squid Guard Sweep at just 5 (gi) and Ringworm at 3, and applied identical gi==nogi numbers ignoring the lapel-death entirely; the panel's head-heavy gi distribution and hard no-gi zeros deliberately override this.
two hard no-gi zeros (Squid Guard Sweep, Squid to Ringworm Guard) both logged in availability_rulings as genuine lapel-dependent unavailability, not 'rare'.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Roger/Mendes + Statistician) tried and failed to break the distribution. Sums verified 100/100. The two hard no-gi zeros (Squid Guard Sweep = lapel-tilt wedge; Squid to Ringworm = lapel-to-lapel transfer) are definitionally cloth-dependent, so 0 no-gi is airtight mechanism, not 'rare' — this fully justifies the flagged Sigma|delta|=76 that got the container selected. The gi/no-gi divergences each carry a mechanism: peak death of the two lapel moves collapses 32 gi points into a get-under-or-reset triad (Single Leg X 20 / X-Guard 19 / Guard Recovery 23), and the De La Riva-up (6->9, hand freed off the lapel) / Berimbolo-down (8->5, no collar/belt to spin) inversion is standard and correct. Rank orders are coach-recognizable in both frames: gi leads with the eponymous sweep (23) then honest recovery and the trapped-arm omoplata family; nogi leads with recovery + underhook entries. Head-mass gi top5=64 fits a one-signature-sweep guard; nogi top5=80 is high but MECHANICALLY FORCED by the two legitimate zeros, not over-concentration. Every proposed value tracks its panel_mean within rounding with low dispersion (panel agreement). The strongest challenges (gi SLX/X-Guard at 8, gi DLR at 6) were withdrawn as consistent with the frame rationale — the outside hand is committed to the lapel in gi, suppressing DLR and X entries there. The residual nogi-semi-fictional caveat is already logged as a flag and argues for engine-completeness retention with a large honest recovery bucket, not for changing any number.

containers.frame_rationale: Squid Guard is a jacket-only (Keenan-lineage) lapel guard: the bottom player wraps the passer's leg with their own lapel to build an asymmetric leg entanglement from an inverted base. In the GI the distribution is head-heavy on position-specific answers — the dedicated strip (Pass Squid Guard, ~20) is the workhorse, backed by Back Step off the wrapped leg (~14), Stack Pass on the inverted player (~12), and Pressure Through (~13), while lapel-trapping the passer's leg suppresses running passes (Toreando drops to ~7, Leg Drag ~9). In NO-GI the guard essentially cannot form — no lapel, no wrap — so the two dedicated moves are DEGRADED to a floor (Pass Squid ~5-11, Pressure Through ~4-7; not zeroed because a squid-shaped shin entanglement can still be attacked rarely) and the frame collapses into generic open-guard movement passing led by Toreando (~18-19), Leg Drag (~15), and Knee Slice (~15-17). Every divergence is mechanism-driven (the lapel traps the passer's leg, gating run-by passes and enabling dedicated strips), so no move is ruleset-illegal and no availability zero is warranted.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is a legal, available pass (or generic pass/takedown node) in BOTH rulesets, so there are no availability zeros — all divergence is magnitude, mechanism-backed. The gi taxes the toreando: opponent grips (sleeve/collar/pants) slow the circling sprint-pass, so its attempt share drops slightly gi and rises no-gi where friction and grip-free hips make it the lowest-commitment first option (its no-gi success advantage reinforces the attempt lean). Mirror-image, the double-under pass skews gi because the pants give something to stack and hold, while legs slip out no-gi. Knee slice edges gi (collar/lapel/cross-face pin sticks the slice), leg drag edges no-gi (clean back-line, no gi to stall the drag). Stack pass is near-flat with an honest minority split (Bravo leans it no-gi for the unstalled bulldoze, Mendes leans it gi for the pant clamp), so it aggregates roughly even. The head stays the toreando/knee-slice/leg-drag trinity (~45% combined) in both frames; the situational footwork tail (X pass, long step, back step) and the two generic catch-all nodes fill an honest, non-smeared remainder.

containers.frame_rationale: The gi/no-gi split from Standing/Top is driven almost entirely by grip legality. Leg-lock entry pulls (shin-to-shin, single-leg-X) tilt up no-gi as deliberate paths into the leg game. The one hard availability zero is Collar Drag in no-gi: no collar, no move. Everything else that is 'rare' stays at a 1-3 floor rather than 0, because those actions are physically possible in both rulesets, just seldom chosen.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger Gracie, Marcelo Garcia, Gordon Ryan + The Statistician) ran the container through 4 hostile rounds and could not break it. (1) why_selected concern (over-populated hub): the 35-move hub sums to exactly 100/100 in both frames; the top-5 head-mass is low (37% gi / 38% nogi), but this flatness is structural for a genuine 35-branch decision point, not an allocation error, and the head is correctly ordered in both frames (gi: Guard Pull >> wrestling/judo cluster; nogi: Single Leg > Double Leg > Guard Pull ~ Snap Down). (2) Zeros: the only zero is Collar Drag nogi, backed by a bulletproof availability ruling (no collar to grip) with panel-majority citation; no illegitimate zeros. (4) Rank order is recognizable to coaches of Standing/Top in both rulesets. (5) The flagged submissions from clean standing (Flying Kneebar, Kimura, Reverse Kimura) are correctly floor-kept at 1-2 rather than zeroed, since they are physically possible-but-rare, matching the '1-3 floor not 0' rule. Defense (fighting the locked hands and re-facing) is the dominant workhorse in both frames and is essentially frame-flat. The Standing Switch is attempted somewhat MORE in no-gi (no jacket friction pinning you to the opponent, plus the wrestler bloodline that lives in no-gi) - the lone exception is Roger, who sees gi grips enabling a rotational switch. The Counter Throw is attempted somewhat MORE in the gi, because judo-style grips give a concrete handle to launch a standing throw off the opponent's clinch; without a jacket that path is harder and rarer no-gi. These two divergences (switch up no-gi, counter-throw up gi) roughly offset within the large Defense head, so total per-frame shape stays similar with Defense >> Switch > Counter Throw.

Available - grip-break-and-face defense is the dominant response in both rulesets.

containers.frame_rationale: Turtle-bottom is the site's cleanest gi/no-gi fork, and the fork is entirely one of degree, not availability — all nine exits exist in both rulesets, so no per-frame zeros apply. The driver is grip friction: in the gi, collar and sleeve grips plus the clock-choke/back-exposure threat make turtle a static re-guard position, so Rolling to Guard and Sit Through to Guard hold the largest share and Granby / standing exits are damped. In no-gi there are no grips to pin you, so turtle becomes a wrestling corridor — Technical Stand-up, Turtle to Standing, Sit Out, and Granby all shift up while the re-guard rolls recede. Sit Out from Turtle is the cross-frame workhorse; Deep Half Entry and Peterson Roll are the honest tail in both frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Diving into deep half from a defensive turtle is a low-percentage, rarely-attempted entry (panel consensus situational-to-rare, ~4-6). Kept for now but flagged as the weakest exit from this role.
Lands at side-control/top — a giving-position roll that concedes rather than escapes; low attempt frequency in both frames (~6-8). Situational at best; candidate for future pruning.

flags: Genuinely broad multi-exit position: top-3 carries only ~40-43%, no single dominant move — this is correct for turtle (a scramble corridor), not a smear artifact.

Sanity-diff: old uncalibrated site values had four gross role-misreads the panel corrects — Sit Out underweighted (6 -> ~15), Deep Half Entry overweighted (14 -> ~5), Turtle to Standing underweighted (7 -> ~13 nogi), Peterson Roll overweighted (12 -> ~7). Did not conform to sealed values.
Every gi/no-gi divergence is same-signed and grip-mechanistic (re-guard rolls up in gi; stand-ups/granby/sit-out up in no-gi); no unexplained forks.

containers.frame_rationale: Turtle top is the single biggest gi/no-gi fork in this batch. In BOTH frames the head of the distribution is identical mechanics: get to the back (Turtle to Back Control ~18-23, plus Chair Sit and the Turtle Attack Sequence) or flatten the opponent out to side control (~11-15) — together roughly two-thirds of all attempts. The fork is entirely in the finishing layer. In the GI the collar is a weapon, so the Clock Choke (~9-13) is a genuine workhorse and the Loop Choke (~4-6) is live; those collar attacks are hard zeros in no-gi with no lapel to grip, logged as availability rulings. That freed no-gi mass flows into the collarless front-headlock chain — the Darce (gi ~4 → nogi ~8-11) and Anaconda (gi ~3 → nogi ~6-8) swell substantially — plus the modern funk rides (Truck/Matrix/Rodeo) which are slightly more attempted in no-gi's elite meta. Gi also nudges the flatten and chair-sit up marginally because collar-and-pants grips aid control. Everything else (direct kimura/armbar/arm-triangle submissions, Boston crab, the obscure Aoki/Russian Cowboy rides, Kiss of the Dragon) is honest tail in both frames.

availability_rulings.reason: Collar-dependent choke — the clock choke pulls the opponent's own lapel/collar across the throat. With no gi there is no collar to grip, so it is genuinely unavailable in no-gi. Nine of ten legends zeroed it; the two who gave 1 conceded a true zero on reflection.
Collar-dependent choke — the loop choke wraps and loops the opponent's collar. No collar in no-gi means no mechanism; unanimous hard zero.

Fringe funk ride, panel tail 1-2; sealed site value (9) grossly overweights it. Candidate for removal or merge.
Very low-frequency back-take flair (panel 1-2 both frames); real but essentially never the primary attempt from turtle top.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site values are structurally wrong here and were NOT conformed to. Site grossly UNDERWEIGHTED three central moves — Clock Choke (site 1 vs panel gi ~10, the signature gi turtle attack), Turtle Flatten to Side Control (site 5 vs panel ~13), and Chair Sit to Back (site 3 vs panel ~10) — and OVERWEIGHTED obscure rides Turtle to Russian Cowboy (site 9 vs panel ~1) and Turtle to Aoki Lock (site 7 vs panel ~1-2). Site also ran the single head move (Turtle to Back 54) spammy-high; panel centralizes it near 20.

Front-headlock chain (Darce/Anaconda) shows the largest legitimate gi→nogi swell, driven by collar removal redirecting finishing mass.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger Gracie / Marcelo Garcia / John Danaher + The Statistician) pressure-tested a distribution whose why_selected flagged a full 100% L1 shift off grossly miscalibrated site priors (Back 54, Clock Choke 1, Russian Cowboy 9, Aoki 7). The panel got the hard part right: centralizing the spammy Back Control (54->~22), restoring the Clock Choke as the signature GI turtle attack (gi 11, hard nogi=0), and demoting the obscure Russian Cowboy/Aoki rides to honest tail. Zeros scrutinized: Clock Choke nogi=0 and Loop Choke nogi=0 both carry bulletproof collar-dependency rulings (the collarless analog mass is correctly re-homed to the separately-listed Darce/Anaconda front-headlock chain), so they survive. ONE defect survives verification: Boston Crab from Turtle proposed gi=0 / nogi=1 is an UNPRINCIPLED asymmetric zero — Boston Crab has no gi/no-gi mechanical dependency (it is a spinal/leg control, collar-irrelevant), so a gi=0 with nogi=1 is a rounding artifact that manufactures a fake availability zero. Corrected to gi=1 to match nogi=1 and eliminate the illegitimate zero; to hold sum-to-100 the head move Turtle to Back Control gi is trimmed 23->22 (still within rounding of its panel mean 22.65). Bounded two-cell correction, 17/19 moves accepted as-is — the panel's work stands.

Trim gi 23->22 (still within rounding of panel mean 22.65) to preserve sum=100 after restoring Boston Crab gi=1; nogi unchanged.

Proposed gi=0/nogi=1 is an unprincipled asymmetric zero. Boston Crab is a spinal/leg control with no collar dependency, so there is no availability mechanism for a gi zero; the 0.0 gi panel mean is a central-tendency/rounding artifact. Symmetric 1/1 restores legitimacy.

containers.frame_rationale: Twister Control escapes are body-mechanic movements (clearing the trapped near leg, rolling through the spinal rotation, framing back to guard) rather than grip-dependent techniques, so gi and no-gi are near-identical here. The small, justified divergences all run one way: no-gi slightly favors the scramble-and-invert options (Scramble to Guard, Granby Roll, and Roll Through) because the absence of grip friction lets the defender spin and slip out faster, while the gi slightly favors the methodical Hip Escape to Guard, where jacket friction and frames let the defender grind the trapped leg free without a clean explosive extraction. No move is ruleset-locked, so there are no availability zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Panel judges it a redundant, worse version of Roll Through Escape / Bridge and Turn to Turtle - it accomplishes the same rotation-kill with a lower success rate (gi 37.6 / nogi 30.4). Craig ranked it rare; kept in the tail for now but flagged for possible folding into Roll Through.

flags: Largest R1 disagreement (spread 10) is Leg Extraction: leg-lock/truck-mechanics camp (Craig/Bravo/Mendes ~17-18) treats freeing the trapped leg as THE priority, while pace camp (Roger/Kade ~9-10) counts it as a byproduct of rolling rather than a discrete attempt. Final distribution keeps it as a co-lead with an honest low tail rather than averaging the split away.

Possible double-count between Leg Extraction and Roll Through Escape / Bridge and Turn to Turtle - all three ultimately free the trapped leg and kill the spinal rotation; treated as distinct discrete attempts here but worth monitoring.

Sanity-diff: old site values under-weighted Leg Extraction (12) and over-weighted Defensive Roll (11) and Bridge and Turn to Turtle (14); the panel's head-heavier Roll-Through / Leg-Extraction shape is intentional and was not conformed to the old numbers.

containers.frame_rationale: The single dominant driver of gi/no-gi divergence here is IBJJF legality, not mechanics. No-gi, Twister Control exists to hit the twister, so the twister co-leads with the back take (~32/~22) as the two headline attempts. In the IBJJF gi the twister and neck crank are banned spinal locks and the calf slicer is belt-restricted, so the same physical control gets mined for its legal exits: the back take becomes the clear gi leader (~32, even higher than no-gi because collar/trapped-arm grips ease the climb) with the guillotine as the strong second legal path (~24). The twister and neck crank stay suppressed but non-zero in gi (not availability-zeroed) because sub-only and ADCC-format gi events permit them; the calf slicer stays a real situational option for the advanced gi population that plays this position.

availability_rulings.reason: IBJJF-banned spinal lock — SUPPRESSED not unavailable. Kept 6-18 (not 0) because sub-only and ADCC-format gi events permit it; illegal in the mainline IBJJF gi population which dominates the weighting.
IBJJF-banned spinal lock like the twister — SUPPRESSED not unavailable. Kept 6-9 (not 0) for the same non-IBJJF gi rulesets; must sit below the twister in gi for coherence since the same ban applies.

IBJJF gi-restricted — illegal below brown belt, legal at brown/black (no heel reaping). Not zeroed: legal for the advanced gi population this position targets, so it stays a genuine situational option ~12-18.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-occurrence move in both frames (gi ~8, nogi ~13) and mechanically a near-duplicate of the twister's spinal-rotation finish — it is rarely a distinct deliberate attempt from this control rather than a byproduct of a failed twister. Logged for review, NOT removed now.

flags: SEALED old site values were flat gi==nogi across all five moves (Twister 35, Back 25, Guillotine 15, NeckCrank 13, Calf 12) — they entirely miss the legality-driven gi/no-gi divergence that is this position's defining feature, and under-weight the gi Back Take (25 vs panel ~32) and gi Guillotine (15 vs ~24). Panel did not conform.

R1 gi disagreement on the Twister (8-28) was the largest spread and traced to whether legends priced an IBJJF-weighted gi population (low) vs sub-only/ADCC-format gi (high); resolved toward IBJJF-weighted ~12 with Craig/Bravo holding modestly higher.

Coherence fix applied: several R1 ballots had gi Neck Crank approx equal to no-gi despite the neck crank being IBJJF-banned exactly like the twister; final ballots suppress gi Neck Crank below the gi Twister.

This is a submission_control position (5 moves, 4 submissions + 1 back-take) — distribution is legitimately head-heavy on Back Take/Twister/Guillotine; the two-move tail (Neck Crank, Calf Slicer) is honestly thin, not a smear.

verify.rationale: Both frames sum to exactly 100 (gi 14+35+26+9+16; nogi 33+22+18+13+14). Every proposed value sits on or within rounding distance of its panel mean, and every gi/no-gi divergence carries a bulletproof mechanism: the IBJJF ban on the twister and neck crank (rotary spinal locks) suppresses those moves in gi and redistributes their mass into the legal exits, which is why gi Back Take (35), Guillotine (26) and even Calf Slicer (16) run higher than no-gi while gi Twister (14) and gi Neck Crank (9) run lower. The neck-crank coherence constraint from R1 holds (gi crank 9 < gi twister 14, same ban applies). No bare zeros exist — every suppressed move keeps a floor per the availability rulings, correctly treating IBJJF suppression as 'illegal in the dominant population' rather than 'physically unavailable in every gi ruleset'. Rank orders are coach-recognizable in both frames: no-gi Twister>Back>Guillotine (the Eddie Bravo twister-system decision tree) and gi Back>Guillotine>Calf>Twister (the legal re-mining of the same control). Head mass (top-3 ~74%) is honest head-heaviness for a 5-move submission_control position. Two contested points were argued and both resolved to accept: (1) gi Twister at 14 vs the flag's stated R1 resolution of ~12 — 14 is simply the panel mean 13.51 correctly rounded, sits 0.16sigma above mean, and pulling it to 12 would need an unmotivated +2 elsewhere; (2) Calf Slicer gi 16 > nogi 14 inversion — thin but backed by the same suppressed-twister redistribution that lifted Back Take and Guillotine, within tight dispersion. Correcting either would be redoing the colleague panel's work, not fixing an error. The why_selected Back Take crosscheck (spread 32) is satisfied by convergence: final Back Take dispersions are tight (gi 2.88, nogi 0.82) and finals sit on the means (35 vs 35.37, 22 vs 22.01).

containers.frame_rationale: Bottom Truck is a grip-agnostic leg-entanglement escape problem: the attacker has your near leg triangled and threatens twister, calf slicer, banana split, and the back. No move in this list depends on lapel/collar grips, and none is gi-illegal (no heel hooks here), so gi and no-gi share nearly the same head-heavy shape — the two leg-extraction lines dominate both frames. The one real, mechanism-backed divergence is the Back Door Escape running higher in no-gi (~11 vs ~9 gi): with no gi friction to slow the attacker's finish and a more acute calf-slicer threat, the bottom player rolls under faster and more often. A minor secondary lean has Defensive Roll and turtle-bailing exits slightly higher in the gi, where grips slow the follow-up back-take and make the conservative bail safer; no-gi that same bail is riskier against fast back-takers. Everything else tracks gi==nogi.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-frequency line on the board (panel lands ~5). A genuine but expert-only counter-roll for the attacker's back while triangled — it happens rarely, so it is a tail move, not a removal. Logged only; kept.

Mechanically near-impossible while the near leg is still triangled (Marcelo/Mikey); only viable in the narrow window before the lock sets. Low frequency (~7) but real — kept, flagged as a candidate to watch if it stays consistently bottom-tier.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: old site values were badly miscalibrated — Granby Roll to Guard was 42 (making a mechanically-hard, situational move the entire position) while the two central leg-extraction lines were starved at 3 (from Truck) and 12 (to Guard), and Escape/Hip Escape from Truck sat at 3-4. The panel inverts this to extraction-dominant, which is the correct reading of a trapped-leg escape menu. Did not conform to the old numbers.

Low R1 dispersion (mean CV 0.122) — near-consensus that leg extraction dominates; genuine (not fake) consensus, confirmed by mechanism, with the only live debates on Leg Extraction to Guard (12-18) and Back Door Escape (6-12), both resolved on mechanism grounds rather than difference-splitting.
No availability zeros required — every move is legal and mechanically available in both rulesets.

verify.rationale: Bottom Truck is a pure trapped-leg-extraction escape menu with no grip-dependent moves and no gi-illegal finishes, so the near gi==nogi collapse is mechanically justified. Sums are exact (100/100) and panel means sum to ~100. Head-mass top-5 = 62% in both frames, appropriate for a menu of ten near-fungible escape variants (not a submission-heavy tree wanting 75%+). Rank order survives adversarial review by a Truck-escape coach: the two leg-extraction lines lead (extraction is mechanically forced before guard recovery), the escape/hip-escape cluster sits mid-pack, and Granby/Rolling-Back-Take/Back-Door trail. The SANITY-DIFF flag is correct: the old priors were inverted (Granby Roll 42 as the whole position, extraction lines starved at 3) and the panel's extraction-dominant reading is the right one. No zeros exist and none should — every move is legal and available in both rulesets. The only two forks are mechanism-backed and ≤2 points: Back Door Escape higher no-gi (+2, faster finish tempo / more acute calf-slicer without gi friction forces rolling-under sooner) and Defensive Roll / Escape slightly higher gi (+1, grip-slowed follow-up makes the conservative bail safer). Panelists could not break any allocation; the two near-ties (extraction from-Truck vs to-Guard, Rolling Back Take gi/nogi) are within noise and harmless.

containers.frame_rationale: The Truck (top) is fundamentally a no-gi position, and the gi/no-gi split is driven by three mechanism-level factors. (1) Collar dependence: Bow and Arrow Choke needs a gi collar, so it is a gi-only finish (nogi=0, availability) and instead absorbs a real ~9-11% of the gi attempt budget. (2) IBJJF leg/spine legality: the twister finish and spinal locks are banned and the calf slicer is belt-gated in the gi, so the entire no-gi leg/spine cluster (Twister Entry ~13-15, Calf Slicer ~15, Banana Split ~8, Spine Lock ~2-3) collapses in the gi — Twister Entry drops to a 2-4% scramble artifact, Spine Lock to 0-1, Calf Slicer to ~7-8. (3) Grip friction: gi grips make the ride slightly stickier (maintenance a touch higher) and also make conventional collar-driven back control preferable to riding, so the gi column funnels its freed budget into Truck Maintenance, Truck to Back Control, and Bow and Arrow. Net effect: no-gi is leg-and-twister-hunt-heavy on top of the two control workhorses; gi is control-and-back-take-heavy with a collar finish and a suppressed-to-zero leg/spine tail. The two workhorses (Truck Maintenance ~20, Truck to Back Control ~15) dominate both frames — the position is a ride first, a submission platform second.

availability_rulings.move: Bow and Arrow Choke from Truck
availability_rulings.reason: Collar/lapel choke — requires the gi. No collar in no-gi means the move cannot be attempted, so nogi=0 across all 10 legends. Its attempt share reallocates to the leg/spine cluster and maintenance.

IBJJF (and most gi rulesets) ban spinal/cervical locks. Effectively unavailable in gi competition — scored 0 by strict-IBJJF voices (Danaher, Mendes) and 1 by the rest to reflect rare non-IBJJF gi rulesets. Soft availability: suppressed to 0-1, not fully removed.

Partial-availability, NOT a hard 0. The twister FINISH is IBJJF-illegal, but ENTERING twister control as a scramble/back-take vehicle is not itself banned. Suppressed to 2-4 in gi (scramble artifact only), never zeroed.

Partial-availability, NOT a 0. Legal only at brown/black belt in IBJJF gi, so gi attempt share is suppressed (~7-8) relative to no-gi (~14-16), but remains nonzero because it is legal and hit at advanced gi levels.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the lowest non-availability move (1-2 both frames across all 10 legends). It is a turtle-phase entry that sits awkwardly inside a truck-top move list — arguably belongs to a turtle/crucifix node, not the truck. Basically never attempted FROM an established truck. Logged, not removed.

This is an ENTRY into the truck, not an action taken FROM truck-top; scoring it as an in-position attempt double-counts arrival. Panel keeps it low (2-6) but flags it as a likely mis-homed move that describes getting to the position rather than what you do once there.

Near-universally illegal (spinal lock) and, even where legal, very rarely the chosen attempt versus calf slicer / banana split. Floor-level everywhere (0-4). Candidate for folding into a generic spine-attack note rather than a standalone weighted move.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: the sealed current-site values grossly UNDERWEIGHTED the two true workhorses (Truck Maintenance=3, Truck to Back Control=2) and grossly OVERWEIGHTED Rolling Back Take=20. The panel's correction is large and deliberate: Maintenance/Back-Control up to ~20/~15, Rolling Back Take down to ~4-5. Old values also used identical gi=nogi numbers (no ruleset fork) — the panel forks every ruleset-sensitive move.
Old site values had no gi/no-gi divergence at all (13/13, 20/20, etc.); this ballot introduces the frame fork, most sharply on Twister Entry, Calf Slicer, Bow and Arrow, and Spine Lock.

Four distinct 'go to the back' moves coexist (Rolling Back Take, Crab Ride to Back, Back Take from Top, Truck to Back Control). Risk of double-counting the back-conversion action; panel deliberately made Truck to Back Control the dominant conversion (~15) and kept the other three modest to avoid smearing.
Bravo dissents high on Twister Entry (nogi 19 vs panel ~13); retained as authentic minority signal, not smoothed to consensus.
Two moves (Roll to Truck, Crucifix from Turtle) are arguably ENTRIES/adjacent-position actions rather than true from-truck-top attempts — flagged as possible mis-homed moves for the graph maintainer.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Roger, Marcelo, Danaher + Statistician) ran 4 rounds attacking the proposed Truck-top distribution and could not break it. Sums are exact (gi=100, nogi=100). Head-mass is coherent: top-5 shares 68 gi / 70 nogi — head-heavy but non-degenerate, which is right for a ride-first control position with a clear top-2 workhorse (Truck Maintenance, Truck to Back Control). ATTACK 1 (L1 head shift): the large correction moving mass into the two workhorses is the honest fix — the sealed prior grossly underweighted them (3/2) and overweighted Rolling Back Take (20). Sustained. ATTACK 2 (zeroed Bow and Arrow nogi): bulletproof hard-availability zero — no collar exists in no-gi, the lapel choke is unattemptable. The only contested cell was the gi side: Roger argued gi=10 slightly overstates a direct-from-truck collar choke (really a two-step go-to-back-then-choke path) and preferred ~8-9; but the panel converged tight there (dispersion 1.11, mean 10.31), the reallocation is <=2 pts within noise, and moving it would only widen an already-large control head — held at 10. ATTACK 3 (unexplained divergences): every gi/no-gi fork is mechanism-backed — collar dependence (B&A), IBJJF spinal/cervical-lock ban (Spine Lock, twister finish), brown/black belt-gate (Calf Slicer), grip friction (Maintenance gi>nogi). ATTACK 4 (rank order): the no-gi order Maintenance 19 then a Twister Entry / Truck to Back Control / Calf Slicer tie at 14 is exactly what a 10th-Planet truck specialist would draw — the twister and calf slicer are the position's signature finishes. Bravo's high Twister-Entry dissent (nogi 19) correctly lost to the general-population panel mean (14). ATTACK 5 (four back-conversion nodes): genuine double-count risk, but the panel already made Truck to Back Control dominant and suppressed the other three — a graph node-merge concern for the maintainer, not a distribution error. No cell warrants a bounded correction.

containers.frame_rationale: No move in this pack is ruleset-unavailable — every escape (frame, shrimp, hip escape, granby roll, rolling, technical stand-up, turn-in, arm extraction) is legal and mechanically available in both gi and no-gi, so there are no zeros or availability restrictions. All gi/no-gi divergences are magnitude-only (=2 points) and mechanism-justified: no-gi is slipperier with no collar/sleeve grips, so scramble exits (Granby Roll +1-2, Rolling +1) rise in no-gi; the gi's grip friction lets the bottom commit harder to a single escape and modestly rewards the post-and-stand, so Technical Stand-up sits a touch higher in the gi (Roger) and the two workhorse escapes complete marginally more cleanly. Everything else is near-mirrored across frames.

removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically the same frame-to-half-guard motion as 'Frame and Shrimp to Guard' / 'Hip Escape to Guard' — a position-specific label on the standard shrimp. Candidate for future consolidation to avoid triple-counting the same escape; NOT removed now, retained per protocol.

Generic 'escape to turtle' label that overlaps conceptually with 'Arm Extraction to Turtle' (same landing) and the shrimp family; a catch-all rather than a distinct technique. Logged as a consolidation candidate, not removed.

Lowest-frequency exit in the pack (panel floor 6-9); you cannot stand from a live pin, only after framing to space, so it is nearly always a follow-on rather than a primary escape attempt from this state. Real but marginal — logged, not removed.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: legacy SEALED site values had a corrupted head — 'Arm Extraction to Turtle' inflated to 31 (single largest bar, exceeding the true workhorses) while the actual workhorses 'Hip Escape' (13) and 'Frame and Shrimp' (14) were suppressed and the named exits starved to near-zero (Escape TSC 4, Frame-from-TSC 2, Turn-In 1). Panel rejects the old head as a role-misread; corrected to head-heavy shape with the two shrimp/hip-escape workhorses leading (~16-17) and Arm Extraction returned to mid-tail (~8-10).

REDUNDANCY: this pack carries 3-4 mechanically overlapping recomposition moves (Frame and Shrimp to Guard, Hip Escape to Guard, Frame from Twister Side Control, and partly Escape Twister Side Control) that are variants of the same frame-and-shrimp motion; attempt frequency is deliberately split across them rather than stacked, but they are strong future-consolidation candidates.

TURN-IN TRUCK-FEED: 'Turn In from Twister Side Control' turns the bottom toward a top player whose entire game is the twister/truck, so its success rate is depressed here relative to a generic pin even though its attempt frequency stays mid-pack; Marcelo dissents high (12, believes in turn-in-to-half), Craig/Gordon caution it feeds the truck.

R1 SMEAR: the seed ballots were nearly uniform (mean CV 0.111, all moves 6-16); the panel deliberately separated a clear top-2 (~34% combined) from the tail to satisfy head-heaviness so the opponent AI does not play mushy.

containers.frame_rationale: The dominant gi/no-gi fork here is legality, not grips. Twister side control is a launchpad whose actual job is back access, front-headlock chokes (darce/anaconda), and feeding the truck for spine/leg attacks. No-gi, the namesake twister is a live iconic finish (~9-10) and the truck/calf-slicer/anaconda line all tick up, because that is where the 10th-Planet game legally lives. In the gi the twister is a spinal lock disallowed by IBJJF (and calf slicer is brown/black-only), so that attempt mass collapses and redistributes into the back-take, the kimura, and plain positional advances (mount, north-south, shoulder of justice) — the gi rewards the grip-anchored control shuffle relatively more precisely because the flashy no-gi finishes are unavailable or restricted. Darce/anaconda tilt slightly no-gi (less arm friction, and the gi has competing collar chokes), while the back-take remains the single modal attempt in BOTH frames since the back is the highest-value target the position was designed to reach.

availability_rulings.reason: Restricted-not-banned: the twister is a spinal lock disallowed in IBJJF gi and most mainstream gi rulesets, but it remains legal in some gi sub-only/superfight formats and is actively trained in the gi, so it is scored a rare 2-4 (rare-not-zero) rather than a hard 0.

containers.frame_rationale: Vaporizer is a 10th-Planet lockdown/electric-chair construct that barely appears in gi competition, so the gi frame is a thinner reality but keeps the same head-heavy shape rather than smearing. Electric Chair Transition and Lockdown Recovery skew no-gi (10P core, grip-free, faster without friction), while Old School Sweep and Closed Guard to Omoplata skew gi (grip-aided, and in the gi you funnel less into the chair so the old-school sweep absorbs the load); Half Guard to Back Take, Escape Vaporizer, and Roll from Vaporizer are roughly frame-neutral. No collar/lapel or gi-illegal (heel-hook) moves exist in this pack, so there are no true availability zeros - every move is mechanically legal in both frames.

availability_rulings.reason: Available and legal in the gi but rarely the plan there - the position is a 10th-Planet no-gi construct, so gi attempts are lower, not zero. Kept at low-to-mid teens, never 0.

containers.frame_rationale: Vaporizer is a 10th-Planet lockdown variant that lives natively in no-gi, but from the TOP the menu barely diverges by ruleset: the top player is defending the persistent sweep threat and knee-slicing/smashing the trapped leg free in both frames. No move is lapel/collar-dependent or illegal in either ruleset, so there are no availability zeros. The only honest divergences are (1) Whizzer, attempted a shade more no-gi because the back-transition off an over-committed sweep is cleaner without a collar to stall it, and (2) Knee Slice, a whisker higher gi for grip-steered players. Everything else mirrors between frames.

Fully available in both frames; a whisker higher gi for grip-steered players (collar/sleeve helps direct the slice). Logged as a minor justified divergence, not a zero.

containers.frame_rationale: Williams Guard is one of the rare guards where gi and no-gi genuinely converge: its engine is a friction-independent shoulder pin and body-connection posture kill, not grips, so the panel keeps the two frames near-mirror. The divergences are all small (1-3 pts) and mechanism-justified: the Omoplata Sweep leans gi because friction helps complete the spin-under and finish the reversal; the Triangle Setup ticks up in no-gi (a sweaty locked neck and fewer collar/grip escapes for the defender); Kimura to Back Take is marginally higher no-gi (no sleeve/wrist grip to defend the trap); and the Belly Down Armbar is a hair higher in the gi where friction helps hold the belly-down rotation. No move is lapel/collar-dependent and none is a heel hook, so there are no ruleset-unavailability zeros.

removal_candidates.reason: Generically-labeled back path that competes with two more specific back routes (Omoplata to Back, Kimura to Back Take) both landing at back-control/top; it is the lowest-volume of the three and may be redundant, but it still happens (tail floor ~7-8), so it is logged, not removed.

flags: namesake-threat-vs-attempt: 'Williams Shoulder Lock' is threatened almost every exchange but converted to a committed finishing attempt far less often; panel landed it mid-teens (below the Triangle workhorse), preserving Gordon-high / Lachlan-Kade-low dissent.

structural-redundancy: two named arm-attacks (Williams Shoulder Lock + Belly Down Armbar) share the SAME trapped arm; both sit moderate only because they are the primary vs fallback finish off one control, not two independent threats.
back-take-cluster: three moves (Omoplata to Back, Kimura to Back Take, Back Take from Bottom) all resolve to back-control/top; ranked in descending honesty rather than tied to avoid a mushy tail.

sanity-diff: old site values had the head/tail inverted vs the panel - old Triangle 12 badly underweighted the position's #1 workhorse (panel ~20) and old Omoplata to Back 17 overweighted a tail back-door (panel ~10); old Belly Down Armbar 3 was too low (panel ~10). Panel did NOT conform; Sweep (~17-18) and Shoulder Lock (~15) matched the old data closely.
