containers.frame_rationale: Williams Guard/Top is a shoulder-pin/omoplata-control position where the top player's posture is destroyed by design, so the attempt distribution is head-heavy on posture work (~40% across the generic Posture Recovery and the position-specific Posture from Williams Guard) with passing downstream. Gi vs no-gi differences are small (±1-2) and mechanistically grounded, not structural: in the gi, collar/lapel grips and mat friction let the top player break the shoulder chain and re-posture more cleanly (slight gi edge on Posture Recovery and Pressure Pass), while in no-gi the sweat-slick shoulder chain is harder for the bottom player to hold, so the top player postures out and stacks a hair more freely (slight no-gi edge on Posture from Williams Guard and Stack Pass). No move here is ruleset-unavailable — all seven postures, stacks, and passes are legal and mechanically live in both frames — so there are no zeros and no availability rulings.

removal_candidates.reason: Mechanically near-fantasy while the shoulder is pinned and the legs stay high — the panel unanimously calls it the tail. It exists only after the position opens, so it survives as a low-frequency (~8) move rather than a removal, but it is the weakest justified entry from this role.

flags: SANITY-DIFF gross miss: sealed site values gave Knee Slice Pass 29 (panel ~8, a fantasy move against a locked Williams guard) and near-zeroed the three position-specific signature moves (Posture from Williams 6, Stack from Williams 2, Guard Pass from Williams 1) — the old data misread this as a generic guard-passing position and ignored the shoulder pin. Panel did not conform.

Two posture entries (Posture Recovery -> combat-base, Posture from Williams Guard -> closed-guard) and two stack entries (Stack Pass -> side-control, Stack from Williams Guard -> half-guard) are distinct by endpoint/intent but structurally near-duplicate in name; watch for user confusion and potential future consolidation.

verify.rationale: Williams Guard/Top is a shoulder-pin position where the top player's posture is destroyed by design, so the honest attempt tree is re-posture first, stack second, clean-pass third. Adversarial review on all five vectors passed. (1) why_selected 'top-40 L1 shift': the old sealed prior (Posture Recovery 35, Knee Slice 29, and the three signature moves near-zeroed at 6/2/1) misread this as a generic guard-passing position and ignored the pin; a knee-slice against a trapped near-arm is a fantasy, so the panel's inversion is a JUSTIFIED correction of broken data, not an over-correction. (2) No zeros, correctly argued: all seven postures/stacks/passes are legal and mechanically live in both gi and no-gi; no availability ruling needed. (3) Every gi/no-gi divergence is <=1 point with a stated mechanism (gi collar/friction aids re-posture and pressure; no-gi slick shoulder chain aids posturing-out and stacking), so no structural or unmechanistic divergence. (4) Rank order is coach-recognizable: position-specific Posture (21/22) and generic Posture Recovery (20/19) lead, signature Stack from Williams (15/16) is third, position-specific Guard Pass (13) outranks the two generic passes, Knee Slice is correctly dead last (9/8). (5) Head-mass is healthy: top-5 share 80/82, max move only 21-22%, no pathological dominance. Rounding is honest -- proposed integers are the standard-rounded panel means and both frames sum to exactly 100 with no thumb on the scale. No move is mislocated beyond rounding noise; no re-elicitation warranted.

containers.frame_rationale: Worm Guard is an intrinsically gi position: the worm sweep, the wormbolo back-take, the lapel elevator, the collar drag and the squid transfer are all loaded with the opponent's lapel and cannot occur without cloth. In gi the distribution is sharply head-heavy on the Worm Guard Sweep (~25-30, the reason the guard exists) with the Bolo, Squid transfer and Lapel Elevator forming a real second tier — the omoplata/triangle/X-guard/DLR moves are conditional branches you hit when the primary sweep is defended. In no-gi the four lapel-dependent moves are hard availability zeros; the node survives only as the nearest supine/leg-entanglement scramble, so the six gi-agnostic mechanics inherit a counterfactual distribution led by the X-Guard Sweep (~24-30) with the Omoplata, Triangle, and De La Riva sweeps behind it. The 9-vs-1 split is genuine: Craig alone holds that no-gi worm guard is a non-position and therefore refuses to crown X-guard, flattening the surviving six instead; the other nine treat the state as playable and let X-guard dominate.

availability_rulings.reason: Lapel-dependent sweep — the elevator lever is loaded with the opponent's lapel, which does not exist in no-gi. Ruleset-unavailable, not merely rare.
Collar/lapel-fed drag specific to the worm guard cloth configuration; no collar to grip in no-gi. True zero.
The signature sweep is definitionally the lapel wrap around the opponent's leg — impossible without a gi. True zero.
Lapel-to-lapel transfer (worm wrap re-fed into the squid/ashi-lapel configuration); both endpoints require cloth. True zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the lowest gi mover (4-6) and a niche branch even no-gi; the panel keeps it live but flags it as the weakest, most redundant entry from this position — borderline garnish per Gordon.

flags: SANITY-DIFF gross miss: the sealed current-site values invert the position — Worm Guard Sweep at 1 (the signature, central move) and Omoplata Sweep at 33 (a conditional branch). The panel corrects this decisively: Worm Guard Sweep ~26 gi, Omoplata Sweep ~8 gi.
Old site values carried NO gi/no-gi split and ran all four lapel-dependent moves at full weight in no-gi, which is structurally impossible for a lapel guard.

Genuine 9-vs-1 no-gi philosophy split logged (not difference-split): Craig treats no-gi worm guard as a null position and flattens the surviving moves (~15-18 X-guard) while the other nine treat it as a playable counterfactual scramble (~24-30 X-guard).

No-gi distribution rests on only 6 live moves; it is intentionally head-heavy on X-Guard rather than smeared, per the Statistician's anti-uniform demand and the Game Designer's playability requirement.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci, Roger Gracie, Rafael Mendes + Statistician) failed to break the proposed distribution. Both frames sum to 100. GI: head is Worm Guard Sweep (28) — the signature move the guard is built on — with a real second tier (Bolo 12, Lapel Elevator 11, Squid 11) and conditional-branch tail; top-5 share 70 is right for a one-signature specialist guard, not over-concentrated. All four no-gi zeros (Worm Guard Sweep, Lapel Elevator, Collar Drag, Worm to Squid) survive the bulletproof-availability bar: each is definitionally lapel-loaded and ruleset-unavailable without cloth, not merely rare. The full Σ|Δ|=126 divergence is mechanistically accounted for (4 moves vanish, 6 survivors absorb the freed mass led by X-Guard 29 as the nearest supine leg-entanglement recovery). The panel already corrected the gross sealed-site inversion (Worm Guard Sweep 1→28, Omoplata Sweep 33→8). Coach-recognition test passes in both frames. The 9-vs-1 no-gi philosophy split is properly weighted (X-guard crowned at 29, top of majority range, not dragged to a compromise by Craig's lone null-position view). The only objection raised — Roger's gi Bolo (12) vs Lapel Elevator (11) ordering — was withdrawn on a sub-1-point panel-mean margin (12.02 vs 11.49), within noise and not correction-worthy. Correcting a colleague panel, not redoing it: all ten moves accepted.

containers.frame_rationale: Worm guard is a purely gi position: the bottom player feeds his own lapel around the top player's leg, converting the top player's gi into a leash that tethers the passing arm and base leg. In the GI frame this inverts normal passing frequencies, the two lapel de-activation moves dominate first attempts (Lapel Strip ~27 as the clear #1, Backstep ~18 as co-primary, together ~45% of exchanges) while all circling/linear passes (Toreando ~6, Leg Drag ~7, Long Step ~8, Knee Slice ~11) are suppressed because you cannot circle away from your own anchored lapel; only the forward-crushing Smash ~13 and Stack ~9 stay mid because they work while the lapel is still semi-live. In NO-GI the guard cannot physically exist, so the node is modeled as its closest legal analog (a de-lapeled open/half-butterfly shape): the Lapel Strip is a hard zero (availability ruling), and the ~27 points it held redistribute into generic head-heavy passing led by Knee Slice ~20 and Toreando ~20, then Leg Drag ~16, with Backstep collapsing to ~12 because there is no leash to step away from. Net: two genuinely different opponent personalities, gi = lapel-obsessed, no-gi = generic head-heavy passer.

availability_rulings.reason: Lapel-dependent action. No-gi has no lapel, so the move is genuinely unavailable, not merely rare. Unanimous panel 0.

removal_candidates.reason: In the gi frame this is near-fantasy from a locked worm guard (attempted ~6%): the wrapped lapel tethers the passing arm/base leg so you cannot circle. It survives only because the no-gi analog frees it. Flag for possible removal from the gi first-attempt set, not the no-gi set.

Same gi mechanism as toreando: you cannot leg-drag through your own tethered lapel, so gi attempts sit ~7%. Central only in the no-gi de-lapeled analog. Candidate for gi-frame pruning if the node is ever split by ruleset.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: the sealed old site values were exactly backwards for a lapel guard, Leg Drag ranked #1 (24) and Lapel Strip near-zero (3) with Backstep tiny (6). That is a classic uniform-passing prior that ignores the lapel mechanic. The calibrated panel independently inverted this (Strip/Backstep dominant in gi); we do NOT conform toward the old numbers.
Old site values were identical for gi and nogi (never modeled the ruleset split); this deliberation forks them, with the largest divergence on the lapel-tethered passes.
No-gi column is a modeled analog, not a real observed meta, since worm guard cannot exist without cloth. Treat no-gi numbers as 'closest legal no-gi shape' behavior.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move here is mechanically and legally available in both gi and no-gi, so the split is magnitude-only — no per-frame zeros. In the GI, grips let the bottom player control and off-balance the top man, so the pure X-Guard Sweep and the come-up moves (Technical Stand Up to Single Leg, X-Guard Technical Stand Up) dominate attempts, and grip-dependent bailouts like Deep Half and Tomahawk sit slightly higher. In NO-GI the leg-entanglement chain is the payoff and fully legal for heel-hook finishing, so a real slice of sweep demand bleeds into X-Guard to Ashi Garami (roughly doubles vs gi), the X-to-SLX transfer, and the straight ankle — X becomes an escalator to SLX/ashi rather than purely a sweeping home. The one persistent camp split: the leg-lock quartet (Danaher, Gordon, Craig, Kade) ranks the SLX transfer and ashi higher in no-gi, while the sweep-first camp (Marcelo, Roger, Mikey, Mendes) keeps the sweep and technical standup dominant; both views are preserved in the individual ballots rather than difference-split.

removal_candidates.reason: Lands at x-guard/bottom — it is an ENTRY INTO x-guard, mis-filed as an attempt FROM x-guard bottom (self-loop / re-entry). Genuinely rare as an action taken while already in X-guard; the panel scored it 3-6 only to represent post-scramble re-establishment. Structurally belongs on the entering position's transition list, not here.

The only submission on the list and, per the panel (even Craig), you rarely finish a straight ankle from PURE X — you transition to SLX/ashi and finish there. As a standalone in-position attempt it is low-frequency; the SLX/ashi transfer moves already carry the leg-attack demand. Kept (not removed) but a candidate for consolidation into the transfer chain.

flags: DUPLICATE_TARGET: 'Single Leg X Entry' and 'X-Guard to Single Leg X' both land at single-leg-x-guard/bottom — the panel deliberately kept the general Entry larger than the X-specific transfer to avoid double-counting SLX demand; consider merging.
SELF_LOOP: 'Butterfly Guard to X-Guard' lands at x-guard/bottom (the position itself) — re-entry mis-filed as an in-position attempt; see removal_candidates.

SEALED_DIFF: old site value put X-Guard Sweep at 35 (over-weighted single-move head) and Technical Stand Up to Single Leg / X-Guard Technical Stand Up / X-Guard to Single Leg X at 7/2/2 (badly under-weighted the come-up + SLX-transfer spine); panel corrected the sweep down to ~23/19 and the standup/transfer family up.
SUBMISSION_IN_ATTEMPT_LIST: 'Ankle Lock from X-Guard' is the sole submission among sweeps/entries; low standalone frequency from pure X.

containers.frame_rationale: X-Guard/Top is a base-and-extraction role, not a passing position: the top player has been elevated/broken and his real behavior is killing the hooks (knee pin), standing to strip, and backstepping out — those three carry ~45-50% of gi attempts, with named passes strictly downstream of hook removal. The gi/no-gi split is driven almost entirely by the counter-leg-entry lane. In no-gi the backstep flows straight into a saddle or outside-ashi entry because the heel hook is the payoff and the pace rewards immediate leg trades — so Saddle Entry (gi ~2 / nogi ~10) and Outside Ashi (gi ~3 / nogi ~8-9) swing 6-8 points each, pulling ~10-12 points of mass out of the gi base moves (standing escape, knee pin) and into the legs no-gi. Conversely gi players stand and strip more (standing escape and step-over slightly higher gi) because grips and the illegal heel hook make committing to the entanglement a bad trade. No move is truly ruleset-unavailable here (no lapel/collar-only techniques), so the leg entries are gi-SUPPRESSED to a 1-3 floor rather than zeroed.

availability_rulings.reason: NOT unavailable — a straight ankle lock from the saddle/inside-sankaku is legal in most gi rulesets, so the entry exists. But it is heavily suppressed (scored 1-3) because the payoff heel hook is illegal in nearly all gi competition and gi grips/friction make the backstep-to-saddle scramble far slower. Gi-suppressed, not zeroed.

NOT unavailable — outside ashi garami and its straight ankle lock are legal in the gi. Suppressed to 2-4 because the outside-heel-hook finish is banned in gi competition and the reaping position invites reaping penalties, so top players rarely commit to it from live X-guard in the gi. Gi-suppressed, not zeroed.

removal_candidates.reason: Panel consensus rates it a genuine rare from live X-guard: stacking requires the hooks already cleared and the opponent's hips already stacked, which is a downstream state, not an attempt made from inside the X. Lands consistently at 3-6 across both frames. Log only — not removed.

A finishing pass that presumes the leg entanglement is already neutralized and you are threading the far leg; from live X-guard-top it is almost never the initiating attempt. Consistently 3-6, several R1 'rare' tiers (Craig, Gordon, Danaher no-gi). Log only — not removed.

flags: SANITY-DIFF: sealed site values were a role misread — they modeled X-Guard/Top as a passing position (Smash Pass 18, Knee Slice 16 as top moves; Back Step 5, Knee Pin 7). The panel unanimously inverts this: base/extraction moves (Knee Pin, Standing Escape, Back Step) are the head, and Smash Pass falls to ~6-8. Panel did NOT conform to the sealed values.

Mechanical overlap between Standing Escape (resets to standing/top, neutral) and Back Step (advances to side-control) and Knee Pin (advances to half-guard): experts fold these three differently, which drives most of the remaining dissent (Gordon/Craig favor backstep, Roger/Bravo/Mikey favor standing escape). All three are genuinely distinct by landing position, so all kept separate.

success_rate_by_ruleset in the pack shows Outside Ashi and Stack Pass with HIGHER no-gi success than gi, consistent with the frame story (leg entries pay off no-gi), reinforcing the occurrence divergence direction.

Head concentration is deliberately moderate (three-move head ~46% gi) so the in-browser opponent plays like a scrambly defender rather than spamming a single pass; the passing tail is kept honest and ranked below the base game per UX.

containers.frame_rationale: Every move in this pack is legal and available in BOTH gi and no-gi — there are no lapel/collar or gi-illegal techniques here — so the gi/no-gi split is purely a matter of weighting driven by one lever: heel-hook legality. In the gi, reverse X is a sweep engine: you off-balance, come up, take two points, and pass, so the sweep is more dominant (26-29 gi vs 20-24 no-gi), the recycle to standard X-guard is higher (players re-attack the sweep for points), and the leg entries are minor tails (ashi 6-9 gi, capped because the IBJJF heel-hook ban removes the payoff). In no-gi the position becomes a leg-lock transit hub: the same off-balancing motion funnels into single-leg-X (primary first entry, ~15-18) and ashi/saddle (~15-20, where the heel hook lives), which together eat the no-gi tail and pull mass off the sweep and the standard-X recycle. The single largest divergence in the whole position is the ashi entry (gi ~7, no-gi ~17), and it has a clean mechanism (heel-hook legality); the SLX entry and the sweep-vs-recycle balance are the milder echoes of the same lever.

availability_rulings.reason: Fully available in the gi (SLX is a sweeping/entry position, not lock-dependent); weighted lower than no-gi only because gi players convert SLX to a sweep-for-points rather than a leg-entanglement, not for any legality reason. No zero.

removal_candidates.reason: Lowest-consensus move and a bailout rather than a plan from a committed reverse X — universally tail-tier (gi high-single-digits, no-gi mid-low single digits). It genuinely happens (stand-up is always available), so keep it, but it is the first candidate to prune if the move list is ever trimmed.

flags: Old SEALED site values were flat (gi == nogi) and completely missed the heel-hook-driven leg divergence that defines this position in no-gi; they also underweighted the signature Reverse X-Guard Sweep (site 15 vs panel 20-29) and overweighted Technical Stand-up (site 13 vs panel high-single-digits) — the calibrated ballots correct all three.

All seven success_rate_by_ruleset values in the pack are near-identical placeholders (58.0 / 40.6, gi == nogi) that do not reflect the real gi/no-gi divergence; this occurrence pass only sets attempt frequency, but the success-rate coherence is worth a separate calibration look for the leg-entry moves especially.

Largest residual dissent is no-gi Ashi Garami Entry: Kade/Marcelo/Gordon lean ~18-20 (leg-hub view) vs Craig ~15 (SLX-first, anti-double-count) — a ~5-point band, mechanism-grounded on both sides, not fake consensus.

containers.frame_rationale: All nine moves are escapes/passes with no lapel, collar, or heel-hook dependency, so every move is legal in both gi and no-gi — there are no availability zeros. The divergence is entirely meta-driven, not legality-driven. In no-gi the bottom man's reverse X is one rotation from an inside heel hook, so the top player must extract the trapped leg immediately; this pushes the fast-extraction answers — Backstep Pass from Reverse X-Guard, Back Step, and Standing Escape — up a few points in no-gi (Gordon, Craig, Mikey, Danaher, Marcelo all bump these). In the gi the leg-lock urgency is gone and pant/sleeve grips let the top player indulge slower classical passing, so the distribution runs a touch flatter across Smash, Knee Slice, and especially Leg Drag — Mendes defends a genuine gi bump on Leg Drag because pant grips let him kill the knee line and drag out, an option that is cleaner in the gi than no-gi. Net: no-gi is spikier toward backstep/stand, gi is slightly flatter across the pass menu.

removal_candidates.reason: Unanimous near-floor across all 10 legends (gi 2-4, nogi 2-4). You cannot butterfly-pass an inverted leg entanglement — there is no butterfly hook to nullify and the geometry is wrong. Kept at floor 2-3 (rare, not impossible) rather than removed now; strongest removal candidate on the list.
Consistently low situational secondary pass (gi 6-8). A distant tail option once extraction is underway; not a first-choice response to reverse X. Logged as a soft removal candidate, not removed.

flags: DUPLICATE-ENTRY: 'Back Step' and 'Backstep Pass from Reverse X-Guard' are the same mechanical answer named twice. The panel treated their COMBINED mass (~30-36 gi / ~32-38 nogi) as the honest workhorse and split it between the two entries; individual splits vary by legend purely as a labeling choice (Kade/Bravo/Mikey load the generic 'Back Step'; Gordon/Lachlan load the named RX entry). Recommend merging these two entries in a future content pass.

SEALED-VALUE GROSS MISS (Smash Pass): old site value 30 vs panel ~10-11 — the old data treated a reverse-X escape like a generic guard pass and massively over-weighted the smash. Panel does not conform; ~10 is correct.
SEALED-VALUE GROSS MISS (Butterfly Pass): old site value 14 vs panel ~3 — butterfly-passing an inverted entanglement barely exists; the old 14 is a clear error.

SEALED-VALUE INVERSION: old site under-weighted the actual structural answers (Backstep Pass from RX = 5, Standing Escape = 1, Knee Slice from RX = 2) while over-weighting Smash/Butterfly. The old distribution had reverse-X passing essentially backwards; the panel's head-heavy backstep/stand distribution corrects it and is confirmed, not redirected, by the sanity diff.

STRUCTURAL: this is a passer's-perspective role (Reverse X-Guard/Top) where frequency and success unusually correlate — the backstep is both the most-attempted and the mechanically-correct answer, so the head of the distribution is intentionally heavy and should not be smeared toward uniform.

verify.rationale: Adversarial panel (Musumeci/Giles/Danaher + Statistician) could not break any individual move value. Both frames sum to exactly 100. why_selected's L1-shift concern is legitimate but resolves in the panel's favor: the old site had reverse-X passing backwards (Smash 30, Butterfly 14, backstep/stand at 5/1/2), and the panel corrected it with mechanism, not vibes. This is a passer's-perspective leg-entanglement role, so (a) the heavy head (top-5 ~71-72%) is correct for a narrow extract-or-pass decision tree, not a smear error; (b) frequency-vs-success is not conflated here even though they correlate, because the top player reflexively ATTEMPTS the backstep/stand extraction constantly under heel-hook threat, which is an attempt-frequency claim independent of success (Giles). No zeros exist and frame_rationale correctly rules that all nine moves are gi/no-gi legal, so no bulletproof-zero attack is needed (Statistician). gi/no-gi divergences are all 0-2 points and directionally coherent (no-gi spikier toward backstep/stand under leg-lock urgency, gi flatter across the classical pass menu). Every proposed_final equals its rounded panel mean, within dispersion. Two documentation defects were found but neither warrants a numeric adjustment: (1) frame_rationale oversells a gi Leg Drag bump that the numbers do not deliver (proposed 9/9 flat) - Musumeci conceded the flat value is within dispersion and forcing a sub-noise split would be overriding the panel; (2) 'Knee Slice Pass' (generic) and 'Knee Slice from Reverse X-Guard' (RX-specific) are a near-duplicate the panel did not flag alongside the backstep duplicate, but they are defensibly distinct (leg-freed vs leg-still-entangled) and their combined ~20-22% is a reasonable #2 conceptual answer. Rank order (backstep > stand > knee-slice > smash/leg-drag > long-step > butterfly) is exactly what a reverse-X passer would recognize. All nine moves accepted; corrections are documentation-only, so the container verdict is accept.

containers.frame_rationale: Single Leg X-Guard bottom is a sweep-and-wrestle-up position in BOTH rulesets — the Single Leg X Sweep is the runaway workhorse (~24 gi / ~20 nogi) and the technical stand-up to a single is a genuine second lane everywhere; that shared head is mechanism-driven (the position off-balances the top player the instant it is secured, so coming up on top is its reason for existing). The frames diverge almost entirely on the LEG-LOCK pipeline: in no-gi the three ashi lanes — Inside Ashi Entry (~11), SLX to Ashi Garami (~11), and Single Leg X-Guard to Inside Sankaku (~8) — collectively absorb roughly a third of the traffic, because heel hooks and reaping are legal and the position is the sport's premier lower-body doorway. In the gi those same lanes shrink to floor because reaping and heel hooks are illegal under IBJJF: sankaku drops to 1-2, inside-ashi to ~5, and SLX-to-ashi survives only as the legal outside-ashi straight ankle lock (~7). That freed gi traffic flows back into grip-dependent, come-up-on-top options — SLX to X-Guard re-pummel (~12 gi vs ~8 nogi) and the Heel Grab / Ankle Pick sweeps run slightly hotter in the gi. Net: same purpose (get up, get on top) both frames, but no-gi forks a third of attempts into the legs while the gi keeps that share in sweeping and X-guard chaining.

availability_rulings.move: Single Leg X-Guard to Inside Sankaku
availability_rulings.reason: Inside sankaku (saddle / 411) is a reaping position and the heel hook it exists to deliver is illegal under IBJJF and most mainstream gi rulesets. Scored at floor (1-2), NOT zero, because some gi events (ADCC-gi, sub-only gi, gym training) permit the entry to a straight footlock and the position itself is not universally banned. Rare, not unavailable.

Deep inside-ashi edges into reaping territory and its primary finish (inside heel hook) is illegal in mainstream gi competition, so gi players rarely chase it. Scored ~4-6 (situational), NOT zero, because shallow/legal inside-ashi to a straight ankle lock exists in the gi. Rare due to ruleset, not unavailable.

Available in the gi as an OUTSIDE-ashi / straight-ankle-lock entry (legal under IBJJF). Not a zero; scored ~5-8. Divergence from no-gi is that the no-gi version chains into reaping/heel-hook finishes that are gi-illegal, so no-gi frequency runs higher. Logged as a mechanism divergence, not an availability restriction.

removal_candidates.reason: This is an ENTRY into an X-guard family position from butterfly, not a move initiated from within Single Leg X-Guard/Bottom. From SLX-bottom you are already past butterfly; re-setting to it to re-enter is a near-nonexistent decision. Consistently floor-tiered (2-3) by all ten legends in both frames. Likely a mis-homed edge (wrong-role / entry-vs-exit confusion).

removal_candidates.move: De La Riva to X-Guard Transition
removal_candidates.reason: Same issue as Butterfly-to-X: this is a DLR-to-X ENTRY, not an option from within SLX-bottom. Floor-tiered (1-3) by all legends, effectively zero no-gi. Structurally reads as an inbound entry edge mis-attached to this position's outbound transition list.

removal_candidates.move: Single Leg X to Estima Lock
removal_candidates.reason: Estima lock is a very specific standing/passing foot-lock scenario; from SLX-bottom it is an oddity, not a live line. Uniformly rare (2-4) in both frames. Kept for honesty but a candidate for pruning if the move list needs trimming.

flags: SEALED site values were a near-uniform ~9 smear across most non-headline moves (Sankaku 9/9, Estima 9/9, Inside Ashi 8/8, SLX-to-Ashi 9/9) — classic uncalibrated flat distribution; the panel rejected it in favor of a head-heavy, frame-forked shape.

Single Leg X Entry was drastically UNDERweighted on the live site (gi 3 / nogi 3) vs the panel's ~11/10. The panel judges re-securing/deepening SLX (control consolidation) to be a genuinely common decision; this is an upward correction, not conformity to the seed.

Site values had ZERO gi/nogi divergence on every move (all frames identical), which is structurally implausible for a leg-entry-heavy position governed by reaping rules — strong evidence the old numbers predate ruleset-aware calibration.

Three moves (Butterfly Guard to X-Guard, De La Riva to X-Guard Transition, and partially Single Leg X to Estima Lock) read as ENTRY edges into SLX-adjacent positions rather than moves initiated FROM SLX-bottom — possible mis-homed/wrong-direction edges worth a graph-coherence check.
No hard availability-0 was issued anywhere: all reap-restricted moves (sankaku, inside-ashi, SLX-to-ashi in gi) were held at floor with reasons, per the 'rare is 1-3, never 0' rule.

containers.frame_rationale: Single Leg X-Guard/Top is fundamentally an extraction position, not a passing position: your near leg is elevated and linked, so the first-order response in every ruleset is to free the trapped foot — either by standing tall and stripping (Standing Escape) or by spinning out (Backstep) — with actual passes strictly second-order and lower-frequency. The gi/no-gi split runs on two mechanisms. No-gi pushes both extractions UP and the Kneebar counter UP: the trapped leg is the direct entry to the heel hook, so clearing it is a fire drill and disengaging fast dominates, while the fully-legal leg-lock meta makes the spinning kneebar counter a live situational option. Gi pushes the actual passes slightly UP and the Kneebar DOWN: with only the straight ankle legal there is no heel-hook panic, so the top man can pass patiently, and pant/sleeve grips make basing to strip cleaner and the Leg Weave specifically more available (a grip to weave with), while the kneebar drops to a legal-but-rare floor. The result is two distinct opponent personalities per ruleset over the same head-heavy shape.

availability_rulings.reason: NOT zeroed. The straight-ankle/kneebar counter is IBJJF-legal for adult brown and black belts, so it is a genuine low-positive (~4), not unavailable. It is merely rare in the gi below black belt because the heel-hook-adjacent entanglements that feed it are absent and gi grips favor patient passing. Logged to document that the low gi number is prevalence-driven, not a legality zero.

Fully legal no-gi and a live spinning/rolling counter when the bottom man over-commits the entanglement. Sits at situational (6-10), not zero. Logged to anchor the clean no-gi > gi divergence to leg-lock-meta prevalence rather than any rule difference.

removal_candidates.reason: Panel-wide agreement it is a spice/novelty counter from this role (unanimous gi=4, no-gi 6-10). It survives comfortably above the never-happens threshold in no-gi and stays a legal low-positive in gi, so it is NOT recommended for removal — logged only as the lowest-frequency, most-marginal edge that a future prune would examine first.

flags: SEALED site values are a gross miss and a role misread: they ranked the four passes as the plurality (HQ 19 / Knee Slice 18 / Leg Weave 16 / Smash 14, combined 67) and buried the two extractions (Backstep 11, Standing Escape 8, combined 19), treating top-of-SLX as a settled passing position rather than an extraction problem. The panel unanimously inverts this. Not conformed to.

SEALED values also had zero gi/nogi divergence (identical in both frames), which is unrealistic for a leg-entanglement position where the heel-hook threat asymmetry is the defining ruleset difference.
SEALED Kneebar 14 was grossly inflated for a spice/counter move; panel lands it at gi ~4 / nogi ~7.

Genuine surviving dissent on Standing-Escape-vs-Backstep ordering: Gordon (elite-efficiency) runs Backstep above Standing Escape; Kade/Mikey/Danaher/Lachlan (population-availability) run Standing Escape clearly higher. Preserved intentionally, not difference-split.

This is a correctly distributed (non-spiky) position — no single move exceeds ~34; head weight sits in the two extractions combined (~50-58), which reads as a real scrambly leg exchange rather than a one-move spam.

containers.frame_rationale: No move here is ruleset-illegal, so there are no per-frame zeros and no availability rulings — every listed action exists in both gi and no-gi. Divergences are behavioral, not legal. Deep Half Entry is higher in the gi (9-11) than no-gi (6-8) because entering deep half without lapels invites the front headlock and a fast pass in no-gi, so the population avoids it there. Lockdown Recovery and Electric Chair Transition run higher in no-gi (5-8) than gi (2-4) because they are 10th Planet lines from a predominantly no-gi subculture that needs no collar grips and is actively de-emphasized in gi competition. Underhook Sweep from Half and Back Take from Bottom tick up slightly in no-gi (no collar to stall the underhook, faster front-headlock/back-shuck scrambles). The signature z-sweep family (Z-Guard Sweep, Z-Guard to Half Guard, Sweep from Z-Guard) and the underhook series carry the mass in both frames, with the gi marginally favoring grip-assisted sweeps.

removal_candidates.reason: Consistently the lowest non-10th-Planet attempt (5-7 both frames); a legitimate but genuinely rare entry from z-guard bottom — the knee-shield player reaches X-guard occasionally when the leg is exposed, but it is a side-door, not a primary action. Logged, not removed.

Floor-tier in gi (2-4) and single-digit in no-gi; a 10th Planet-specific line that is a rounding error outside those rooms. Panel keeps it above zero (rarely, not never) but flags it as a candidate if the move list is ever trimmed.

flags: LEGACY_MISWEIGHT: SEALED current-site values invert reality — Old School Sweep at 35 (a half-guard staple, minor here) and the three signature z-sweeps floored at 1-3 (Z-Guard to Half Guard=1, Sweep from Z-Guard=1, Z-Guard Sweep=3). Panel did not conform; the z-sweep family + underhook correctly carry the top of the distribution.

NAMING_OVERLAP: 'Z-Guard Sweep' and 'Sweep from Z-Guard' both land in the side-control/mount family and are hard to distinguish as discrete attempts; panel kept them co-weighted rather than letting either balloon, but they may represent one real-world action split across two nodes.
TENTH_PLANET_SUBCULTURE: Lockdown Recovery + Electric Chair Transition carry a large gi/no-gi behavioral split driven by a specific school; population estimates depend heavily on room demographics.

verify.rationale: The SEALED site prior was an inverted half-guard-node bleed (Old School Sweep=35, the three signature z-sweeps floored at 1-3); the panel correctly refused to conform and rebuilt a sweep-dominated distribution that a Z-Guard-bottom coach would recognize. Head mass (top-5 = 71 gi / 69 nogi) is appropriate for a sweep/recovery position that genuinely funnels into ~4-5 core actions, not a red flag. Sums are exactly 100/100. All gi/no-gi divergences are <=3 points and each carries a stated mechanism: Deep Half Entry gi 10 > nogi 7 (no lapels invites the front headlock entering deep half in no-gi), Lockdown Recovery and Electric Chair higher in no-gi (10th Planet subculture, collar-free), Underhook Sweep + Back Take tick up in no-gi (no collar to stall the underhook). The signature z-sweep family plus the underhook recovery correctly carry the top of both frames, with the gi marginally favoring grip-assisted sweeps and the no-gi tying Underhook Sweep with Z-Guard Sweep at the top (the collar-free underhook recovery is THE no-gi z-guard action). Adversarial pressure surfaced two soft concerns: (a) Back Take from Bottom at 9/10 reads ~1-2 points rich versus x-guard/deep-half transitions off the same underhook, and (b) Electric Chair no-gi 6 may be a touch high at the population level since most no-gi z-guard players are Craig-Jones-lineage rather than 10th Planet. Both are sub-dispersion (panel dispersions 0.5-1.6, every proposed_final within 0.5 of its panel_mean) and do not justify overriding a colleague panel. NAMING_OVERLAP (Z-Guard Sweep vs Sweep from Z-Guard as one real action split across two nodes) is a graph-structure duplication the panel handled correctly by co-weighting rather than ballooning one node; it is not a weighting error. No move falls outside the panel's own credible interval, so no correction is warranted.

containers.frame_rationale: Z-Guard top is a knee-shield problem solved two ways: cut through the shield (the three knee-slice entries — Knee Slice Pass, Knee Slice from Z-Guard, Knee Slice from Half — which together form ~38-42% of attempts, the plurality) or circumvent it (Back Step, Long Step, Smash). The one genuine ruleset divergence is Back Step, which rises materially gi→nogi (roughly 12-13 gi to 16-17 nogi) for two mechanical reasons: no-gi removes the collar/pant grips the bottom player uses to arrest the passer's turn, and the backstep doubles as a leg-entanglement entry that is legal and central in modern no-gi. Correspondingly the knee-slice cuts sit a point or two higher in the gi, where cross-collar and knee-pin grips make the deliberate cut the first instinct. Every move on this list is a passing mechanic available in both rulesets — none is grip- or leglock-gated — so there are no per-frame zeros; all divergences are behavioral, not availability-driven.

removal_candidates.reason: Duplicate-sounding generic label — near-synonymous with 'Pass Z-Guard' and functionally a catch-all 'complete the pass' entry rather than a distinct technique. It DOES happen (kept ~8-9), but the two generic-pass labels should be consolidated into one.

The mirror duplicate of 'Z-Guard Pass' — same low-information generic-pass catch-all. Kept modest (~10) rather than zeroed because generic passing completions do occur, but one of the two labels is redundant.

flags: Label fragmentation: three near-synonymous knee-slice entries (Knee Slice Pass / Knee Slice from Z-Guard / Knee Slice from Half) split one mechanical family; individual splits are somewhat arbitrary though the family total (~40%) is robust.
Duplicate generic-pass labels: 'Pass Z-Guard' and 'Z-Guard Pass' read as the same catch-all completion and should be consolidated (see removal_candidates).

Sanity-diff vs SEALED site values: old site collapsed the entire knee-slice family into a single 'Knee Slice Pass' at 40 and buried 'Knee Slice from Z-Guard' (4), 'Pass Z-Guard' (2), 'Z-Guard Pass' (1); it also underweighted Back Step at 9. Panel redistributes the knee-slice mass honestly across the three labels and lifts Back Step (esp. no-gi) — a confirmed prior underweight of a genuinely central move — without conforming to the old numbers.
